title: Manager-Project Controls - Sr.
description:

title: Body and Paint Repair Combo Technician
description:
Rally Fleet is seeking a dynamic individual to join our team as an Automotive Body Repair/Paint Technician. This position plays a pivotal role in providing high-quality body repair and painting services for our fleet vehicles. We are looking for a forward-thinking professional who shares our commitment to excellence and aligns with our values.

Our ideal candidate is an experienced technician with a minimum of 3 years' experience in automotive body repair and painting. They should have expertise in working with various surfaces, including fiberglass and metal, and be able to perform light to heavy repairs efficiently. The ability to work in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment is essential.


What You’ll Do

  • Perform light to heavy automotive body repairs on different types of surfaces.
  • Repair fiberglass fenders and hoods using a two-part epoxy.
  • Pull metal and fill with fiberglass as needed.
  • Disassemble and reassemble semi-truck body parts.
  • Prep panels for primer and paint.
  • Perform auto body repairs to OEM standards.
  • Prime and tape trucks for paint application.
  • Paint semi-trucks using a single-stage or base/clear coat application.
  • Dispose of waste properly per OSHA/EH&S standards.

What You Need

  • Previous experience as a Body Shop Repair person and automotive Painter or Paint Prepper.
  • Experience working with metals, including aluminum.
  • Ability to straighten sheet metal.
  • Previous welding experience.
  • Frame machine and welding experience.
  • Ability to lift heavy objects (20 – 75 lbs).
  • Reliable transportation.
  • What We Offer
  • Competitive Weekly Pay
  • Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance for Full-Time Employees
  • 401k Plan with Matching Investment
  • Vacation and Paid Holidays

Who We Are

Rally Fleet is a dynamic and innovative company specializing in unique fleet management services. We are experts in driving out the inefficiencies in the body repair process, end to end, delivering high quality service while driving down cycle time. We utilize our proprietary Rally Lean System to keep our fleet partners on the road. We specialize in quality, fast paced, automotive body repairs on Fleet Vehicles.

Who is RallyX?

RallyX is a management company which owns and operates a suite of businesses in diverse sectors including health care, residential and commercial construction, and fleet repair services. Grounded in our faith-driven approach, we focus on delivering quality work, building a solid team, and actively contributing to the community.


RallyX is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and applicants, without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or expression. This commitment extends to all aspects of employment, including hiring, promotion, termination, and other conditions of employment.

title: ERP Integration Expert (all genders)
description:
About GeneralMind

GeneralMind builds AI Systems of Action for complex enterprise workflows. We deploy AI employees that automate messy operational handovers across supply chains - processing orders, validating invoices, coordinating suppliers, and handling exceptions directly on top of enterprise systems like SAP, Oracle, JDE, and Dynamics.

Our platform combines AI agents, operational context graphs, and real transaction data to achieve Autopilot-grade automation in real operational environments.

We work closely with leading global companies across manufacturing, retail, and logistics to deploy AI into mission-critical workflows.

About the role

Every GeneralMind deployment stands or falls with one thing: how well our AI agents talk to the customer's ERP. As our ERP Integration Expert, you own exactly that. You design and build the technical bridges between our platform and our customers' ERP landscapes, from digital cores like S/4HANA and ECC to integration platforms like BTP and Integration Suite, and make sure order confirmations, invoices, and master data flow reliably in both directions.

You'll work at the sharpest edge of the company: real enterprise systems, real transaction data, real go-lives. And you'll help turn every integration you build into reusable patterns, so each deployment gets faster than the last.

What You'll Do

  • Own the integration architecture for new customers end to end: assess their ERP landscape, choose the right interface pattern (OData, RFC/BAPI, IDoc/EDI, CPI/BTP, staging tables, file-based), and design something their IT will approve and operate.
  • Lead technical discovery with customer IT, basis, and process teams, and surface the blocking constraint in week one, not week nine.
  • Own the data and field mapping from the customer's order, item, partner, and pricing structures onto our internal model, including the custom fields that carry the real business logic.
  • Design and build our ERP connectors in Python (S/4HANA and ECC, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Salesforce) and turn per-customer work into reusable abstractions, so the tenth connector costs a fraction of the first.
  • Build durable, long-running integration workflows with safe write-back into customer systems of record: idempotency, retries, replay semantics, and recovery paths from the start.
  • Own integration observability: know when a sync is stuck, degraded, or silently writing the wrong thing before the customer notices.
  • Define the authentication, network, and security posture per customer and get it through their review.
  • Feed what you learn in customer landscapes back into the product. You will see the same five problems before anyone else does.

What we are looking for

  • ERP integration depth, non-negotiable: you have delivered productive ERP integrations and know the interface landscape first-hand (IDoc, BAPI/RFC, OData/Gateway, CPI/BTP Integration Suite), on both S/4HANA and ECC, and you know which one to reach for and why.
  • Functional grounding: fluent in at least one of SD (order-to-cash) or MM (procure-to-pay), credible in the other, plus the FI touchpoints for AP/AR. You know what a schedule line, a condition record, and a three-way match actually are.
  • Engineering, not just configuration: 5+ years building and operating backend systems with real Python depth, owning production services rather than just delivering features.
  • Reliability instinct: idempotency, retries, and observability are part of how you design, not afterthoughts. A workflow engine like Temporal in production is a strong plus.
  • Customer-facing credibility: you can stand in front of an enterprise IT department, absorb their constraints, push back where it matters, and leave them confident.
  • End-to-end ownership: you identify what's broken or missing before you're asked, and you don't leave the system worse than you found it.
  • Professional English; German is a strong advantage given our customer base.
  • You're happy being in the office five days a week.

title: Aerospace Program Manager
description:
About Us:

Burloak Technologies is a leader in the additive manufacturing industry and provides engineering services for additive manufacturing, materials development, high precision CNC machining and metrology. Burloak Technologies works with the most innovative companies in the space, aerospace, automotive and industrial markets to rapidly transition their most challenging part designs to be additively manufactured at scale.


Position Summary:

The Program Manager is a customer-facing role that serves as a critical link between customers and internal teams, ensuring that orders are expertly managed from handover through execution in a dynamic, high-performance manufacturing environment. Reporting to the General Manager, this role is responsible for managing the handover of orders from the Business Development team and translating customer and commercial requirements into clear, actionable inputs for internal teams.
Operating with moderate autonomy, the Program Manager serves as a key information conduit between customers, the PMO, and internal departments, working closely with the Project Coordinator to ensure customer purchase orders and timelines are accurately converted into department-level execution plans.
This role is central to ensuring customer commitments are met, project compliance is maintained, and internal teams remain aligned on priorities and deliverables. Success in this position requires strong organizational skills, clear communication, and the ability to coordinate effectively across a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities:

Customer and Order Management

  • Manage the handover of new orders from the Business Development team, ensuring all commercial and technical requirements are clearly documented and communicated to internal stakeholders.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for customers throughout the project lifecycle, maintaining professional, timely, and transparent communication.
  • Coordinate and facilitate customer meetings, track action items, and follow up on outstanding deliverables.
  • Monitor and manage customer timelines, contractual commitments, and delivery requirements to ensure alignment with internal execution plans.
  • Translate customer and commercial requirements into clear, structured inputs that enable internal planning, scheduling, and production teams to execute effectively.

Project Scheduling and Compliance

  • Maintain and manage the master project schedule, ensuring it accurately reflects current priorities, milestones, and customer commitments.
  • Ensure all projects comply with internal PMO processes, documentation standards, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Accurately documenting the project's creation, development, and execution as well as documenting the project's scope, budget, and justification.
  • Manage all customer documentation, including all output documentation using best practices and secure file transfer
  • Monitor project progress against contractual and customer requirements, identifying variances and escalating risks to the VP of Operations, as required.
  • Coordinate with the Project Coordinator to ensure customer requirements are translated into accurate department-level work plans.
  • Support the continuous improvement of PMO processes, templates, and documentation practices.
  • Act as the focal and ensure compliance with all Trade and Export Control, including Canada Controlled Goods Program.
  • Support development/internal project planning, as required.

Cross-Functional Coordination and Communication

  • Act as a reliable and organized conduit between customers, the PMO, and internal departments including operations, engineering, quality, and additive manufacturing.
  • Provide timely and accurate project status updates to internal stakeholders and customers, ensuring all parties remain aligned on priorities and deliverables.
  • Coordinate with Project Coordinator and operational teams to support effective sequencing of work and on-time delivery.
  • Manage all communications and data flow with customer.
  • Participate in internal project reviews, escalating issues proactively and supporting resolution of schedule or quality risks.

Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date project records within the ERP system and PMO tools, including order status, milestones, and customer communications.
  • Prepare and distribute project reports, meeting summaries, and status updates as required.
  • Support the development and maintenance of standard PMO documentation, including project trackers, customer communication logs, and schedule templates.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support departmental and organizational objectives

title: B2 Fraud Decision Maker - Social Security Scotland
description:
Social Security Scotland is looking for an individual to join the Fraud and Error Resolution Unit (FERU) as a Fraud Decision Maker.

Do you have experience in undertaking complex benefit decision making, particularly in relation to Adult Disability Payment? Do you have a proven ability to work effectively with stakeholders in a changing environment and contribute to overcoming challenges? If so, this permanent opportunity for a B2 Fraud Decision Maker could be for you.

As a Fraud Decision Maker within the Error and Insights Branch, you will play an important role in protecting the integrity of Scotland's social security system. Working within a dynamic and collaborative environment, you will apply your decision-making expertise to assess complex evidence and make fair, consistent and legally robust entitlement decisions.

This role offers the opportunity to contribute to the safeguarding of public funds while ensuring individuals receive the correct entitlement in line with legislation and policy intent.

The successful candidate will demonstrate flexibility, be comfortable in a changing environment, and enjoy working collaboratively to identify opportunities for improvements, exploring new ideas and solutions.

Responsibilities

  • Reviewing fraud investigation reports, to inform a balance of probability decision as to whether a new benefit decision is required.
  • Undertaking new benefit decisions as required.
  • Creating benefit overpayments.
  • Determining client liability for overpayment.
  • Instigating recovery action by referral to Debt Management.
  • Providing evidence in court as a witness on behalf of the Agency in fraud prosecution case proceedings.
  • Supporting CSD with Re-determination requests.
  • Supporting Appeals Officer as appropriate where a Tribunal hearing is requested.

Success Profiles
We use an assessment framework called ‘Success Profiles’ which lists the elements we test and provides detailed descriptions of each. Find out more about the framework here

For this post, the following Success Profile elements will be assessed:

Experience:

  1. Extensive experience of making complex decisions on Adult Disability Payment cases.

  2. Significant experience of producing high-quality reports on complex cases, evaluating evidence from multiple sources, applying policy, and delivering balanced, evidence-based decisions and recommendations within agreed timescales.

Behaviours:

  • Communicating and Influencing - Level 3
  • Making Effective Decisions - Level 3
  • Seeing the bigger picture - Level 3
  • Working at Pace - Level 3

You can find out more about Success Profiles Behaviours here.

How to Apply
Apply online, you must provide a CV and a Supporting Statement (of no more than 1000 words) which provides evidence of how you meet the Success Profiles above. Both the CV and the Supporting Statement provided will be assessed against the criteria for the role

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can be used to support your application, but all statements and examples provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, and presented as your own) applications will be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action.

Please see our candidate guidance for more information on acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI in recruitment.

Should a large number of applications be received, an initial sift may be conducted using the CV and Supporting Statement on Experience - Significant experience of producing high-quality reports on complex cases, evaluating evidence from multiple sources, applying policy, and delivering balanced, evidence-based decisions and recommendations within agreed timescales. Candidates who pass the initial sift will have their applications fully assessed.

If invited for further assessment, this will consist of an interview and a job simulation exercise.

We aim to provide feedback on request. However, if we receive a large number of applications it may not be possible for us to provide specific feedback on your application. We will provide feedback on request to candidates who attend an interview/assessment.

Information Session
We are holding a candidate information session to provide you with information about the application and interview process, as well as further information on the role and team.

The session will be held on Tuesday 27th October from 12 noon to 1pm.

Please join us using the following link - Click here to join the meeting.

We offer rewarding careers and employ people across Scotland in a wide range of professions and roles. We are committed to recruiting a diverse workforce that is representative of the clients we serve. Find more about us here.

We offer a supportive and inclusive working environment along with a wide range of employee benefits. Find out more about what we offer.

We embrace a hybrid working style where all colleagues will spend time in either our Glasgow or Dundee offices. title: Receiving Specialist
description:
Position Summary

The Receiving Specialist is responsible for ensuring the accurate receipt, inspection, documentation, and tracking of incoming inventory while maintaining inventory accuracy across warehouse and inventory management systems. This role combines hands-on receiving functions with analytical inventory control responsibilities to support efficient operations, minimize discrepancies, and optimize inventory performance.


Key Responsibilities

description:
Position Description:

Would you like to have a career with a collaborative, diverse, and dynamic mining company? We have an exciting opportunity for you!

We are looking for a Water/Wastewater Operations Project Manager to join the Team at our Grants closure site. This role oversees day to day groundwater treatment operations, plans and executes projects to ensure ongoing treatment success, makes strategic operational and closure recommendations, and will collaborate with other site staff to plan and prepare for site reclamation milestone projects. The Project Manager will routinely plan, schedule and perform or oversee engineering and technical tasks relating to the site’s groundwater treatment systems and infrastructure.

At Barrick, our vision is to be the world’s most valued gold and copper mining business by finding, developing, and owning the best assets with the best people. We are committed to a safe work environment sending every person home safe and healthy every day, and leaving a sustainable legacy on our host communities.

Responsibilities:

  • Oversee day-to-day groundwater treatment operations, including supervision of RO Operator hourly staff

  • Collaborate with other staff on all projects pertaining to groundwater treatment, site reclamation, engineering, construction, reclamation and decommissioning work including work scope, schedule, and budget

  • Ensure on-going communication and cooperation with other site personnel to optimize the ability for all to obtain the necessary information and/or accomplish a shared objective

  • Participate in preparation of comprehensive technical reports to support groundwater reclamation activities based on collected data, capital and O&M costs, and health & safety

  • Manage the preparation and administration of consultant and contractor contracts

  • Liaise with tailings storage facilities (TSF) Engineer of Record to ensure the stability of the onsite TSFs as to not pose a potential risk to human health and/or the environment

  • Facilitate organizing and scheduling of “water watch” call out activities

Qualifications:

  • A bachelor’s degree in engineering or a technical field is required

  • Greater than 5 years of experience in the mining, construction, or consulting industry is required

  • Possess and apply project management skills to multiple projects pertaining to groundwater operations, reclamation, and decommissioning is required

  • Excellent communication skills, both orally and written, with both internal and external contacts and the ability to work with all levels of the organization required

  • Knowledge of regulatory constraints related to radioactive material and activities is a plus

  • Knowledge of geotechnical engineering principles pertaining to tailings storage facilities monitoring and maintenance is a plus

  • Knowledge of process engineering principles pertaining to water treatment plant operations and maintenance is a plus

  • Willingness to work during non-work hours should upset conditions occur at the site is required

  • Have a demonstrated ability to lead a multi-disciplinary team of peers and junior site personnel, while maintaining effective working relationships with other personnel and/or consultants/contractors is preferred

What We Can Offer You

  • A comprehensive compensation package including a competitive medical, dental, and vision plan with national provider networks, a 401k retirement plan with employer contribution, paid time off, company match share purchase program, and much more!

  • Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team.

  • Opportunities to grow and learn with the industry colleagues are endless.

  • Access to a variety of career opportunities across the organization.

  • Barrick is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

About Barrick

At Barrick, our mission is to be the world’s most valued gold and copper mining business by finding, developing, and owning the best assets, with the best people, to deliver sustainable returns for our owners and partners. Our vision is to be the world’s most valued gold and copper mining business by finding, developing, and operating the best assets with the best people. We are committed to a safe work environment sending every person home safe and healthy every day and leaving a sustainable legacy on our host communities. We are committed to partnering with our host countries and communities to transform their natural resources into tangible benefits and mutual prosperity.

Barrick has gold and copper mining operations and projects in 13 countries in North and South America, Africa, Papua New Guinea and Saudi Arabia. Our diversified portfolio spans many of the world’s prolific gold districts and is focused on high-margin, long-life assets.

The company’s shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol B, and on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol ABX.

Bursting with culture, energy, and opportunity, the London Borough of Waltham Forest is a fantastic and exciting place to work.

We are a highly ambitious borough. Driven by culture and the innate creativity of our residents, we have developed new and innovative ways to build our communities. Our Council is relentlessly resident-focused, insight-led, digitally driven and commercially minded; a Council focused on meeting the needs of our existing and future residents.

About the role:

Every day in Waltham Forest, people face the risk of losing their home. In this role, you won’t just process cases; you’ll change outcomes.

We’re looking for experienced, resilient Housing Options & Assessment Officers who can think on their feet, make sound decisions, and work compassionately with residents in crisis. If you thrive in a fast paced environment and want your work to have visible impact, this could be the role for you.

This is not a desk job; it’s frontline, high impact work.

As a Housing Options & Assessment Officer, you’ll manage a varied caseload of residents who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. You’ll be responsible for assessing needs, making legally robust decisions and, crucially, identifying realistic solutions that prevent homelessness wherever possible.

You’ll be working with residents who may be vulnerable, in crisis, or facing complex challenges. Success in this role requires confidence, sound judgement, emotional resilience, and the ability to stay focused under pressure.

The ideal candidate for this role would be someone who has a extensive understanding of the realities of frontline housing work

This role offers a Career Development salary range, however it is important to note that candidates with substantial and directly relevant experience may be considered for the higher starting salary within the advertised grade, subject to assessment and the Council's pay policies

>> Click here to download the Role Profile <<

Key Responsibilities:

  • Assess housing needs and determine statutory duties under the Homelessness Reduction Act 2018
  • Conduct detailed interviews (face-to-face and telephone) with residents in housing need
  • Produce clear, compliant statutory decision letters and Personal Housing Plans
  • Take proactive action to prevent homelessness, including engaging with landlords and agents
  • Promote a full range of housing options including private rented solutions
  • Work collaboratively with colleagues and partners to progress cases and remove barriers
  • Maintain accurate records, manage data, and contribute to service performance.

Qualifications and Requirements:

To be considered for this position, you should meet the following requirements:

  • Minimum 2 years’ experience of having worked in a fast paced, resident focused environment to manage a varied caseload of applicants.
  • Minimum 2 years’ experience in a busy Housing Options / Prevention & Assessment service
  • Knowledge of frontline housing services (Desirable)
  • Excellent knowledge and application of IT systems and software packages.
  • Ability to work with minimum supervision, using problem solving skills and initiative to provide a resident focused support service.
  • Excellent levels of literacy and numeracy.
  • Ability to work flexibly, balancing competing priorities and meeting deadlines whilst understanding the needs, timescales and deadlines of others.
  • Ability to deal diplomatically and confidentially with a wider range of stakeholders internally and externally.
  • Strong working knowledge of homelessness legislation and processes
  • Confidence managing a complex caseload independently
  • The ability to make sound decisions in challenging, time pressured situations
  • Excellent communication skills, including handling difficult conversations with empathy and clarity
  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail

Just as important:

  • You’re resilient; you can handle pressure without losing focus
  • You’re proactive; you look for solutions, not just processes
  • You’re committed; you want to make a genuine difference

What you’ll get in return:

  • A role where your work has visible, meaningful impact every day
  • A supportive team environment with opportunities to learn and develop
  • A council that is committed to fairness, inclusion, and staff wellbeing

title: Mgr, Interconnections Planning & Policy
description:
JOB TITLE

Manager, Interconnections Planning & Policy

LOCATION

Atlanta, GA

POSITION SUMMARY

At Georgia Power, we are making historic investments to support unprecedented load growth while maintaining a clean, safe, reliable, and affordable electric system. The Manager, Interconnections Planning & Policy is a strategic leadership role responsible for the end‑to‑end integration of generation onto the Georgia Power system, including distribution- and transmission-connected generation resources across all technology types such as gas, renewables, battery storage, and others. The scale, complexity, and speed of integrating these generation assets continues to increase to support Georgia’s clean, safe, reliable, and affordable growth. For the Transmission team, direct responsibility for origination and partnerships with other Transmission teams for the direct interconnection and upstream delivery projects. This includes capital budget approvals for initial scoping and COD, final design, support through construction, and true-up accounting at closeout.

This position leads other people-leaders and several highly-technical, industry subject matter experts. This role is responsible for leading the strategy and development of solutions that proactively enable the safe, reliable, affordable, and timely interconnection of generation assets to the grid. Additionally, this position will ensure compliance with federal and state regulatory policies including engagement with Public Service Commissioners and Public Service Commission Staff as well as other stakeholders such as generation developers. To be most effective, this manager will coordinate across a wide range of Southern Company’s enterprise functions including but not limited to Transmission, Distribution, Generation, Renewables, Resource Planning, Policy & Services, Compliance, Operations, Legal, and Customer organizations. The role serves as a single point of accountability for Georgia Power’s interconnection policies, processes, and execution to ensure Georgia continues to reliably grow capacity resources to meet increasing customer growth.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position will have responsibilities across four primary focus areas.

  1. Strategic Vision for Interconnections Processes and Strategy

  • Own generation interconnections strategy, governance, and enterprise accountability, including clear escalation paths and readiness criteria.

  • Lead cross-functional alignment and communication across Southern Company functions and with external stakeholders to coordinate cradle-to-grave solutions development and execution for all generation interconnections to protect grid reliability.

  • Set the strategy for interconnections policy and process needs to enable compliance through continued successful interconnection of all types of generation assets to the grid, including opportunities to integrate technologies and analytics into work practices.

  • Through close coordination with enterprise partner organizations and external stakeholders, identify and execute opportunities to ensure timely, reliable, and accurate project solution identification and reduce delays and risk of project scope changes. Some partner organizations include Transmission, Distribution, Planning, Generation, Policy & Services, Compliance, Operations, and Customer organizations.

  1. Transmission Interconnections

  • Provide the strategy and direction for transmission interconnections leadership in concert with partner organizations and ensure senior leaders remain informed and provide input as needed, including executives.

  • There have been and continue to be numerous RFPs to procure generation capacity resources that increase generation in Georgia. Given Georgia’s growth, these RFPs continue to develop at a faster pace and with increasing scope. In 2025, Georgia Power certified nearly 10GW of capacity resources with the Public Service Commission and currently has another capacity RFP to procure between 2-6 GW of new generation. These are some of the largest but not the only RFPs the transmission interconnections team is responsible for studying and shepherding through the project and interconnection lifecycle processes.

  • RFPs to procure capacity resources through transmission-connected generation will not only serve to meet the growing energy demands of Georgia but also the retirement/replacement strategy for existing generation assets in the future.

  • Continue to inform and coordinate with large load interconnections process and the development of projects to ensure consistency with transmission interconnections policies as well as project engineering and cost allocation methodologies.

  1. Distribution Interconnections

  • Provide the strategy and direction for distribution interconnections leadership in concert with partner organizations and ensure senior leaders remain informed and provide input as needed, including executives.

  • There are a growing number of DER assets and technology types seeking to interconnect to the grid. Focus should continue to be placed on ensuring appropriate policies, study capabilities, and methodologies to evaluate these requests to not lose sight of our core principles of safety, reliability, cost, and customer satisfaction.

  • Lead strategy to address the increasing complexity of distribution interconnections. For example, adding battery storage to solar distributed generation projects changes the interconnection considerations, and enabling DERMS to allow inverters and customer controls requires additional coordination. Successful implementation of BTM and Customer DER programs requires a balanced approach of support to ensure our customers are protected from a safety, affordability, and reliability perspective.

  1. Policy Leadership and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Represent Georgia Power and Southern Company professionally with customers, regulators, industry groups, and external stakeholders.

  • Regular communications and coordination with senior leaders at Georgia Power and Southern Company, including executives.

  • Own compliance and governance for all interconnections projects to comply with Southern Company, Georgia Power, and other regulatory or industry interconnection requirements and other applicable planning/operational requirements prior to energization. Provide guidance on behalf of Georgia Power as needed.

  • Provide ongoing regulatory support and develop positive relationships with the Georgia Public Service Commission through interactions with Commissioners, Commission Staff, and direct participation in other stakeholder requests such as the Distributed Generation Working Group to represent interconnection issues and requirements. Also serve as an interconnections subject matter expert to support other regulatory proceedings or legislative issues as needed such as the IRP and Rate Case filings or potential proposed legislation.

  • Drive continuous improvement by identifying systemic gaps, lessons learned, and opportunities to continue enabling Georgia’s growth in a reliable, safe, and affordable manner and strengthen grid readiness.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of experience in the energy sector, utilities, infrastructure, or large‑scale project delivery.
  • 3+ years of people leadership or team management experience.
  • 2+ years as a leader-of-leaders is a plus.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating complex, enterprise & cross-functional initiatives with significant safety and reliability implications.
  • Strong understanding of transmission and distribution systems, grid operations, and generation interconnection processes and requirements.
  • Experience with regulatory policies in the energy industry is preferred.

SKILLS, ABILITIES & LEADERSHIP ATTRIBUTES

  • Strong focus on safety with preferred field experience in transmission and distribution, control/communication schemes, legal/contracts, knowledge of DER capabilities, and regulatory policy.
  • Creativity and strategy development, ability to lead evolving requirements, building a strong learning culture that is not afraid to make mistakes and learn quickly, and comfortable in working in a fast-changing environment.
  • Proven ability to lead teams, develop strategy, and execute in a highly regulated, safety‑critical environment to balance customer growth with grid reliability and compliance.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of engaging executives, technical teams, and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to build consensus, manage conflict, and drive decisions across organizational boundaries.
  • High judgment, accountability, and comfort operating with ambiguity during rapid growth.

LEADERSHIP EXPECTATIONS

This role is expected to consistently demonstrate Southern Company leadership behaviors, including:

  • Safety & Integrity – Enforces technical standards without compromise.
  • One Team – Coordinates seamlessly across organizations to deliver outcomes.
  • Operational Excellence – Brings discipline and rigor to large load execution.
  • Customer & Community Focus – Enables growth while protecting reliability and affordability.

title: Senior Frontend Engineer
description:
About GeneralMind

GeneralMind builds AI Systems of Action for complex enterprise workflows. We deploy AI employees that automate messy operational handovers across supply chains - processing orders, validating invoices, coordinating suppliers, and handling exceptions directly on top of enterprise systems like SAP, Oracle, JDE, and Dynamics.

Our platform combines AI agents, operational context graphs, and real transaction data to achieve Autopilot-grade automation in real operational environments.

We work closely with leading global companies across manufacturing, retail, and logistics to deploy AI into mission-critical workflows.

About the role

We are looking for an exceptional Senior Frontend Engineer to join our Bangalore team. This is not a role for someone looking to execute tickets handed down from above. You will own technical decisions end to end, shape how we build our product interfaces, and directly influence our product trajectory.

You will operate primarily as an individual contributor (80%), while also stepping up to lead and mentor a small squad of engineers (20%). We expect you to bring strong opinions, hold them loosely, and always optimize for what's right in the long run.

What You'll Do

Engineering & Architecture

  • Take full ownership of frontend systems from scoping through delivery - you ask the right questions early, cut through ambiguity, and drive things to completion.

  • Make and defend architectural decisions that balance shipping velocity with long-term maintainability; you know when to build a custom component and when to reach for a proven pattern.

  • Build fast, accessible, and reliable interfaces with React and Next.js as your primary stack, with enough full-stack range to collaborate effectively across Python-based backend services.

  • Evaluate AI tooling critically - you use it daily to move faster, but you understand that vibe coding is a liability, and you hold your AI-generated output to the same standard as everything else.

Technical Leadership

  • Lead your squad during planning cycles: go deep on each ticket, challenge scope where needed, and make sure the team ships with clarity.

  • Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through code review, pairing, and design discussions - not by micromanaging, but by setting a high bar.

  • Proactively identify bottlenecks, technical debt, and systemic risks before they become emergencies.

What we are looking for

  • Experience: 8+ years of hands-on frontend engineering experience, with a consistent track record of shipping production applications at scale.

  • Technical depth: TypeScript and React are non-negotiable. Deep experience with Next.js (App Router, server components, data fetching patterns) is expected. Familiarity with modern styling (Tailwind CSS), state management (Zustand, TanStack Query), and component architecture (Radix UI, headless patterns) is a strong plus.

  • Judgment: You understand the trade-off between a pixel-perfect custom component and a pragmatic library solution - and you know which the situation actually calls for.

  • Ownership: You don't wait to be told. You identify what needs doing, flag it, and drive it to completion.

  • Discipline: Detail-oriented to a fault. You can take over sprint and cycle planning for a squad and make it better - tighter tickets, cleaner scoping, fewer surprises.

  • AI-native, not AI-dependent: You integrate AI tools naturally into your daily workflow for speed and leverage, but you review, reason about, and take full responsibility for everything you ship.

  • Independent thinker: You form your own technical views, push back when something doesn't make sense, and don't need consensus to act.

  • Supply chain domain experience: A meaningful plus - we work in a space where understanding warehouse workflows, inventory logic, or ERP-adjacent systems translates directly into better engineering decisions.

title: CFCV/2026/040 Intern (Programme Engagement and Health Information), Pekanbaru
description:
Reference No. : CFCV/2026/040

Duty Station : Pekanbaru, Indonesia
Organization Unit : Pekanbaru Office
Type of Appointment : Internship
Report to : Head of Field Office
Estimated Start Date : As soon as possible
Closing Date : 2 November 2026


Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a related organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, IOM works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non- governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all.

Operational in Indonesia for more than 40 years, IOM Indonesia is working on a wide range of activities in partnership with the Government of Indonesia, civil society, private sector actors, migrants and communities. IOM Indonesia is engaged in several thematic areas, including: Counter-Trafficking (CT), Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion (LMI), Disasters, Climate and Resilience (DCR), Immigration and Border Governance (IBG), Refugee Care, Migration Health, Migration Governance, and Resettlement and Voluntary Returns.

IOM Indonesia aims to improve the quality of care for refugees and asylum seekers referred to IOM by the Government of Indonesia according to applicable international humanitarian and human rights standards. IOM also contributes to the increased protection of vulnerable subgroups of displaced persons, such as unaccompanied migrant children (UMCs), victims of sexual and gender-based violence, pregnant women, and the elderly, among others, through the establishment of referral mechanisms involving the active participation of specialized state and non-state service providers.

Under the direct supervision of the Head of Field Office in Pekanbaru and technical supervision of the Refugee Care and Migration Health Units, the incumbent will work in close coordination with the relevant technical focal points and support the implementation of Refugee Care and Migration Health programme activities in Pekanbaru.

Responsibilities and Accountabilities

  1. Under the direct guidance of the Head of Field Office, participate in relevant Refugee Care and Migration Health programme activities.

  2. Support the implementation of mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and migration health activities under the supervision of the relevant technical unit.

  3. Co-facilitate general/non-clinical counselling and psychosocial support sessions under appropriate technical supervision.

  4. To facilitate professional development, participate in selected components of the case management process under the guidance and supervision of the Head of Field Office and the relevant technical unit.

  5. Contribute to the collection, review, and analysis of programme data related to MHPSS and migration health.

  6. Participate in health and psychosocial awareness activities, including health cadre meetings and community-based initiatives.

  7. Support Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration (AVRR) and associated movement activities, as appropriate and under relevant supervision.

  8. Undertake other duties and programme-related learning activities relevant to the internship, as assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (minimum undergraduate school) in Psychology, Social Welfare, Social Work, Education, or a related field from an accredited academic institution; or
  • Enrolled in a second university degree (graduate school/equivalent); or
  • Have graduated with a university degree within one year of graduation.

Experience

  • Relevant professional or volunteer experience with civil society organizations, volunteer groups is an advantage.

Skills

  • Excellence computer skills (word processing, spreadsheet, database, email exchange, Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Access), SPSS);
  • Flexible and open to learning new experiences
  • Good interpersonal, networking, and communication skills
  • Ability to work effectively and harmoniously with colleagues from varied culture and professional backgrounds
  • Ability to write clear and concise report.

Languages

For this internship, fluency in English and Bahasa Indonesia is required (oral and written).

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Notes

We encourage applications from candidates who are currently based in the same area as the duty station. This is a locally recruited position

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Depending on experience and location, interns are granted a small monthly stipend to help offset costs. Interns benefiting from an internship allowance or scholarship granted by their university or other sponsoring body that includes financial remuneration or credits for coursework will not be eligible for the stipend.

IOM covers Interns against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the internship. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Interns are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Maintenance Director
description:
About Us

RAM Partners, LLC, is a full-service real estate management company that manages more than 80,000 apartments throughout the United States. We specialize in multi-family community management for a variety of third-party owners. We are a service-oriented, hands-on company. Our brick and mortar are our people.


Compensation: $85,0000 to $95,000 annually


ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:


Project Management

  • Working with the Property Manager and Area Vice President to create and maintain budget, project plan, and schedules for capital improvements, deferred and preventative maintenance, building construction including HVAC, fire suppression systems, electrical, building maintenance contracts, building signage, security installations, furniture, etc.

Assemble, analyze, and submit bids to the Business Manager with a recommendation for action; acknowledge receipt of all goods and materials delivered to the site for maintenance and repairs; manage ongoing contracts with contractors and vendors.

Maintenance Management

Maintenance Supervision (coordinate with / supervise the Maintenance Supervisor)

In cooperation with the Property Manager and Maintenance Supervisor, perform associate annual reviews, candidate selection, and changes in maintenance staff assignments. Work with HR, PM, and AVP on employee relations issues.
  • Ensure facilities spaces are kept clean, safe, orderly, and organized, and ensure that there is a current inventory at all times.
  • With the Maintenance Supervisor, maintain employee work schedules, including assignments, job rotation, training, vacations and paid time off, coverage for absenteeism, and overtime scheduling.
  • Coordinate with building operations for utility, facility, or other shutdown activity that can affect operations.
  • Set objectives to more effectively implement work procedures and techniques to eliminate underutilization of personnel. Report status of workload and other information on the efficient operation of the department.
  • Complete other duties as assigned.

title: Senior Production Planner - Fabrication
description:
Job Summary

The Senior Production Planner, Fabrication is responsible for developing, maintaining, and executing the detailed fabrication production schedule within an Engineer-to-Order (ETO) manufacturing environment. The role balances capacity, material, and engineering readiness to keep fabricated components flowing on time to Assembly.

This role serves as the primary planning liaison between Fabrication, Engineering, Supply Chain, Programming, and the Assembly Planning team and owns fabrication jobs from release through completion.


Job Duties and Responsibilities

Fabrication Scheduling & Execution

  • Translate the 12-week assembly production plan into a detailed fabrication schedule by resource and work center, and maintain it as priority, capacity, and material availability change.
  • Sequence and level-load work to optimize fabrication resources and ensure components are completed on time to support Assembly.
  • Monitor shop-floor progress, open jobs, and WIP against the schedule, adjusting priorities as needed.
  • Own fabrication performance metrics, including schedule attainment, on-time delivery to Assembly, and WIP levels.

Fabrication Job Ownership

  • Manage the full job lifecycle, including job release, material issuance, component receipt, and timely job closure.
  • Maintain accurate job dates, schedules, quantities, and production data within Epicor.

Capacity & Constraint Management

  • Proactively identify bottlenecks and constraints (capacity, workload, material, programming, and engineering readiness) and coordinate cross-functional actions to resolve them.
  • Escalate risks to production commitments and recommend recovery or mitigation plans when needed.

Cross-Functional Planning & Communication

  • Coordinate with Engineering, Supply Chain, Production, Programming, Quality, and Project Management to support fabrication execution.
  • Manage and communicate the scheduling impact of engineering changes, customer revisions, material shortages, and production disruptions.
  • Lead daily and weekly fabrication scheduling reviews.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve fabrication flow, resource utilization, schedule adherence, and planning processes.
  • Drive the development and standardization of production planning and scheduling processes.
  • Mentor planners and schedulers and serve as subject-matter expert for fabrication planning in Epicor.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree with 4+ years of experience in production planning, scheduling, or manufacturing operations; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • Advanced ERP/MRP proficiency with a strong understanding of BOM structures, routings, production scheduling, and capacity planning.
  • Experience coordinating across Engineering, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and make effective decisions in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and production scheduling tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in an Engineer-to-Order (ETO), Make-to-Order (MTO), or project-based manufacturing environment.
  • Epicor ERP experience.
  • APICS CPIM or CSCP certification.

Benefits:

  • PTO/ESST
  • Paid holidays
  • $100 individual deductible and $300 family deductible health insurance
  • Paid Weekly
  • Vision and Dental Insurance
  • 401K / Life Insurance / STD

title: Engineering Supervisor - InterContinental Ras Al Khaimah Mina Al Arab Resort & Spa

As the world’s largest family of luxury hotels, we take great pride in being genuine ambassadors of the InterContinental® brand. title: Director of Contracts
description:
The Director of Contracts is a key leadership role responsible for shaping and strengthening Capstone’s contracts and compliance functions during an exciting period of growth and innovation. This position plays an important role in helping the business move quickly and strategically while ensuring strong legal and regulatory compliance across state, federal, and international environments.


This leader will drive best practices in contract management, improve compliance processes, and help build scalable systems that support the organization’s continued growth. Working cross-functionally with teams across sales, marketing, digital product development, content development, finance, and executive leadership, the Director of Contracts will help ensure contracts align with business goals while thoughtfully managing risk.


The role also oversees contract negotiation and administration, intellectual property compliance, and supports royalty-related processes in partnership with finance. We’re looking for someone who is both strategic and hands-on — a collaborative problem solver who enjoys building processes, improving operations, and working in a fast-paced, evolving environment.


This hybrid position is based out of either our Mankato or Eden Prairie, MN office. Employees are expected to work from their designated office a minimum of two (2) days per week, with the flexibility to work remotely up to three (3) days per week.


Why You’ll Want to Join Capstone

We support teaching and learning with amazing content that engages students, inspires teachers, and connects families and communities to move literacy forward. Capstone is a fast-paced growth company committed to cultivating a love of reading and learning. We know that Learning is for Everyone.


For over 30 years, Capstone has been a national leader in K-5 educational content including digital products (PebbleGo, PebbleGo Next, PebbleGo Create, Capstone Interactive, Capstone Connect) and award-winning books. We combine a passion for helping foster a powerful love of reading and learning with the talent to create amazing content.


We are a mission-driven company that provides opportunities for professional learning and development and a culture of inclusion and belonging.


YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES


Leadership

  • Serves as the senior leader overseeing contracts and compliance, responsible for developing and executing functional strategies that optimize contracting and risk management practices.
  • Builds, develops, and leads a high-performing team; fosters a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Acts as a trusted advisor and cross-functional partner to sales, marketing, digital product, content, finance, and executive leadership.
  • Communicates effectively with external vendors, partners, and regulatory agencies.
  • Proactively identifies, assesses, and mitigates risk; communicates key risks and leads mitigation efforts across the organization.
  • Establishes organizational best practices, tools, and processes for contract management and compliance.
  • Operates as a “strategic doer,” balancing leadership with hands-on execution.
  • Navigates a complex and evolving regulatory landscape with transparency and adaptability.
  • Demonstrates strong emotional intelligence, responsiveness, and a solution-oriented mindset.
  • Delivers clear, effective communication tailored to diverse audiences.

Contracts

  • Drafts, reviews, negotiates, and has oversight over a wide range of agreements, including but not limited to content licensing, foreign rights, technology and SaaS agreements, distribution agreements, master service agreements, NDAs, and intellectual property licenses.
  • Reviews and approvals of legal documents executed by the Company, collaborating with outside counsel as needed.
  • Oversee trademark and copyright processes, including preliminary clearance and coordination with external counsel on registrations.
  • Evaluates intellectual property assets and provides recommendations on usage and risk.
  • Supports business development initiatives by assessing contractual risk and structuring agreements, accordingly, including those related to partnerships and M&A activity.
  • Leads the development, standardization, and continuous improvement of contract templates, playbooks, and workflows.
  • Manages departmental budget and external legal spend.

Compliance

  • Designs, implements, and continuously improves compliance frameworks aligned with applicable laws and regulations.
  • Evaluates internal systems and processes to ensure adherence to legal, regulatory, and policy requirements.
  • Develops, updates, and communicates company policies related to contracts, data privacy, and compliance.
  • Partners with internal stakeholders to educate and reinforce compliance standards across the organization.
  • Establishes and monitors risk management strategies to maintain acceptable levels of compliance risk.

Education, Experience, and Skills desired:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, legal studies, paralegal studies, or related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 6+ years of experience in contracts, compliance, and/or data privacy.
  • Demonstrated experience leading and developing teams.
  • Experience in publishing, K-12 education, or EdTech industries preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of contract law, intellectual property, and regulatory compliance.
  • Excellent negotiation, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including virtual communication.
  • High attention to detail with strong organizational and project management capabilities.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (especially Outlook and Excel); experience with contract lifecycle management tools is a plus.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.

Travel Requirements

Approximately 5-10% travel may be required in the future.


Inclusion & Belonging

Capstone embraces equal opportunity and a culture of belonging for all employees and applicants. We are an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer. All candidate information will be kept private according to EEO guidelines. If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or the recruiting process, please send a request to hrservices@capstonepub.com.


The pay range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered surrounding compensation including but not limited to: skill sets, experience and training, work location, and other business and organizational needs. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $115,000-$145,000.


Capstone strives to provide comprehensive and market-competitive benefits to meet the needs of our employees and their families. Click here to see our benefits.


Pre-Employment Background Check Required.


California Applicants:

Applicants from California can access our California Privacy Notice here.

At this time Capstone unfortunately cannot sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa. To be considered for one of our roles, applicants must be authorized to work in the United States.

title: UK & US Expansion (all genders)
description:

title: Deburring Technician
description:
About Us:

Burloak Technologies is a leader in the additive manufacturing industry and provides engineering services for additive manufacturing, materials development, high precision CNC machining and metrology. Burloak Technologies works with the most innovative companies in the space, aerospace, automotive and industrial markets to rapidly transition their most challenging part designs to be additively manufactured at scale.


Position Summary:

The Deburring Technician is responsible for safely and efficiently performing deburring, support removal, surface finishing, and post-processing activities on additively manufactured metal components to ensure they meet engineering specifications and quality standards. Working with a variety of hand tools, mechanical finishing equipment, and precision measuring instruments, this role inspects components for dimensional accuracy and surface quality while maintaining detailed production documentation. The Deburring Technician collaborates closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, CNC Machining, and Quality teams to support efficient production flow, identify process improvements, and ensure parts are ready for the next stage of manufacturing. This role plays a critical part in delivering high-quality components for the aerospace, space, automotive, and industrial sectors while maintaining a strong commitment to safety, quality, and continuous improvement.


Key Responsibilities:

Deburring and Post-Processing

  • Utilize hand tools including files, grinders, and deburring knives to remove burrs and sharp edges from additively manufactured metal components in materials such as aluminum, titanium, steel, and nickel-based alloys.
  • Operate mechanical deburring equipment including blasters, vibratory finishers, and grinding machines to smooth and polish component surfaces to required specifications.
  • Remove support structures from additively manufactured parts in accordance with work instructions and engineering requirements, ensuring components are not damaged during the process.
  • Select and apply appropriate deburring techniques based on part geometry, material type, and specified surface finish requirements.

Inspection and Quality Assurance

  • Conduct dimensional inspections using calipers, micrometers, and gauges to verify that parts meet specified tolerances following deburring and post-processing.
  • Perform visual inspections to identify burrs, sharp edges, surface defects, and non-conformances using magnifying tools or microscopes as required.
  • Ensure all deburring processes meet the company’s quality standards and specifications prior to releasing parts for the next stage of production.
  • Identify and escalate non-conformances or quality concerns to the quality control team in a timely and accurate manner.

Documentation and Reporting

  • Accurately document all deburring activities, inspection results, and corrective actions in accordance with company guidelines and quality requirements.
  • Maintain detailed records of deburring processes, including methods used, tools applied, and any part-specific observations or corrective actions taken.
  • Communicate effectively with quality control and production teams to provide timely status updates on parts and report any issues encountered during processing.

Tool and Equipment Maintenance

  • Regularly clean and maintain deburring tools and equipment to ensure optimal performance, accuracy, and longevity.
  • Identify and report equipment performance issues or maintenance needs promptly to prevent disruptions to production output.
  • Organize and maintain a clean, orderly workspace that reflects the expectations of an advanced manufacturing operation.

Safety and Compliance

  • Adhere to all workplace safety protocols at all times, including the proper use of personal protective equipment such as gloves, safety glasses, and hearing protection.
  • Follow all company policies and procedures, including attendance, workplace behaviour, and operational protocols.
  • Identify potential safety hazards and report concerns promptly to supervisors to maintain a safe working environment for all team members.

Team Coordination and Process Improvement

  • Work closely with CNC machinists, 3D printing technicians, and quality control inspectors to ensure seamless production workflow and consistently high-quality output.
  • Collaborate with engineering and production teams to troubleshoot and resolve issues related to burrs, surface finishes, and post-processing challenges.
  • Identify and suggest improvements to deburring processes to enhance efficiency, quality, and safety across the production area.

Professional Attributes and Team Contribution

  • Contribute positively to a collaborative team environment by sharing observations, supporting colleagues, and maintaining a respectful and professional attitude on the shop floor.
  • Communicate clearly and promptly with team members, supervisors, and cross-functional partners regarding part status, process issues, and production priorities.
  • Demonstrate accountability for the quality and accuracy of completed work, taking ownership of assigned tasks through to completion.
  • Maintain focus and composure during periods of high production demand, approaching challenges in a calm, solution-oriented manner.
  • Adhere consistently to established standards for workmanship, safety, and documentation, and encourage the same standards in those around them.
  • Embrace a mindset of continuous improvement by actively seeking to develop technical skills, learn new processes, and contribute to the efficiency and effectiveness of the deburring area.

title: Land Reform Unit - Policy Official
description:
Job description
This opportunity is only open to internal Scottish Government applicants who are currently 'Priority Movers'. Applications from individuals not currently on the Priority Mover list will be rejected and not considered.

Land Reform is a highly political area of policy that has been a priority of successive Governments since devolution. Land Reform is about how control, influence and ownership over our limited landmass is distributed across society. Policy areas under the broad umbrella of Land Reform include Community land ownership, the various Community Rights to Buy, the Scottish Land Fund, sponsorship of the Scottish Land Commission, policies relating to transparency of control/ownership of land and production of the government’s Land Rights

The Government recently passed the Land Reform (Scotland) Act 2025. This landmark legislation will:

  • Require owners of large landholdings to engage with local communities, including through the development of publicly available Land Management Plans which will be hosted by a public sector agency.
  • Enable communities to be pre-notified of land sales to they have more opportunity to buy land in a way that benefits the local area – including through utilising their Community Right to Buy.
  • Give Ministers new powers to require that large estates are sold into separate lots – thereby reducing concentration of land ownership in Scotland.
  • Create a new Land and Communities Commissioner (LCC) to be part of the Scottish Land Commission. The LCC will enforce some of the obligations on landowners in the Act and have a role in advising on the lotting of landholdings.

Though the Act has now passed, significant amounts of secondary legislation and guidance are needed before the policies can come into effect. The holder of this post will play a key role in the implementation of the Act in the coming years. Ministers are keen to deliver on implementation of the Act at pace and stakeholders are taking a keen interest in progress.

This is an opportunity to work on the delivery of landmark legislation that - once fully implemented - will impact over 50% of Scotland’s land. You will have the chance to work with stakeholders across rural Scotland, and work on policy development and secondary legislation and guidance, all whilst being part of a friendly, supportive and welcoming unit. We are seeking an individual who embraces working with a team to deliver for ministers, who has a strong interest in developing policy and legislation and who has a positive and supportive working style.

Responsibilities

Policy development and legislation :

  • Lead on policy development for certain areas of secondary legislation, working with internal and external stakeholders and with SGLD on instructions and supporting passage of the SSIs through Parliament.
  • Lead on drafting of statutory and non-statutory guidance, consultation materials and impact assessments for policy workstreams.
  • Work with analysts, stakeholders and researchers to ensure policy has a strong evidence base.

Policy support :

  • Lead on or contribute to relevant Micase, PQs, engagement briefings, submissions and FOI responses as required.

Other implementation :

  • Work with other policy organisations such as the Scottish Land Commission and Registers of Scotland on non-legislative areas of implementation.
  • Develop possible options around a portal for publication of land management plans and implement preferred option.

This role offers an excellent opportunity to further develop skills across stakeholder engagement, use of evidence and analysis, legislation, working with Ministers and broader policy development skills. The team works closely together and is flexible so exact policy areas of responsibility can be discussed in the team as a whole and may evolve depending on priorities.

Working pattern

This role is a permanent level transfer position.

How to Apply

Applications for this position will only be accepted from substantive B3 employees.

Please submit a statement outlining your suitability for the role, relevant skills and experience, and what you would bring to the team (maximum 500 words).

Selection Process

All candidates will be invited to an informal discussion with the Hiring Manager.

Informal discussion dates tbc.

title: Freight Handler- Full Time- 3rd Shift
