title: Strategic Policy Lead
description:
This is an Expression of Interest (EOI) opportunity, available on a lateral move basis only. Applications are open to Core Scottish Government employees only.

Job Title – Strategic Policy Lead

Working Arrangement – Staff in roles compatible with hybrid working should spend 40% of their contracted working time working in person at their contractual workplace. More information can be found within Hybrid Working Policy .

Grade – C2

Advert type – level transfer

Duration – Permanent

Eligibility - Expressions of interest are invited from substantive colleagues on level transfer from Core SG only.

Skilled Worker Sponsorship not being offered

Skilled Worker sponsorship is not available for this role. As a result, we are unable to appoint candidates who require Skilled Worker sponsorship now or in the future. Applicants must have an existing and ongoing right to work in the UK

The Directorate plays a leading role in the Scottish Government's work to ensure our economy, climate and communities all benefit from the green industrial transition and are resilient to climate change. This includes developing a thriving decarbonised economy, with world class public utilities and the best outcomes for Scottish consumers. Scotland has some of the most challenging targets for carbon reduction in the world and the Scottish Government is committed to pushing Scotland to the forefront in addressing climate change while tackling cross-cutting issues such as creating a prosperous future for children and young people, and promoting homegrown growth and international investment

An exciting opportunity has arisen within the Energy and Climate Change Directorate to lead a team to support the Director to coordinate the Directorates delivery plan, ensuring that we are meeting our agreed outcomes and the needs of Ministers and identifying synergies or improvements we can make to our policy approach across the Directorate and wider DG.

This is a high profile role that requires close working with Senior Management, Ministers and stakeholders across government, the wider public sector and industry. The role provides direct support to the Director of DECC and will be a key part of driving change in the directorate, supporting new ways of working, delivering ministerial priorities and aligning deliverables within available resources.

We require a C2 Strategic Lead that sits within the Directors Office. This role is ideally suited for someone with relevant experience working within a DG or Directorate office where they will have gained substantial experience in co-ordinating a range of strategic policy and business information to support the Director and the wider Directorate in fulfilling their duties. This will include an ability to handle policy and project information, manage policy and programme communications and framing policy and programme plans.

You will have an excellent understanding of governance and business co-ordination and be able to work confidently across the SG, Ministerial and wider public sector networks to aid information flow, unblock issues and ensure the priorities of the Directorate continue to be progressed.

To operate effectively you offer strategic thinking, strong organisational and communications skills and the ability to influence and negotiate at a senior level. In this high-impact role you will work alongside Deputy Directors across 5 divisions to provide strategic oversight, policy and planning insight, and connectivity across the Directorate and Senior Leadership Team. You will play a pivotal role in aligning priorities, enabling informed decision-making, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and collaboration.

Being flexible in your approach and comfortable working in new areas for short periods is required as undertaking short term projects across divisions or programmes to ensure delivery of key objectives is envisaged. It is therefore important you possess a broad range of business, project and planning experience and skills and a good understanding of core SG functions. You will actively display the values and behaviours set out in the Service of Scotland as you will lead the Strategy for the Directorate. You will be an active member of our Senior Leadership Team helping ensure that divisions are collegiate, priorities are collectively supported to meet the Directorates objectives, and that business and performance management are considered and prioritised at a Directorate level.

This post reports to the Director of Energy and Climate Change.

The Directors office is currently made up of 1 B3 and 2 B2s and also manages the EA support across the Directorate (currently 2 further B2s). As part of continuous improvement you are expected to work across boundaries supporting Deputy Directors to deliver and prioritise key objectives across the Directorate.


Responsibilities

Working closely with the Director, and in partnership with Deputy Directors and others, you will play a key role in ensuring that the strategic priorities for the Directorate are delivered. You will be responsible for:

  • Leading the Directorate's team of executive assistants, ensuring good information flow, smooth executive operations, strategic alignment of policy initiatives and supporting the Director to unblock issues and enable progress.

  • Acting as a key connector between the Director, senior leadership and wider government by supporting the Director and wider Senior Management Team in collective leadership of the Directorate.

  • Working in partnership with the head of DECC Operations (who leads on corporate responsibilities (e.g. workforce planning and management, finance, assurance, accountable officer activities, business planning, business continuity, and risk management)) to ensure that Directorate strategy is underpinned by data and tested for deliverability.

  • Developing a comprehensive understanding of Ministerial policy priorities, the strategic context and leadership and using this to inform Directorate strategy.

  • You will be central to co-ordinating Directorate Policy and Programme Planning and associated Reporting data and bringing together advice on a range of performance information to understand the overall progress of the Directorate in meeting its strategic priorities.

  • You will work with the Directorate and SLT to adjust the strategy and priorities for the Directorate as required, drawing on strategic, programme and policy information and horizon scanning to anticipate challenges, advising the Director on critical issues and enabling informed decision making.
  • Providing the Director and others with advice and support relating to strategic duties and responsibilities and providing cover at meetings where required.
  • Championing a positive, engaging working environment where Civil Service values are actively promoted and adhered to.
Success Profile
Success profiles are specific to each job and they include the mix of skills, experience and behaviours candidates will be assessed on, you should provide evidence of how you meet these in your statement.
Behaviours:
  • Communicating and Influencing – Level 4
  • Leadership – Level 4
  • Changing and Improving - Level 4

  • Working Together - Level 4

    You can find out more about Success Profiles on gov.scot.

Experience :

The successful candidate should have significant experience of creating strategy, managing programmes or complex projects and experience of planning and governance arrangements to ensure public sector interventions are driven by value for money, supported by appropriate governance and deliver intended outcomes.

In addition, applicants should demonstrate:

  • Excellent communication skills, with a proven ability to explain detailed and complex financial and strategic business planning information clearly and concisely, influencing key stakeholders and maintaining strong working relationships.

  • Excellent self motivation and an ability to identify and proactively resolve issues.

  • An ability to work at pace from time to time to address the Director or Ministers urgent issues.

  • Experience working across multidisciplinary teams and managing complex stakeholder environments.

  • Experience developing business cases, governance structures, benefits management approaches and policy delivery plans.

  • Experience working on complex agendas, projects or programmes that require cross-boundary collaboration.

  • Experience in handling a range of data, understand key trends and make it accessible for wider dissemination.

Working Pattern

The post is a full-time role, but staff with different working patterns are invited to apply, and we will assess proposed working patterns against the business requirements for this post.

Our standard hours are 35 hours per week and we offer a range of flexible working options depending on the needs of the role, including Flexi-leave. Scottish Government staff in hybrid-compatible roles should work in-person 40% of the time, either in an office or other agreed work location. If you have specific questions about the role you are applying for, please contact us.

Further Information

Further information about this opportunity is available from geraldine.russell@gov.scot.

How to Apply

Please submit a CV and an Expression of Interest (maximum 500 words) outlining your suitability for the role, relevant skills and experience, and what you would bring to the team. Please align this to how you meet the behaviours, experience and technical skills listed in the Success Profile above.

Vacancies close at 11:59pm on the date displayed in the table, unless otherwise stated on the job advert.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can be used to support your application, but all statements and examples provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, and presented as your own) applications will be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action.

Please see our candidate guidance for more information on acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI in recruitment.

If invited for further assessment, this will consist of a light touch interview.

Discussions are scheduled for w/c 26th October, however this may be subject to change


Recruitment Principles

As a government organisation, we adhere to the Civil Service Commission Recruitment Principles and we investigate any complaints received in relation to recruitment cases.

About us

The Scottish Government is the devolved government for Scotland. We have responsibility for a wide range of key policy areas including: education, health, the economy, justice, housing and transport. We offer rewarding careers and employ people across Scotland in a wide range of professions and roles.

Our staff are part of the UK Civil Service observing the Civil Service Codeand working for Ministers and senior stakeholders to deliver vital public services which improve the lives of the people of Scotland.

We offer a supportive and inclusive working environment along with a wide range of employee benefits. Find out more about what we offer.

As part of the UK Civil Service, we uphold the Civil Service Nationality Rules.

Equality statement

We are committed to equality and inclusion and we aim to recruit a diverse workforce that reflects the population of our nation.

Find out more about our commitment to diversity and how we offer and support recruitment adjustments for anyone who needs them.

Further information

Find out more about our organisation, what we offer staff members and how to apply on our Careers Website.

Read our Candidate Guide for further information on our recruitment and application processes.

title: Vendor Manager
description:
IRIS Networks is looking for a Vendor Manager to join our team and play a key role in supporting our commercial, sales, and operational objectives.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working across teams, building strong vendor relationships, negotiating commercially sound agreements, and helping turn complex telecommunications requirements into workable solutions for our customers.

The Vendor Manager will work closely with Sales, Operations, Finance, leadership, and our external vendor partners to source and manage third-party network services, support competitive customer solutions, maintain accurate vendor and contract information, and continuously improve the processes behind our quoting and vendor-management functions.


What You’ll Do

In this role, you will:

  • Partner with Sales to obtain, validate, and document vendor pricing and service options for transport, Internet, dark fiber, wavelength, colocation, wireless, and other off-net services.
  • Negotiate vendor pricing, service offerings, service-level commitments, and contract terms that support IRIS’s commercial and operational requirements.
  • Administer vendor agreements, amendments, exhibits, service orders, and related contract records.
  • Review vendor proposals, pricing, contracts, and other documentation for accuracy, completeness, commercial reasonableness, and alignment with company standards.
  • Maintain accurate contract information, including pricing, key terms, renewal and notice requirements, expiration dates, and vendor obligations.
  • Maintain Vendor Management information and tools within Salesforce/VISION, including products, service areas, pricing resources, PMT, contract records, and reports.
  • Monitor vendor performance, recurring service issues, SLA performance, and potential service-credit opportunities, coordinating escalations through resolution.
  • Maintain vendor contacts, escalation paths, operating procedures, and supporting documentation.
  • Partner with Sales and Operations to resolve vendor-related quoting, ordering, service, and escalation issues.
  • Identify opportunities to improve processes, data quality, automation, quoting speed, and overall operational efficiency.
  • Keep internal stakeholders and management informed regarding contracts, quotes, negotiations, and vendor escalations.

title: Sr. Program Manager
description:
Join Weiss-Aug – A Leader in Precision Manufacturing and Innovation


Be part of a company that’s shaping the future of manufacturing where your ideas, skills, and passion matter.


Weiss-Aug, is a leading provider of advanced manufacturing and engineering solutions with advanced facilities across the U.S. and Mexico for over 50 years.


Why Join Us?

At Weiss-Aug we are driven by a commitment to excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement. As a recognized leader in the industrial and commercial sectors, specializing in high-volume metal stamping, thermoplastic molding, and value-added assembly solutions for the medical, aerospace & defense, automotive, interconnect, telecommunications and consumer goods industries, we take pride in cultivating a collaborative and forward-thinking work environment.


We're currently seeking a passionate and skilled Sr. Program Manager to join our team and contribute to our mission of delivering high-quality, engineered solutions to our customers worldwide. In this role you will be responsible for representing the customer in order to ensure that the customer’s expectations are clearly understood and being met and must be capable of directing teams across all organizational areas (Design, Engineering, Tooling, Quality, Manufacturing, and Sales).


Responsibilities

  • Represent the customer in order to ensure that the customer’s expectations are clearly understood and being met.
  • Provide leadership to technical teams responsible for successful launch of multiple complex programs.
  • Responsible for overseeing the coordination and on-time/in-budget completion of all projects which may involve some or all of the following technologies: progressive stamping, insert molding, factory automation and other related tooling/processes. Oversee all aspects of programs beginning at customer order through to successful transfer to Manufacturing.
  • Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) including completion of related documentation, including but not limited to: DOE’s, FMEA’s, Process Flowcharts, Control Plans, Capability Studies, Gage R&R’s and PPAP.
  • Ability to participate in product design (R&D) meetings with customers in relationship with Weiss-Aug Manufacturing technologies.
  • Oversee the creation and distribution of project schedules. Ensure that project milestones and deadlines are met including assignment of responsibilities, monitor progress and report status to management/customer.
  • Facilitate Tooling Kickoff, Specification Review, Design Review and Lessons Learned (Post Mortem) Meetings.
  • Oversee the development and input of initial BOM and detailed Routing
  • Oversee the initiation and/or coordination of the change control process (ECO) relating to Engineering documentation.
  • Jointly responsible for successful transfer of tooling to Manufacturing along with Toolroom and Design Engineering functions.
  • Oversee the selection and management of key suppliers as required by project. Oversee the completion of requisitions for approval by management for purchased tooling or other product or services. Interface with outside suppliers to ensure they provide product or services on-time and to specifications.
  • Identify and facilitate new and/or special equipment needs along with Manufacturing Engineering.
  • Interface with customer on technical and schedule-related issues. Ensure program progress is communicated to customer at regular intervals.
  • Participate in customer, internal and registrar quality system audits.
  • Support Sales and New Product Development Teams. May assist in identifying potential leads and opportunities.

title: Specialist Sistem MDM
description:

  • Analizezi și aplici cerințele legislative în domeniul energiei electrice și al contorizării inteligente (ANRE, OMEPA, legislație națională, directive europene etc.)
  • Răspunzi pentru calitatea datelor livrate în procesul de facturare, în raportări și în răspunsurile la solicitările autorităților, precum și pentru definirea datelor de tip master data în MDM, care intervin în procesul de colectare și validare a datelor. Asiguri monitorizarea validării în masă a datelor de măsurare, precum și monitorizarea emiterii și închiderii comenzilor de citire pentru facturare și procesele de contractare
  • Asiguri analiza, monitorizarea și validarea estimărilor în MDM în cazul contoarelor indisponibile sau al problemelor de comunicație și monitorizezi comenzile de deconectare/reconectare la distanță
  • Analizezi și transmiți puncte de vedere privind reclamațiile către alte entități din cadrul companiei, rezolvi erori specifice de tarifare și gestionezi rapoarte specifice în MDM și SAP, în vederea analizării și monitorizării
  • Participi și răspunzi de realizarea programului de implementare și extindere a sistemelor de contorizare inteligentă, care presupune: definirea scopului și a graficului de desfășurare, stabilirea activităților de proiect și a riscurilor, raportarea, stabilirea acțiunilor preventive și corective, precum și elaborarea caietelor de sarcini necesare în cadrul procedurilor de achiziție publică

Realizezi și alte sarcini care decurg în mod natural din rolul tău, adaptate la cunoștințele și abilitățile tale

title: Cadet
description:
POSITION TITLE: Cadet


DEPARTMENT: Special Constable Service

RATE OF PAY: As per Schedule `A' of the Unifor 444 Collective Agreement

SHIFT: Rotating 12-hour shifts

The University of Windsor is situated on the traditional territory of the Three Fires Confederacy of First Nations: the Ojibwa, the Odawa, and the Potawatomie. We respect the longstanding relationships with First Nations people in this place in the 100-mile Windsor-Essex peninsula and the straits – les détroits – of Detroit.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY:
The University is seeking an energetic individual to work within a team of pro-active crime prevention, security, and community service-oriented officers.

ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS:
• Completed secondary school education or its equivalent and must be eligible for Special Constable status
• Related work experience as well as a working knowledge of the Criminal Code of Canada and pertinent Provincial and Federal legislation
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills
• Excellent interpersonal skills, particularly as they relate to the candidate’s ability to interact with a diverse student, staff, faculty, and community population.

APPLICANTS WILL BE REQUIRED TO POSSESS:
• Valid Ontario Driver’s License
• Valid Standard First Aid Certificate
• Valid C.P.R. Certificate (Basic Rescuer Level)
• Ability to pass a background check, medical examination, psychological examination and receive a police clearance report (including a Vulnerable Sector check)

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
• A University degree or post-secondary education in the field of law and security
• Ontario Police College education is also considered a valuable asset in application, as well as past work experience in security/police setting
• Knowledge of computers, record management systems and emergency radio systems
• Knowledge and experience working with First Nation communities and / or diverse multi-cultural groups is considered an asset

Since 1963, the University of Windsor has been a forward-looking community that comes together to study, to learn, to teach, and to serve. Our symbol is the bridge; our vista is cross-border; our commitment is local; and our impact is global. We are a dynamic, inclusive community of higher learning with roots going back more than 160 years and with a future full of promise.

In pursuit of the University's commitment to employment equity, members from the designated groups including women, Indigenous Peoples (First Nations, Métis, Inuit), racialized persons/visible minorities, persons with disabilities, and persons of a minority sexual orientation and/or gender identity are encouraged to apply and to self-identify.

If you need an accommodation for any part of the application and hiring process, please notify the Talent & Workforce Team (employment@uwindsor.ca). Should you require further information on accommodation, please visit the website of the Office of Human Rights, Conflict Resolution and Mediation (OHRCRM).

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.

We thank all applicants in advance for their interest in the University of Windsor, however, only those under consideration will be contacted. Applications submitted through employment agencies will not be considered.

title: Material Preparation & Delivery
description:
For over six decades, Sorenson Engineering in Yucaipa, California has been a global leader in microtechnology solutions for industries including Aerospace & Defense, RF Interconnect, Fiber Optics, Microwave Test, and Medical Devices.

We specialize in delivering ultra-precise micro components through cutting-edge precision machining, electroplating, value engineering, and advanced contact assembly. We are AS9100D and ISO9001:2015 certified and proudly hold Nadcap accreditations for specialized services including heat treatment and chemical processing.

At Sorenson Engineering, we thrive on solving complex challenges and advancing high-precision solutions that shape the future. As we approach 70 years of excellence, we’re looking for exceptional individuals ready to grow, innovate, and make an impact.

Be part of something extraordinary. Apply today.

Summary:
Receives, labels, stocks, pulls, tags, delivers and loads raw material (metal bars or coils) for production operations. Verifies material, quantities and records inventory. Ability to operate powered industrial machinery (i.e., forklifts) stay aware of possible hazards and follow all company safety procedures.

Prepare raw material for use in production areas which may include: receiving, labeling, stocking, pulling, tagging, verifying, cataloging, chamfering, and loading of raw material.

Level I:

Entry level position learning to follow procedures for preparing raw materials for delivery, handliing and delivering raw materials to production, and inventory control.
Level II:
Experienced level position for examining delivered goods and compares with records, such as delivery, bill of lading, receipts, purchase orders or packing slips to verify accuracy of incoming shipment. Records shipment data, such as quantity, weight, damages, or discrepancies for reporting purposes. Assist with training of new employees.
Essential Job Functions:
Demonstrate knowledge of raw material inventory, material lot numbers (heat numbers), material types, proper tagging procedures, and material handling requirements.
Verify incoming material shipments against purchase orders, bills of lading, packing slips, labels, tags, travelers, and inventory records.
Identify missing, lost, or damaged materials and promptly notify the supervisor.
Read and follow instructions to move materials to designated areas of the plant as directed.
Follow established inventory control, material movement, and documentation procedures.
Perform end-of-shift duties and maintain a clean and organized work area in accordance with housekeeping procedures.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
Ability to read, understand, and follow written and verbal instructions. Ability to work effectively in a team environment to identify and resolve work-related issues. Knowledge of basic shop math and ability to apply mathematical concepts to assigned tasks. Ability to communicate effectively in English, both verbally and in writing. Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately verify materials, quantities, and documentation. Ability to follow established procedures, organize work, and complete assigned tasks accurately and efficiently.
Education and Experience:
High school diploma or GED preferred. Previous experience in a manufacturing, warehouse, shipping, receiving, or material handling environment preferred but not required.
Physical Demands:
Must be able to occasionally exert push force up to 50 pounds, must have good eye sight, hearing and hand dexterity, and able to identify and distinguish colors.
Work Environment:
Work is performed primarily in a manufacturing and warehouse environment with exposure to moving machinery, noise, oils, solvents, fumes, and odors. The position may involve varying temperatures and frequent movement throughout the facility. Employees are required to follow established safety procedures and use appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) when necessary.

Work Environment

Within safety guidelines, there will be exposure to noise, moving mechanical parts, oils/solvents, fumes, and odors that may affect the eyes, ears, nose, throat and/or skin.

Compensation Disclosure:
In accordance with California law, the salary range for this position reflects a good faith estimate of the base compensation. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience and other factors permitted by law.

Equal Employment Opportunity:
EOE – Disability/Vet. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Background Checks & Drug Testing:
Background screenings and pre-employment drug tests may be conducted following a conditional offer of employment, where permitted by law.

California Applicant Privacy Notice:
If you are a California resident, personal information collected as part of your application will be processed in accordance with applicable California law.

You may have the right to request access to, correct, or delete your personal information, subject to certain exceptions.

To learn more, please review our Privacy Policy:

To submit a request, please contact us at privacy@sorensoneng.com or call 855-479-4241. We may require verification of your identity before processing your request.

title: Site Supervisor (San Diego)
description:
Reports To: Divisional Director of Early Childhood Education and Compliance

Department: Early Childhood Education

Classification: [Exempt/Non-Exempt]

Location: San Diego, C


Position Definition

Under the direct supervision of the Divisional Director of Early Childhood Education and Compliance, the Site Supervisor is responsible for the day-to-day leadership, administration, supervision, regulatory compliance, and overall operational effectiveness of an assigned Heartbeat Music & Performing Arts Academy (HBMPAA) early childhood education site. The Site Supervisor is accountable for maintaining a safe, nurturing, developmentally appropriate, and compliant educational environment for children from infancy through kindergarten. This position is responsible for ensuring that site operations consistently meet applicable requirements established by the California Department of Social Services, Community Care Licensing Division; California Department of Education (CDE) requirements applicable to funded programs; Title 5; Title 22; and all other applicable federal, state, local, licensing, funding, and HBMPAA requirements. The Site Supervisor provides direct leadership and oversight to Teachers, Teaching Assistants, Volunteers, Interns, and other assigned site personnel. This position is expected to maintain current knowledge of applicable regulatory requirements, identify and immediately address deficiencies, hold employees accountable for performance and conduct, and ensure corrective actions are implemented and sustained. The Site Supervisor also serves as a member of the enrollment team and supports enrollment, family engagement, program quality, and student success. When designated by leadership, the Site Supervisor serves as the primary on-site contact for Community Care Licensing representatives and participates in licensing visits, inspections, audits, and corrective-action activities.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

1. Site Leadership and Regulatory Compliance

  • Provide direct leadership and oversight of daily site operations and ensure the program operates in accordance with applicable Title 5, Title 22, licensing, funding, and HBMPAA requirements.
  • Maintain current working knowledge of laws, regulations, licensing standards, funding requirements, and organizational policies applicable to the assigned program and site.
  • Ensure required staff-to-child ratios and supervision requirements are maintained at all times.
  • Maintain a safe, sanitary, organized, nurturing, and developmentally appropriate environment for children, employees, families, and visitors.
  • Conduct routine site reviews and inspections to identify potential licensing, health, safety, operational, or program deficiencies.
  • Take immediate action when a compliance or safety concern is identified. The Site Supervisor is responsible for addressing the concern, communicating expectations, initiating corrective action, verifying completion, and monitoring the issue to ensure sustained compliance.
  • Ensure required licenses, notices, emergency information, postings, inspection records, and other regulatory documentation are current and properly maintained.
  • Maintain site readiness for announced and unannounced licensing, funding, health, safety, and organizational inspections or audits.
  • Immediately escalate serious licensing, child safety, health, employee conduct, or regulatory concerns to appropriate leadership.
  • Serve as an on-site representative during licensing visits and inspections when designated by leadership and ensure identified deficiencies are addressed within established deadlines.

2. Staff Supervision, Performance, and Accountability

  • Provide direct supervision, direction, coaching, and performance management for Teachers, Teaching Assistants, Volunteers, Interns, and other assigned site personnel.
  • Clearly communicate job expectations and ensure employees follow HBMPAA policies, classroom procedures, licensing requirements, safety standards, and leadership directives.
  • Monitor employee attendance, punctuality, reliability, conduct, classroom performance, supervision practices, and compliance with assigned responsibilities.
  • Address employee performance, attendance, conduct, safety, or compliance concerns promptly and consistently in coordination with Human Resources and appropriate leadership.
  • Hold employees accountable for failure to meet established performance, conduct, attendance, safety, or regulatory expectations.
  • Document coaching, performance concerns, attendance issues, policy violations, and other matters requiring formal follow-up in accordance with HBMPAA procedures.
  • Conduct employee performance evaluations at least every six months or as otherwise required by HBMPAA.
  • Evaluate employee performance using established measures, which may include:
    • Desired Results Developmental Profile (DRDP) outcomes;
    • Parent Satisfaction Survey results;
    • kindergarten readiness and student-development measures;
    • attendance, punctuality, and reliability;
    • documented callouts affecting classroom ratios, coverage, or operations;
    • classroom management and student engagement;
    • compliance with licensing and safety requirements;
    • completion and accuracy of required documentation; and
    • overall job performance and adherence to HBMPAA standards.
  • Identify training and development needs and provide or coordinate appropriate coaching, mentoring, and professional development.
  • Model professional conduct, accountability, effective communication, and appropriate interactions with children, families, employees, and visitors.

3. Child Supervision, Education, and Program Quality

  • Ensure children receive appropriate care, supervision, education, and developmental support throughout the program day.
  • Monitor classrooms and program areas regularly to ensure active supervision and compliance with established child-safety practices.
  • Intervene immediately when unsafe, inappropriate, or noncompliant practices are observed.
  • Ensure curriculum and instructional practices are developmentally appropriate and aligned with HBMPAA program objectives and applicable early childhood education standards.
  • Monitor completion and accuracy of student assessments, including DRDP documentation and other required developmental measures.
  • Ensure individualized learning goals are informed by assessments, observations, developmental needs, and family input.
  • Support Teachers in implementing appropriate classroom management and positive guidance strategies.
  • Monitor student progress and kindergarten readiness and implement improvement strategies when program outcomes do not meet established expectations.

4. Family and Community Engagement

  • Develop and maintain professional, respectful, and collaborative relationships with parents, guardians, families, and community partners.
  • Ensure families receive timely and appropriate communication regarding student progress, classroom activities, program expectations, incidents, and other relevant matters.
  • Conduct or oversee parent/guardian conferences regarding student development, progress, goals, behavioral concerns, and kindergarten readiness.
  • Respond professionally and promptly to parent/guardian questions, concerns, and complaints and escalate significant matters when appropriate.
  • Maintain confidentiality of student, family, and employee information in accordance with applicable laws and HBMPAA policies.
  • Participate in enrollment activities and support efforts to maintain appropriate program enrollment.

5. Health, Safety, and Emergency Preparedness

  • Ensure compliance with all applicable health, sanitation, child supervision, food safety, emergency preparedness, and injury-prevention requirements.
  • Ensure required daily child wellness and health observations are completed and documented as applicable.
  • Maintain emergency plans, emergency supplies, evacuation procedures, and required emergency documentation.
  • Ensure employees understand and follow emergency procedures and participate in required drills and safety training.
  • Immediately address and report suspected child abuse or neglect, injuries, safety hazards, licensing violations, or other serious incidents in accordance with mandated reporting obligations and HBMPAA procedures.
  • Ensure incidents involving children or employees are appropriately documented, reported, investigated, and escalated when required.

6. Administrative and Operational Management

  • Maintain complete, accurate, organized, and timely student, employee, attendance, licensing, enrollment, compliance, and program records.
  • Ensure required documentation is completed accurately and submitted within established deadlines.
  • Review site records routinely to identify missing, expired, inaccurate, or incomplete documentation and ensure deficiencies are corrected.
  • Utilize required daily, weekly, and monthly site compliance checklists and other monitoring tools established by HBMPAA.
  • Review emergency binders, employee and student files, licensing documentation, staff credentials, required postings, program records, and other assigned compliance materials.
  • Monitor classroom materials, instructional supplies, equipment, and other site resources and ensure responsible use of organizational funds and property.
  • Coordinate staffing and classroom coverage to maintain required ratios and minimize disruption to program operations.
  • Maintain consistent communication with the Divisional Director of Early Childhood Education and Compliance and other designated leadership regarding site performance, staffing, compliance, safety, and operational concerns.

7. Continuous Improvement and Accountability

  • Monitor program performance and implement corrective and continuous-improvement strategies when deficiencies or opportunities are identified.
  • Review assessment results, family feedback, attendance trends, classroom observations, compliance findings, and other program data to identify areas requiring improvement.
  • Develop and implement action plans when site or employee performance does not meet established standards.
  • Follow through on identified concerns until corrective actions have been completed and sustained.
  • Participate in organizational audits, compliance reviews, leadership meetings, professional development, and quality-improvement initiatives.
  • Perform other duties reasonably related to the position as assigned by HBMPAA leadership.

title: Leading Hand Wetlands Plantations and Farmland
description:
Live and work in a culture rich location minutes from the Murray River, just a short drive to one of Victoria’s best wine regions and with the ski fields so close you will be zooming down the mountains in under two hours.

Our employee benefits include professional development and flexible working conditions. Our conditions of employment support equal opportunities and an ethical, diverse, and inclusive workplace.

We also recognise and value your priorities beyond work. It’s important to us that you have a sustainable work–life balance, so we offer flexible working arrangements, a nine-day fortnight (full-time staff) and a range of leave options and support programs.

AlburyCity is committed to being a child safe organisation by creating cultures, adopting strategies and taking action to empower children. We work hard to keep them safe from harm because child safety is everyone’s responsibility.

DIRECTORATE:
Infrastructure, Planning & Environment

CLASSIFICATION:
Grade F

SALARY:
$85,633 to $99,334 pa + 12% employer contribution to superannuation

REPORTING TO:
Supervisor Wetlands, Plantations and Farming

EMPLOYMENT TYPE:
Permanent Full Time

THE POSITION:
The position plays a key role in supporting the management of Wonga Wetlands, Maryvale site, irrigated plantations and pump stations, wastewater farm assets and wastewater lagoons.

KEY RESPONSIBILITES:

• Coordinate and supervise staff, contractors and volunteers to ensure works are carried out to required standard.

• Routine property management and maintenance of the farmlands.

• Perform staff annual performance appraisals and skill assessments
• Management and maintenance of all fire trails, tracks and levee banks.
• Manage and control noxious weeds and feral animals.
• Operation and maintenance of the Waterview and Floodplain irrigation systems.
• Oversee and provide maintenance of agisted farmlands.
• Data collection and collation of Council's weather station and moisture meters located at Waterview and the wetlands.
• Perform dam compliance checks, and maintain records.
• Perform other tasks or duties as directed by the Supervisor which are within the limits of the employee's skill, competence and training.
• Observe requirements of the WHS Legislation, relevant to the job and adhere to AlburyCity Policies and Procedures regarding WHS.
• Observe appropriate AlburyCity Policies and Procedures regarding day to day operations including Equal Employment Opportunity policies, AlburyCity's Dress Code and Standards Policy and AlburyCity's Code of Conduct.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS:

Internal

  • Our People

External

  • Our Community
  • Contractors
  • Lessees
  • Statutory Authorities
  • Volunteers

EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS:

  • Based on a 38-hour week, with actual days and times being Monday to Friday, 7.00am to 4.00pm, with an RDO in accordance with AlburyCity’s RDO guidelines. These times may vary due to operational requirements and will be determined by the supervisor.
  • This position may involve work outside normal working hours. Additional hours over the standard 38 hours will attract a time in lieu arrangement or payment of overtime rates as agreed with your supervisor.
  • This position will be required to be on call outside normal working hours on occasions. This will be in agreement with the supervisor and will attract the appropriate allowance.
  • In line with the provisions of the Local Government (State)Award, this position will receive the Level 1, Adverse Working Conditions Allowance.
  • This position requires you to wear a compulsory uniform as per AlburyCity’s Our People Dress Code Standards. Our People are required to present a smart and professional image to the public at all times including when in public and when working remotely.
  • This position will be provided with vaccination against the following infectious diseases:
    ➢ Hepatitis A
    ➢ Hepatitis B
  • This position involves working in a predominantly outdoor environment where a varying range of temperatures, weather conditions and walking surfaces may be experienced. The position requires a moderate level of aerobic and physical fitness to undertake regular physical activities such as walking, lifting, pulling, pushing along with the capacity to maintain normal manual handling tasks across the work day – depending on the nature of the tasks undertaken. The use of relevant work method statements and appropriate WHS standards are an integral part of the role. A full functional and medical assessment is required for this position.
  • This position is subject to alcohol and other drug testing.
  • This position is subject to pre-employment and ongoing audiometric (hearing) assessment in accordance with AlburyCity Procedures.
  • This position is delegated with certain powers, authorities, duties and functions of Council underthe AlburyCity Delegations of Authority in accordance with section 378 of the Local Government Act.

  • Certificate in Plumbing, Irrigation or Horticultural discipline and/or extensive relevant industry experience

DESIRABLE CRITERIA:

  • First Aid Certificate

EXPERIENCE:

SPECIALIST KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS:

  • Extensive knowledge in the development/re-development of wetlands and eco-systems
  • Computer literacy proficiency in Microsoft Office applications
  • Knowledge of OH&S and risk management practices
  • Demonstrated knowledge, experience and skills in:
  • Horticulture including bush regeneration, plant identification, noxious plant control, spraying, tree/bush pruning and drainage
  • Irrigation systems, including installation, maintenance and operations
  • Pumps and pipeline system operations and maintenance
  • Civil engineering basics including roads and culvert construction, embankments, erosion control works, etc
  • Demonstrated knowledge and experience in the operation, inspection and management of water storage assets, including an understanding of regulatory compliance, risk management and dam safety requirements.
  • Property and fire control management
  • Understanding of animal habitat and conservation of the environment

title: CNC Technician
description:
Join Weiss-Aug – A Leader in Precision Manufacturing and Innovation

Be part of a company that’s shaping the future of manufacturing where your ideas, skills, and passion matter.


Weiss-Aug, is a leading provider of advanced manufacturing and engineering solutions with advanced facilities across the U.S. and Mexico for over 50 years.


Why Join Us?

At Weiss-Aug we are driven by a commitment to excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement. As a recognized leader in the industrial and commercial sectors, specializing in high-volume metal stamping, thermoplastic molding, and value-added assembly solutions for the medical, aerospace & defense, automotive, interconnect, telecommunications and consumer goods industries, we take pride in cultivating a collaborative and forward-thinking work environment.


We're currently seeking a passionate and skilled CNC Technician to join our team and contribute to our mission of delivering high-quality, engineered solutions to our customers worldwide. In this role you will be responsible for programming/operating 3-axis or higher CNC milling centers or similar equipment. Must be capable of programming cutting paths based off supplied CAD geometry, setting-up /fixturing work pieces in machines and efficiently operating /maintaining the equipment to produce progressive die components within a tolerance of +/- .0001” of expected dimensions.


Responsibilities:

  • Program cutting paths of CNC machining equipment utilizing Computer Assisted Machining (CAM) software and CAD geometry supplied by Engineering. Archive data as required for future use.
  • PCNC – Develop electrode geometry from solid models of work components.
  • Efficiently operate CNC machining equipment. Responsible for producing or accurately reproduced tool components within +/- .0001” of CAD geometry according to the published CNC work center schedule.
  • Assist in developing the CNC work center schedule.
  • Perform routine maintenance on CNC machining equipment as specified. Responsible for coordinating subcontracted service/repair work of CNC machining equipment and ancillary equipment whenever necessary. Responsible for maintaining proper tool condition/degree of sharpness to ensure operator safety and optimal cutting speeds.
  • Coordinate the purchase of CNC machining equipment spare parts and tooling. Responsible for maintaining an adequate stock of critical spare components and tools to ensure that equipment will remain operational in the case of failure of commonly replaced items.
  • Arrange and track the purchase of CNC machining center consumable products including cutting fluid /coolant, mill cutters, electrodes, etc.
  • Maintain an inventory of clamps/fixtures/vises to ensure proper work holding is achieved.
  • Assist in the design of fixtures, gages and other custom tooling or equipment as required.
  • Provide technical assistance to Engineering and Toolroom regarding CNC machining design and process issues throughout die design, die fabrication and grooming.
  • Instruct and mentor Toolroom apprentices.
  • Maintain integrity of W-A Design Engineering files/databases.
  • Ensure quality conformance checks of finished components is performed such as Point Cloud scans with reports in PCNC.
  • Other duties as assigned by WEDM/ PCNC Group Lead, Toolroom Managers or V.P. of Engineering.

description:
ABOUT YOU

The position requires a practical and motivated chemistry graduate who takes pride in accurate work, enjoys learning new techniques and can contribute positively within a busy laboratory team.

Previous industry experience is not essential. We're particularly interested in the scientific foundation and practical laboratory experience you've gained through your degree, together with examples of using initiative, organising your work and taking responsibility.

You'll join a close-knit team of experienced colleagues who work together to meet client deadlines. A full programme of role-based training will help you develop your technical knowledge and build a long-term career with Intertek.

Required skills and experience:

  • A degree in Chemistry or a closely related scientific discipline
  • A sound understanding of chemistry and broad awareness of analytical techniques gained through academic study or employment
  • Practical laboratory experience gained during your degree or through work; wet chemistry, titrations or gravimetric analysis would be beneficial
  • A proactive approach, with the confidence to use initiative and take responsibility for your work
  • Good planning and organisational skills, with the ability to manage priorities and work accurately to deadlines
  • Excellent attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, high-quality records and reports
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Computer literacy, including the ability to work with laboratory data and prepare clear written information
  • Knowledge of food contact regulations, EU or FDA methods, or ISO 17025 would be advantageous, but full training will be provided

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

As an Analyst in our Food Contact team, you'll carry out practical laboratory testing that helps customers demonstrate that packaging and other materials comply with UK, European and international food contact requirements.

The work is varied and spans two laboratories. You'll support migration testing, wet chemistry and chemical analysis across materials including plastics, metals, alloys and ceramics. You may also contribute to substance identification work for REACH, pharmacopoeial testing, spot tests and other analytical projects as required.

You'll begin with a comprehensive training programme based on your existing knowledge and experience. As your capability develops, you'll take on greater responsibility and may have the opportunity to join our Scientist Development Programme.

This permanent, full-time role is based at our Wilton site and offers an excellent platform to develop within an established global testing, inspection and certification organisation.

Key activities:

  • Prepare samples and carry out food contact compliance testing using established EU and FDA methods
  • Perform migration testing, wet chemistry and chemical analysis in accordance with approved procedures
  • Record and report results accurately in line with Intertek quality standards and ISO 17025 requirements
  • Provide the Delivery Manager, Regulatory team and Project Managers with timely updates on laboratory work
  • Prepare clear written reports within agreed timescales to meet customer requirements
  • Plan and organise practical laboratory activities across a varied and deadline-driven workload
  • Follow laboratory quality, health and safety procedures and contribute to a proactive safety culture
  • Work collaboratively with colleagues to meet client priorities and support the wider Food Contact service
  • Complete the required technical training and take an active approach to your ongoing development

WHAT WE OFFER

Join Intertek and become part of our global network of inspiring and entrepreneurial colleagues. We are a global family that values diversity and we thrive working together with precision, pace, and passion. We are working to make the world Ever Better, ensuring the quality, safety and sustainability of products and services used by millions of people around the world.

title: Research Intern - Next Generation Systems (3 months)
description:
At IBM Research, we are the innovation engine of IBM. Exploring what’s next in computing and shaping the technologies the world will rely on tomorrow. From advancing AI and hybrid cloud to pioneering practical quantum computing, we anticipate challenges and unlock new opportunities for clients, partners, and society. Working in Research means joining a team that accelerates discovery at the intersection of high-performance computing, AI, quantum, and cloud.   • PhD or Master's candidates in computer science, physics, applied mathematics, or related disciplines.
  • Experience in two or more of: quantum computing (e.g., Qiskit), mathematical optimization (e.g., MIP, QUBO), generative AI / LLM agents, and distributed cloud systems.

title: Instructional Designer II
description:
At Infoblox, every breakthrough begins with a bold “what if.”

What if your ideas could ignite global innovation?

What if your curiosity could redefine the future?

We invite you to step into the next exciting chapter of your career journey. Bring your creativity, drive, your daring spirit, and feel what it’s like to thrive on a team big enough to make an impact, yet small enough to make a difference. How we empower our people is extraordinary: we’re recognized as a Glassdoor Best Place to Work 2025, Great Place to Work-Certified in five countries, and honored by Cigna as a Healthy Workforce honors for three consecutive years; and what we build is world class: named CybersecAsia’s Best in Critical Infrastructure 2024 — clear evidence that when first-class technology meets empowered talent, remarkable careers take shape. So, what if the next big idea, and the next great career story, comes from you? Become the force that turns every “what if” into “what’s next.”

In a world where you can be anything, Be Infoblox.

Instructional Designer II

We have an opportunity for an Instructional Designer II to join our Education team in India- Remote, reporting to Kate O’Connor, Manager, Instructional Design. In this role, you will design and develop engaging technical learning experiences for Infoblox products, including eLearning, instructor-led materials, virtual learning, hands-on activities, job aids, and knowledge assessments. Collaborating closely with technical trainers, product management, engineering, technical marketing engineering, customer support, and subject matter experts, you will translate complex networking and cybersecurity concepts into clear, effective learning solutions for global audiences.

You will contribute to customer-facing technical education through the Infoblox Launchpad platform and help improve learning quality, accessibility, and scalability. You will also use approved AI-enabled tools responsibly to support research, content development, personalization, analytics, and workflow automation while applying human judgment to verify technical accuracy, security, accessibility, and instructional quality.

Be a Contributor — What You’ll Do

  • Design and develop technical learning solutions aligned with learning objectives, audience needs, product requirements, and adult learning principles
  • Apply instructional design models such as ADDIE and Bloom’s taxonomy to structure learning experiences, activities, assessments, and knowledge checks
  • Create and update eLearning modules, course outlines, workbooks, presentations, trainer notes, job aids, product documentation, and other learning assets using approved authoring and multimedia tools
  • Collaborate with technical trainers, product managers, engineers, technical marketing engineers, customer support, and subject matter experts to gather, validate, and organize source content
  • Translate complex networking, cybersecurity, and Infoblox product concepts into clear, engaging, and learner-centered content
  • Build practical scenarios, demonstrations, simulations, labs, and assessments that reinforce product understanding and knowledge retention
  • Coordinate assigned learning projects, including timelines, reviews, revisions, stakeholder communication, and delivery readiness
  • Evaluate learning effectiveness through learner feedback, assessment results, usage data, and available learning analytics; recommend improvements based on findings
  • Use approved AI-enabled tools to accelerate content discovery, draft and refine instructional copy, generate content variations, summarize feedback, and identify potential learning gaps
  • Review and fact-check AI-assisted outputs against authoritative product and technical sources; protect confidential information and follow Infoblox policies for responsible AI use

Be Prepared — What You Bring

  • 2–4 years of experience in instructional design, technical training, eLearning development, customer education, technical communication, or a related field
  • Bachelor’s degree in instructional design, education, learning and development, communications, technology, or a related discipline; a master’s degree is preferred
  • Experience designing and developing learning solutions for technical products, software, networking, cybersecurity, or other complex subject matter
  • Intermediate proficiency with eLearning development tools, learning management systems, presentation and multimedia tools, and project collaboration platforms
  • Working knowledge of instructional design models, adult learning principles, learning assessment, and learning analytics
  • Experience coordinating learning projects and managing multiple priorities, deadlines, reviews, and stakeholder expectations
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with technical subject matter experts and convert source material into accurate, accessible, and engaging content
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled productivity, content development, analytics, or automation tools, with the judgment to validate outputs and use them responsibly
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, attention to detail, curiosity, adaptability, and commitment to continuous improvement
  • Relevant instructional design or learning certifications, such as ATD, APTD, CPLP, or equivalent, are a plus; familiarity with networking, cybersecurity, DNS, DHCP, IPAM, or Infoblox products is also beneficial

Be Successful — Your Path

First 90 Days: Immerse in our culture, connect with mentors (Blox Buddies), and map the systems and meet with key stakeholders that rely on your work. Discuss and create short- and long-term goals.

Six Months:

  • Build strong working relationships with technical trainers, subject matter experts, product management, engineering, and other Education stakeholders
  • Contribute to at least three technical learning modules or significant content updates from analysis through review and delivery
  • Independently apply instructional design practices to create engaging activities, assessments, job aids, and eLearning content
  • Use approved AI-enabled tools to improve content development efficiency while documenting review steps and validating technical accuracy
  • Demonstrate working knowledge of relevant Infoblox products and the networking and cybersecurity concepts required for assigned learning projects
  • Use learner feedback, assessment results, and available analytics to recommend measurable improvements to assigned learning experiences

One Year:

  • Own the end-to-end design and development of multiple technical learning solutions for global audiences
  • Become a trusted instructional design partner for assigned product areas and contribute confidently in technical reviews with subject matter experts
  • Deliver learning assets that meet Education standards for accuracy, accessibility, usability, inclusivity, and learner engagement
  • Establish repeatable, responsible AI-supported workflows for content research, drafting, analysis, or automation while maintaining human oversight and data protection
  • Use learning analytics and stakeholder feedback to improve learner outcomes, content adoption, and the overall customer education experience
  • Contribute to scalable learning approaches, including modular content, blended learning, reusable assets, and localization-ready design

Belong — Your Community

Our culture thrives on inclusion, rewarding the bold ideas, curiosity, and creativity that move us forward. In a community where every voice counts, continuous learning is the norm. So, whether you code, create, sell, or care for customers, you’ll grow and belong here.

Be Rewarded — Benefits That Help You Grow, Thrive, Belong

  • Comprehensive health coverage, generous PTO, and flexible work options
  • Learning opportunities, career-mobility programs, and leadership workshops
  • Sixteen paid volunteer hours each year, global employee resource groups, and a “No Jerks” policy that keeps collaboration healthy
  • Modern offices with EV charging, healthy snacks, plus hackathons, game nights, and culture celebrations
  • Charitable Giving Program supported by Company Match
  • We practice pay transparency and reward performance. Offers reflect role location, internal equity, experience, skills, education, and certifications

Ready to Be the Difference?

Infoblox is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic information, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis.

title: Specialist Cleaning Operative
description:
Salary £26,606 - £26,847 per annum | Permanent, Full Time, 37 hours per week | FM Specialist Cleaning | Lancashire

Anyone applying for this post will be subject to Police Vetting, which requires a minimum of three years’ UK residency. A formal offer of employment cannot be issued until vetting has been successfully completed.

This post is required to work flexibly within 37 hours, to deliver a reactive and rapid response service to cover absences and cleaning incidents across Lancashire.

Key Accountabilities

  • Provide cleaning cover for cleaning roles in Lancashire Constabulary buildings, Care homes, and Lancashire County Council premises.
  • Provide biohazard cleaning at Lancashire County Council premises and Lancashire Constabulary premises and equipment.
  • Deliver a cleaning service in line with Health and Safety regulations ensuring adherence to the use of correct chemicals and equipment
  • To use specialist cleaning equipment for surfaces that require various cleaning methods, which include, professional grade heavy-duty floor scrubber dryers, industrial spray extraction carpet cleaners, and high-pressure steam or water systems to provide fast and hygienic results for commercial, industrial, internal and outdoor environments.
  • To ensure safe methods of working and taking responsibility for health and safety of yourselves and building users when on duty.
  • Provide county wide cover for cleaning in Police, Care, and corporate establishments
  • Deliver a cleaning service in line with regulations ensuring adherence to the use of correct chemicals and equipment and undertaking training for any specialist equipment used or surfaces that require various cleaning methods
  • Work to corporate risk assessments and safe methods of working, taking responsibility for health and safety of yourselves and premises users when on duty and for those that have key holding duties

Whilst in the main the duties will be between normal working hours, the specialist cleaning service is a 24 hours 7 days a week service, therefore there is a requirement to provide an element of 'on call' / standby duties, this is evenly shared between the team. An on-call standby allowance and any additional working hours are paid over and above the stipulated salary. During the interview the on-call duties will be explained in more detail.

You will be provided with a vehicle for use in connection with the duties of this post. We may consider you if you cannot drive because of a disability.

In return Lancashire County Council offers a range of benefits, which can be found on LCC Vacancies website.

We reserve the right to close down a vacancy early, before the closing date, if we receive sufficient applications.

The post you are applying for is covered by the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975 (as amended in 2013). If successful you will be required to apply to the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) for a 'disclosure'. Further information can be found on the 'Our Recruitment Process' tab.

Local Government Reorganisation

The Government has confirmed that local government across Lancashire will be reorganised, with the current 15 councils being replaced by four new unitary councils covering North, South, East and West Lancashire from April 2028.

If you are successful in your application, you will initially join Lancashire County Council. However, as part of the planned transition, your employment will transfer to one of the new unitary councils from April 2028, subject to the implementation of the reorganisation and relevant employment legislation.

Throughout this period, our focus remains on delivering excellent services to our communities. By joining us now, you'll play an important role in shaping the future of local government and helping to build a strong new organisation that will serve residents for years to come.

title: Chief Medical Officer
description:
Bronx Community Health Network

Job Description

Job Title: Chief Medical Officer

Schedule: Monday – Friday 9:00am – 5:30pm and some weekends as needed.

Supervisor: Chief Executive Officer

Department: Clinical Administration

Job Type: Full-Time (37.5 hours weekly)

FLSA: Exempt


Bronx Community Health Network is seeking an experienced physician executive to serve as Chief Medical Officer. This is a rare opportunity to shape clinical care for one of the most underserved communities in the country at a moment of significant organizational growth.


The Chief Medical Officer is the senior physician executive at BCHN, with primary responsibility for clinical quality, provider performance, productivity, and patient outcomes across all BCHN clinical services and sites.


About BCHN

Founded in 1996, Bronx Community Health Network is a not-for-profit, community-based organization and Federally Qualified Health Center. BCHN ensures that low-income and medically underserved residents of the Bronx have access to high-quality, comprehensive health care.


BCHN provides coordinated primary medical, oral, and mental health care along with diagnostic, pharmacy, social support, and enabling services. Our service area covers the entire borough of the Bronx and all 25 zip codes, with sites focused on low-income and underserved populations.


Our mission is to improve the health of people and families in the Bronx, provide access to affordable and quality health care, promote disease prevention and early treatment, and secure the resources that make this work possible.


Key Responsibilities:


Clinical Quality and Patient Safety

  • Maintain and advance the standard of care delivered to all BCHN patients.
  • Direct the quality assurance and quality improvement program as it relates to patient care.
  • Review and update standards of practice and clinical protocols.
  • Address clinical risk management matters and lead clinical incident review.
  • Review patient complaints and satisfaction data and direct responses where clinically indicated.
  • Lead the ongoing development and clinical optimization of the electronic health record.

Provider Leadership and Workforce

  • Lead recruitment, orientation, evaluation, and retention of clinicians and direct patient care providers
  • Oversee credentialing and privileging for all BCHN clinicians, including students and trainees
  • Establish performance standards and provide formal and informal feedback to providers
  • Recommend and participate in final determinations on clinical disciplinary action
  • Arrange clinical call coverage and approve clinical time off and continuing education requests
  • Plan in-service training and orientation for clinical staff
  • Build collaborative clinical teams and convene regular clinician meetings

Regulatory and Compliance

  • Oversee BCHN's medical policies and procedures, including scope of service under the Section 330 application and FTCA coverage
  • Maintain compliance with HRSA Health Center Program requirements, Article 28, HIPAA, OSHA, infection control, and patient privacy requirements
  • Support audit readiness, survey preparation, and clinical documentation standards
  • Provide clinical oversight of ancillary services including laboratory, radiology, and pharmacy
  • Contribute clinical data and analysis to UDS and other required reporting

Strategic and Organizational Leadership

  • Partner with the CEO, CFO, COO, and Executive Leadership Team to advance strategic, operational, and clinical goals
  • Participate in strategic planning and recommend clinical priorities and objectives
  • Present on clinical quality and improvement to the Board of Directors on a regular basis
  • Participate in development of the clinical budget and ongoing financial monitoring
  • Interpret clinical data for executive leadership and the Board
  • Support grant development and review clinical components of proposals and reports
  • Serve as clinical liaison to the local and state medical community, professional societies, health officials, and training institutions
  • Represent BCHN in public forums and in the community as appropriate
  • Support new site openings, mobile health operations, emergency preparedness, and special projects

Clinical Practice

  • Provide direct primary care to BCHN patients for a minimum of three days per week

Qualifications:


Required

  • MD or DO from an accredited medical school
  • Current, unrestricted license to practice medicine in New York State
  • Board certification in Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, Obstetrics and Gynecology, or a related primary care specialty
  • Current DEA controlled substance registration in good standing
  • Current BLS certification
  • Minimum of three years of clinical practice
  • Demonstrated experience in ambulatory clinical operations, quality improvement, and performance metrics
  • Experience leading and developing clinical teams

Preferred

  • Experience in a community health center or FQHC setting
  • Experience in health care administration in a community health environment
  • Familiarity with HRSA Health Center Program requirements, Article 28 licensure, and FTCA
  • Spanish language proficiency

Attributes

  • Demonstrated commitment to serving diverse and underserved communities
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to build consensus and lead through influence across clinical and administrative teams
  • Sound judgment under pressure and the ability to carry initiatives through to completion
  • Comfort with clinical information systems and data-driven decision making

Licensure, certification, and registration requirements are firm. Beyond those, we encourage candidates who meet most, though not all, of these qualifications to apply.


Compensation and Benefits


The base salary range for this position is $260,000 to $325,000 annually.


Total compensation for the selected finalist will be determined based on level of experience, education, accomplishments, internal equity, budget, and Fair Market Value evaluation. The range above is a good faith determination at the time of posting and may be modified in the future.


BCHN offers:

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Retirement savings plan
  • Paid time off and holidays
  • Continuing medical education allowance and time

How to Apply:
Submit a resume and a brief cover letter describing your interest in BCHN's mission through our career page at www.bchnhealth.org. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.


Important Notice Regarding Recruitment Fraud
BCHN has become aware of fraudulent recruitment activity by individuals or organizations falsely claiming to represent BCHN. BCHN never requests payment or fees from job applicants at any stage of the recruitment process. All legitimate openings are posted exclusively on our official career website at www.bchnhealth.org, and all email communication from our recruitment team comes only from addresses ending in bchnhealth.org. If you receive suspicious communication, do not engage or provide personal information, and report the incident to your local authorities.


Bronx Community Health Network is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion in all aspects of recruiting and employment. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration without regard to race, color, gender, gender identity or expression, sex, sexual orientation, transgender status, gender dysphoria, national origin, age, religion, disability, military and veteran status, marital or parental status, citizenship status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Summary:

The Industrial Engineering Specialist supports manufacturing efficiency, capacity, facility utilization, and production flow through the application of industrial engineering and continuous improvement principles. Working cross-functionally with Operations, Engineering, Quality, Finance, and other stakeholders, the Industrial Engineering Specialist leads defined improvement projects, supports facility and capital planning, coordinates with external contractors and suppliers, and provides data-driven recommendations to support operational decisions and future growth.

Facility Layout & Project Support

  • Develop and maintain facility layouts to support manufacturing operations, material flow, space utilization and future growth.

  • Coordinate with contractors and suppliers to support facility-related projects and services.

Process, Capacity & Continuous Improvement

  • Analyze manufacturing processes, capacity, flow and operational performance to identify constraints and improvement opportunities.
  • Develop capacity and resource recommendations to support current production requirements and future demand.
  • Apply industrial engineering and Lean principles to improve productivity, throughput, material flow, space utilization and process effectiveness.
  • Lead or design cross-functional improvement projects and support broader continuous improvement and 5S initiatives.

Operational & Capital Support

  • Provide analysis and recommendations to support capital planning, equipment requirements and operational decision-making.
  • Analyze operational performance measures, including OEE, capacity and equipment utilization, to identify constraints, trends and opportunities for improvement.
