title: Head of Community Empowerment and Governance Reform - C2
description:
This opportunity is only open to internal Scottish Government applicants who are currently 'Priority Movers'. Applications from individuals not currently on the Priority Mover list will be rejected and not considered.

The Community Empowerment and Governance Reform Unit brings together two critical areas of policy and programme delivery within the Public Service Reform Directorate. Its purpose is to lead the development and implementation of local governance and community empowerment policy, and associated delivery programmes. It leads effective collaboration and cross-government delivery of two significant Public Service Reform commitments: to empower communities and strengthen local democracy and to agree and implement bespoke governance arrangements for island communities.

The postholder will manage a diverse team and ambitious portfolio of work led by four C1 Leads, three B3 Policy Managers with B1 policy and administrative support; working across government, including in partnership with colleagues in Local Government and Health and Social Care Directorates and in close collaboration with wider directorates.

The role requires regular ministerial and senior official and external/public facing engagement, including building effective relationships with local authority, public sector and third sector partners. Over the next twelve months the focus will be on establishing and leading high profile implementation programmes, providing effective programme management and oversight; support to a matrix teams working across multiple DGs and portfolio areas and leading the development and delivery of effective policy design.

The postholder will

  • lead the development of the Democracy Matters/community empowerment policy workstream as part the cross-government programme of work to reform local governance arrangements.
  • lead the development and implementation of Single Authority Models, working closely with Local Governance and Health and Social Care reform programmes.
  • lead an experienced team responsible for developing and maintaining policy on existing community governance arrangements, including support for community councils, community development, including grant management and support for the community development sector, supporting participatory and deliberative democracy, including the National Participatory Budgeting Support Programme.

Responsibilities

  • Establishing a cross-government and cross-sector implementation programme for Democracy Matters, putting community empowerment and innovative new approaches to community-led decision-making at centre of design and delivery.
  • Leading engagement with SAMs geographies, including at senior officer level with Local Government and Health and develop a framework for model development which ensures alignment with national reform programmes whilst tailored to bespoke needs of island communities.
  • Undertaking and promoting research and evidence on innovative models for participatory democracy; community governance and community led decision-making.
  • Co-ordinating cross-government policy development including leading ‘virtual team’ comprised of health, social care, Local Government, island policy and wider policy areas.
  • Building strong effective relationships with external partners and stakeholders including local government; community development organisations; equalities groups; public sector partners to develop joint policy and implementation.
  • Managing relationship with COSLA to ensure partnership approach and handle sensitivities
  • Identifying and appraising options for sustainable community financing, funding for community development sector, and increasing community capacity.
  • Leading Community Councils policy, support and communications.
  • Working in partnership to redesign the National Participatory Budgeting Programme.
  • Grant management and identifying a sustainable funding approach for community development sector.

Working pattern

This role is a temporary position with an expected commitment of 12 months.

How to Apply

Applications for this position will only be accepted from substantive C2 employees.

Please submit a statement outlining your suitability for the role, relevant skills and experience, and what you would bring to the team (maximum 500 words).

Selection Process

All candidates will be invited to an informal discussion with the Hiring Manager.

Informal discussion dates tbc.

title: Receiving Associate
description:
Position Overview

The Receiving Associate is responsible for accurately receiving, inspecting, documenting, and staging incoming materials and components used in the manufacture of electrical distribution products and engineered power solutions. This role verifies shipments against purchase orders and packing documentation, identifies discrepancies or damage, completes required system transactions, and ensures material is properly labeled and routed to the appropriate storage or production location.

The Receiving Associate works closely with Supply Chain, Inventory, Quality, Production, and other departments to maintain material accuracy, support production schedules, and help ensure incoming materials are available when needed.


Typical Scope

  • Receive electrical components, fabricated parts, copper/busbar, enclosures, hardware, and other production materials.
  • Verify incoming shipments against purchase orders, packing slips, quantities, part numbers, and other receiving documentation.
  • Perform receiving transactions and maintain accurate material records within the ERP/MRP system.
  • Identify damaged, incorrect, short, or excess shipments and communicate discrepancies promptly.
  • Label, organize, stage, and route received material to inventory, Quality, Production, or designated project locations.

Key Responsibilities

1. Receiving & Material Verification

  • Unload and receive incoming deliveries in a safe and organized manner.
  • Compare shipments to purchase orders, packing slips, and other documentation to confirm part numbers, descriptions, quantities, and condition.
  • Inspect packaging and material for visible damage, shortages, overages, or other discrepancies.
  • Document and communicate receiving issues to Supply Chain, Purchasing, Quality, or other appropriate personnel.
  • Ensure required receiving paperwork and documentation are complete and accurate.

2. System Transactions & Inventory Accuracy

  • Complete receiving transactions accurately and timely within the company's ERP/MRP system.
  • Apply required labels, identification, project information, or inventory markings to received material.
  • Maintain accurate records of receipts, discrepancies, returns, and supporting documentation.
  • Assist with inventory accuracy activities, cycle counts, material location verification, and reconciliation as needed.
  • Follow established material control and traceability requirements.

3. Material Handling & Staging

  • Safely move, organize, and stage materials using appropriate material-handling equipment.
  • Route material to designated warehouse locations, Quality inspection areas, production staging areas, or project-specific locations.
  • Maintain clean, organized, and clearly identified receiving and staging areas.
  • Support proper storage and handling practices to prevent material damage or loss.
  • Coordinate priority receipts and urgent material needs with Supply Chain and Production.

4. Quality & Discrepancy Support

  • Identify incoming materials requiring Quality inspection or additional verification and route them appropriately.
  • Support the documentation and segregation of damaged, nonconforming, or questionable material.
  • Assist with supplier returns, replacement shipments, and material discrepancy resolution as directed.
  • Escalate recurring or significant receiving issues to the appropriate team members.

5. Cross-Functional & Operational Support

  • Work closely with Supply Chain, Purchasing, Quality, Production, Engineering, and Inventory/Warehouse personnel.
  • Communicate material availability, receiving delays, and discrepancies that may affect production schedules or customer commitments.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives related to receiving, material flow, inventory accuracy, safety, and workplace organization.
  • Follow company safety procedures and required material-handling practices.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Previous receiving, warehouse, inventory, shipping, material handling, or manufacturing experience preferred.
  • Ability to accurately compare part numbers, quantities, purchase orders, packing slips, and other documentation.
  • Basic computer skills and ability to learn ERP/MRP and inventory systems.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently while coordinating effectively with multiple departments.
  • Ability to manage changing priorities and maintain accuracy in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience in an electrical equipment, industrial, engineered-to-order, or other manufacturing environment.
  • Experience receiving electrical components, fabricated parts, copper, enclosures, hardware, or similar production materials.
  • Previous experience with ERP/MRP systems, barcode scanning, inventory transactions, or material traceability.
  • Forklift, pallet jack, or other material-handling equipment experience.

Physical Requirements

  • Frequently stand and walk throughout receiving, warehouse, and manufacturing environments.
  • Regularly bend, reach, push, pull, and handle materials throughout the workday.
  • Regularly lift and carry up to 50 pounds, with assistance or material-handling equipment used for heavier items.
  • Operate or work around forklifts, pallet jacks, carts, and other material-handling equipment as trained and authorized.
  • Wear required personal protective equipment (PPE).

Role Success

Success in this role is demonstrated through accurate and timely receiving, strong inventory and documentation accuracy, proper material handling, effective communication of discrepancies, safe work practices, and reliable support of production and material flow.

title: National/International Legal Consultant – MIDAS Legal Assessment
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Project Context and Scope

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is supporting the Government of the Kingdom of Lesotho in the modernization of border and migration management systems through the deployment of the Migration Information and Data Analysis System (MIDAS). MIDAS is IOM's flagship Border Management Information System (BMIS), designed to facilitate the electronic collection, storage, processing, sharing, and analysis of traveller information at border crossing points.

The MIDAS deployment project in Lesotho aims to strengthen border governance, improve migration management, enhance national security, facilitate legitimate cross-border movement, and strengthen the generation and analysis of migration data for evidence-based decision-making. The project includes technical and legal assessments as foundational requirements to guide the implementation, configuration, and long-term sustainability of the system. The project documentation specifically foresees a legal assessment to review legislative and regulatory frameworks relevant to border management, migration governance, automated border control procedures, data protection, and data privacy.

The Kingdom of Lesotho has established a legal framework for the protection of personal information through the Data Protection Act, 2011 (Act No. 5 of 2012), which regulates the processing of personal information, establishes principles for lawful processing, provides safeguards for sensitive personal information, and contains provisions regarding data security, data subject rights, and cross-border transfers of personal data.

As the deployment and operation of MIDAS will involve the collection, processing, storage, use and sharing of personal and biometric data obtained through relevant immigration and border control procedures, the implementation of the system must be assessed against the Data Protection Act, relevant constitutional protections relating to privacy and fundamental rights, and applicable legislation governing immigration, border management, national security, information management, and the relevant powers and functions of competent border authorities.

Furthermore, MIDAS may facilitate interoperability and information exchange between government systems and, where authorised, with regional or international partners. A comprehensive review of the legal, regulatory, institutional, and policy environment is therefore required to determine whether existing legislation adequately supports the collection, processing, retention, sharing, and protection of traveller information and biometric data and to identify any legal, regulatory or operational gaps that could affect implementation, in compliance with national legislation, international obligations, human rights standards, and recognised principles of data protection and privacy.

Particular attention shall be given to legal provisions governing data sharing, cross-border transfers of personal information, the processing of sensitive personal information and biometric data, and safeguards necessary to ensure compliance with applicable data protection requirements.

IOM therefore seeks the services of a qualified legal expert to undertake a comprehensive legal assessment to inform the development and strengthening of the legal and institutional framework governing border management data in Lesotho, including recommendations and a roadmap for its implementation.

Objective of the Consultancy

The overall objective of the consultancy is to conduct a comprehensive legal assessment of the legislative, regulatory, policy, and institutional framework governing border and migration management, personal data protection and privacy, biometric data processing, information management and information-sharing arrangements, and interoperability between government information systems in Lesotho, in order to determine the legal basis for the deployment and operation of MIDAS in Lesotho.

The assessment shall examine the extent to which existing national legislation, including the Data Protection Act, 2011 (Act No. 5 of 2012) and applicable immigration and border management legislation, supports the lawful collection, processing, retention, sharing, and protection of personal and biometric data within MIDAS.

The assessment shall further evaluate compliance with applicable regional and international obligations, international human rights standards, and internationally recognized data protection principles, and provide practical recommendations to address identified legal, institutional, operational, and policy gaps necessary for the sustainable implementation and operation of MIDAS in Lesotho.

Specific Objectives

The consultant shall:

  1. Review the legal and institutional framework governing border management and migration governance in Lesotho.

  2. Assess the adequacy of the legal basis for the collection, processing, storage, retention, transmission, sharing, protection and lawful use of personal and biometric data for border management purposes, including in the context of MIDAS.

  3. Evaluate the alignment of the national framework with applicable constitutional protections, international human rights obligations, regional commitments and international data protection principles.

  4. Assess the legal, regulatory and institutional arrangements governing interoperability and information-sharing between relevant national systems and institutions.

  5. Identify legal, regulatory, policy, and institutional gaps that may affect the effective governance of border management data and the sustainable deployment of MIDAS.

  6. Develop recommendations and a roadmap to strengthen the legal, regulatory and institutional framework governing border management data, including measures required to support the sustainable deployment and operation of MIDAS.

    Scope of Work

The consultant shall conduct a legal and institutional assessment of the national framework governing border management data in Lesotho. The assessment shall focus on the collection, processing, storage, retention, sharing, protection, transfer and governance of border management data, including personal and biometric data, and shall identify gaps and recommendations necessary to strengthen the national framework in line with national legislation and applicable regional and international standards.

The consultant shall include the following components:

  1. Review of the Legal and Regulatory Framework

Conduct a detailed review of relevant constitutional, legislative, regulatory, and policy instruments governing border management, migration management, identity management, data protection, privacy, information management, cybersecurity, and related areas.

The review shall assess the extent to which the existing framework provides an adequate legal basis for the collection, processing, storage, retention, sharing, protection and lawful use of border management data by competent authorities.

The review shall also examine the legal mandates and powers of competent authorities involved in border management, migration governance, identity management, law enforcement, and national security, insofar as these relate to the collection, access, use, and sharing of border management data.

This includes, but is not limited to, the Immigration Act and Regulations, passport and citizenship legislation, and refugee and asylum legislation. Human trafficking and transnational organised crime legislation, Border management policies, strategies and operational frameworks, National migration policies and strategies, Civil registration framework, National identity management framework, Population registry systems, Foundational identification systems, constitutional privacy protections, Data protection laws and regulations, ICT legislation, Cybersecurity frameworks, Evidence and electronic transactions legislation.

  1. Stakeholder Consultations

Undertake consultations with relevant governmental and non-governmental stakeholders involved in border management, migration governance, identity management, data protection, information and communications technology, law enforcement and national security.

This may include, as appropriate, the following actors: Ministry of Home Affairs and Police; Department of Immigration Services; Ministry of Justice; national ICT authorities; National Identity Management Agencies; Civil Registration Authorities; Lesotho Mounted Police Service; National security stakeholders: border agencies operating at Points of Entry, development partners, and technical stakeholders.

The consultations shall seek to map institutional mandates and responsibilities, identify existing practices relating to border management data governance, assess institutional coordination and oversight mechanisms, identify challenges, gaps, and priority needs, and validate preliminary findings and recommendations.

  1. Assessment of Institutional Arrangements and Data Governance Frameworks

Examine the mandates, functions and responsibilities of institutions involved in the collection, management, sharing, protection and oversight of border management data.

The assessment shall analyse:

  • institutional roles and responsibilities;

  • coordination and accountability mechanisms;

  • data governance and oversight arrangements;

  • safeguards governing access to, use, disclosure and sharing of border management data;

  • institutional capacities and challenges affecting effective data governance.

  1. Assessment of Information sharing, interoperability and cross-border data exchange

Assess the legal, regulatory and institutional arrangements governing the exchange of border management data within and between competent national authorities and with external partners. This may include legal provisions governing data exchange between immigration systems, national ID systems, passports systems, civil registration systems, law enforcement systems, and international systems (e.g. INTERPOL).

Particular attention shall be given to:

  • inter-agency information sharing mechanisms;

  • interoperability between border management, identity management, civil registration and law enforcement systems;

  • legal safeguards governing data exchange;

  • cross-border sharing of personal and biometric data;

  • applicable requirements, limitations and safeguards relating to international data transfers.

  1. Assessment of Data Protection and Privacy Safeguards

Assess the adequacy of existing legal and institutional safeguards relating to the protection of personal and biometric data processed for border management purposes.

The assessment shall consider:

  • lawfulness of processing;

  • data protection principles;

  • processing of sensitive personal information and biometric data;

  • purpose limitation and data minimization requirements;

  • rights of data subjects;

  • retention and disposal requirements;

  • security and confidentiality safeguards;

  • oversight and accountability mechanisms;

  • remedies and redress mechanisms.

  1. Analysis against Regional and International Instruments

Assess the alignment of the national framework with applicable regional, continental and international obligations, standards and good practices, including where relevant:

  • ICAO standards and recommended practices

  • African Union legal instruments relating to migration and border governance

  • The SADC Model Law on Data Protection and relevant regional data protection frameworks

  • Relevant SADC protocols and regional cooperation frameworks related to migration, border management and information sharing

  • Relevant International human rights instruments

  • Refugee and migration-related conventions ratified by Lesotho

  • Internationally recognized principles and standards relating to privacy, data protection and biometric data processing

  1. Gap Analysis and Recommendations

Identify legal, regulatory, institutional and operational gaps affecting effective border management data governance and provide recommendations to strengthen the national framework.

Recommendations should include:

  • legislative and regulatory reforms;

  • institutional strengthening measures;

  • governance and accountability mechanisms;

  • information-sharing and interoperability arrangements;

  • data protection and privacy safeguards;

  • standard operating procedures and cooperation frameworks;

  • priority implementation actions.

The recommendations shall include a roadmap for the implementation of the recommendations, including immediate actions, medium--term legal, policy, and operational reforms, long-term legislative and institutional strengthening measures, as well as a draft framework for data-sharing agreements and institutional protocols.

The assessment is not intended to constitute a technical, operational, cybersecurity or compliance audit of any specific border management information system. Any reference to existing or planned information systems, including MIDAS, shall be made solely for the purpose of assessing the broader legal, regulatory and institutional framework governing border management data. The assessment shall focus on the national framework for border management data governance rather than on the performance or compliance of any particular system.

title: Sr Design Quality Assurance Engineer
description:
Job Summary:

The Sr. Design Assurance Engineer owns design quality for Forgent's Solutions product lines: find recurring design errors, drive root cause and corrective action, and catch defects before they reach manufacturing.


The role also owns the two governance forums where design issues and changes are dispositioned: the Corrective Action Review Board (CARB) and the engineering change control (ECC) process, including the Change Control Board (CCB).


Key Responsibilities:

Corrective Action Review Board

  • Run the CARB for design issues: set agenda and cadence, present incoming issues, and secure an owner, containment action, and due date for every accepted item.
  • Perform root cause analysis on design defects, non-conformances, and field issues, and drive corrective actions that prevent recurrence rather than fix one job.
  • Own closure: track actions against due dates, escalate stalled items, verify effectiveness with evidence, and close only once the fix is embedded in a standard, checklist, template, or tool.

Engineering Change Control and Change Control Board

  • Manage the ECC process end to end: intake, review, disposition, implementation, verification, and closure, with clear rules for what requires board review.
  • Run the CCB: convene on a fixed cadence, prepare change packages, drive each to a documented disposition, and hold owners to committed implementation dates.
  • Confirm approved changes land in every affected document and system (drawings, schematics, models, BOMs, PLM/PDM), and enforce change record data quality.

Design Reviews and Issue Closure

  • Attend cross functional design reviews as the design quality voice and support the peer and team lead tiers, bringing known failure modes and open corrective actions into each.
  • Ensure design review effectiveness and adherence to the process.
  • Publish review effectiveness as a red/green indicator by review type, project, and site. Own the design quality metrics: design accuracy by engineer and by project, issue closure rate, and escape rate into manufacturing.

Analysis, Pareto, and Prevention

  • Quantify the cost, rework, and schedule impact of design driven engineering changes.
  • Prioritize root cause analysis on the design issues that disrupt manufacturing flow.
  • Classify root causes as process, person, or tool, and aim the countermeasure accordingly.
  • Maintain Pareto and trend analysis by product line, site, discipline, root cause, and change cycle time, and drive top contributors to permanent resolution through CARB.
  • Improve design standards, checklists, and training to stop design issues from recurring.

Reporting and Communication

  • Share ECC and design change analysis with engineering on a regular cadence: top failure modes and the actions addressing them.
  • Report performance to engineering and Quality leadership: CARB and CCB throughput, open and overdue actions, change volume and cycle time, and top Pareto items with countermeasure progress.

Cross Site and Compliance Support

  • Partner with the Engineering Managers to drive open design quality actions to closure.
  • Standardize design quality practices, corrective action handling, and change control across Solutions sites (Hanover, Champlin, Dayton).
  • Verify that UL listing and labeling escapes (UL 891 / UL 1558) are addressed at the design stage.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • 5+ years in design engineering or quality engineering within electrical equipment, switchgear/switchboard, or panel manufacturing.
  • Problem solving and root cause analysis (8D, A3, DMAIC) and CAPA experience.
  • Experience owning an engineering change control process (ECO/ECN) and facilitating a cross functional board (CCB, CARB, or MRB).
  • Able to turn quality and change data into Pareto, trend, and cost of poor quality analysis, and translate findings into process or standard changes. Strong Excel required; Power BI or Smartsheet a plus.
  • Working knowledge of low voltage switchboard/switchgear design and UL 891 / UL 1558 requirements.

title: Tool and Die Maker
description:
Summary:

Sets up and operates conventional and CNC machines. Performs the layout and fabrication of tools, dies, special machines, machine modifications, and K-Fast tooling. Develop new products using exotic and composite materials while meeting established quality standards. Has moderate control to make process adjustments after tasks are assigned.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Tooling Fabrication: Determines the layout, fabrication, and assembly of complex tools, dies, special machines, machine modifications, fixtures, and K-Fast tooling using prints, drawings, sketches, and verbal instructions.
  • Machine Setup & Operation: Sets up and operates conventional and CNC lathes, mills, grinders, honing machines, center laps, and other specialized equipment.
  • Precision Machining: Performs complex machining operations to produce tooling and components to exact dimensional and tolerance requirements.
  • Tooling Layout & Development: Performs detailed layouts for tooling and components and develops sketches for tooling designs, part development, and progressions.
  • Specialized Materials & Processes: Works with exotic and composite materials and applies specialized processes, including EDM, grinding, jig boring, welding, and heat treatment, as required.

  • Design & Process Improvement: Recommends tooling design revisions, material substitutions, and alternative fabrication methods. Constructs temporary tooling for short production runs as required.
  • Inspection & Quality Control: Uses precision measuring instruments and inspection equipment to verify tooling and components meet dimensional and quality requirements.
  • Training & Knowledge Sharing: Trains and provides guidance to Tool & Die apprentices and employees with less experience or skill.
  • Equipment Maintenance: Performs routine maintenance on machines and equipment, including changing grinding wheels.
  • Material Handling: Safely lifts and transports materials, tooling, and parts weighing up to 30 pounds.
  • Safety & Housekeeping: Maintains a clean, safe, and organized work area and equipment while following all applicable safety procedures.
  • Other Duties: Performs other duties of equal or lesser skill as assigned.

Benefits/Salary:

The position includes competitive wages and a comprehensive benefits package available day one of hire, including health insurance (medical, dental, vision), excellent 401k matching program, paid holidays and vacation. Howmet Aerospace curates a strong working environment through opportunities for career progression, community engagement activities, and flexible schedules contingent upon role and location. The salary range for this position ___$24.70____ - ___$41.99____.

Education, Experience, and Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or GED preferred.
  • 5-7 years of experience in a tool room environment or equivalent previous experience with a fastener manufacturing company. Ability to trouble-shoot and solve problems of the most advanced level. Must possess a working knowledge of ferrous and non-ferrous metals and their alloys.
  • Advanced troubleshooting and problem-solving skills with a working knowledge of ferrous and non-ferrous metals.
  • Ability to read and interpret blueprints, technical documents, safety procedures, and work instructions.
  • Proficient in basic math, precision measurements, and completing production documentation.
  • Effective verbal communication and computer skills, including experience with Syteline Manufacturing software preferred.

  • Employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

title: Production Specialist
description:
Workplace: St. Helier, Jersey (This is an office-based role unsuitable for hybrid working).

Production Specialist

ITV News Channel Television

The role

ITV News Channel TV are looking for a talented Production Specialist.

As a Production Specialist, you will work as part of a multi-skilled team providing technical, craft, operational and administrative skills across all areas of the news service, primarily based at our newsroom and studio in Jersey.

To be eligible for this role, candidates will ideally be multi-skilled and familiar with craft editing or live studio operations. Proven skills in, or knowledge of areas including editing, programme timing, vision, sound, directing, media ingest and transfer, production administration or scheduling is an advantage.

You must be willing, and have the aptitude, to develop new skills (with appropriate training) and to move between different duties daily as the needs of a busy and vibrant news operation require. You’ll also be required to share your own skills with others.

As a Production Specialist, you will be a highly motivated individual as well as friendly and approachable. You will be committed to working as part of a successful team, sharing the responsibility for supporting news production. Above all, you will be an excellent communicator who is quick-thinking and calm under pressure, with strong and decisive decision-making skills.

If you have a passion for News and Technology and are looking to expand on your current skills and experience, this could be the perfect role for you.

Everyone in the Production Team will have a core skill in one or more of the following areas on appointment but will increase their skills over time:

  • Live studio and location operations, including Directing, Vision mixing, Sound, Gallery PA-ing, Autocue, Newsroom and Studio Cameras and Floor Management
  • Media Ingest & Transfer, Playout, Ingest
  • Production Technology Support assistance
  • Scripts, Scheduling, Rosters, Logging, Clearance and Returns and other Programme administration and support
  • ITVX/Digital support
  • Editing and templated Graphics
  • Studio systems technical operation, first-line fault finding and maintenance and issue reporting
  • Server management and Media storage

Please note, the rostered hours for this role will include weekend working , late shifts as well as early morning shifts and Bank Holidays. The working pattern will incorporate late shifts (typically 23:00 finish) as well as early morning (typically 05:00 start). You are expected to provide your own means of transportation to and from your main workplace.

Because of the nature of news production, there will be occasions when you are required to work long and unsociable hours at short notice.

Skills you’ll need (minimum criteria)

  • You must have a core skill in one or more of the following areas: Editing, Sound, Directing, Programme Timing, Vision, Media Ingest & Transfer, Production Technology Support
  • The ability to multi-skill and shift seamlessly from one task to another if necessary, often under pressure, is key
  • The ability to be proactive
  • Experience of working effectively as part of a team
  • Confident and clear communication skills
  • Proven ability to learn and apply new skills

Other things we’re looking for (key criteria)

  • Proactivity, drive and resilience
  • A positive attitude to work
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Social Media/Digital awareness
  • Candidates should demonstrate passion, enthusiasm, a knowledge of the business, an understanding of technology, and an awareness of production methods
  • Candidates should be informed about the news agenda both nationally and for the region/nation.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion is at the heart of what we do at ITV Channel, and we want to ensure we reflect our audience both on screen and in our workforce. ITV is for Everyone, and we encourage applications from Deaf, Disabled and Neurodivergent people and People of Colour to apply for this role.

Newsrooms are busy and pressurised environments, involving live news production, which often requires colleagues to make quick decisions under pressure. We also need people who are able to use their initiative.

We need to test these abilities at the interview stage to understand how candidates will react when operating in a pressurised environment. This is a fundamental requirement of the role. We will always consider any request for reasonable adjustments as part of the interview process, for example, sharing key themes when that is requested in connection with a neurodivergent condition, whilst still ensuring that we can test a candidate's ability to operate in the specific environment of a newsroom.

Closing date: Tuesday 3rd November 2026

Please note the notice period for this role is 2 months (this will include any new contracts/ secondments)

title: Additive Manufacturing (AM) Technician
description:
About Us:

Burloak Technologies is a leader in the additive manufacturing industry, providing engineering services for additive manufacturing, materials development, high-precision CNC machining and metrology. Burloak Technologies works with innovative companies across the aerospace, defense, nuclear and industrial markets to rapidly transition their most challenging part designs to additive manufacturing at scale.


Location:

3280 South Service Road, Oakville, Ontario, CA L6L 0B1, On-site Position


Summary:

The Additive Manufacturing (AM) Technician is a hands-on production role responsible for operating, monitoring, and maintaining advanced additive manufacturing equipment to produce high-quality parts for aerospace and other high-precision industries. This position supports all aspects of the additive manufacturing process, including machine setup, build preparation, powder handling, preventive maintenance, in-process inspection, and production documentation while ensuring compliance with AS9100 quality standards and workplace safety requirements.


Working closely with manufacturing, engineering, and quality teams, the AM Technician plays a key role in maximizing equipment uptime, troubleshooting production issues, maintaining process discipline, and supporting continuous improvement initiatives. The successful candidate is a safety-focused, mechanically inclined individual who thrives in a fast-paced manufacturing environment and is committed to delivering high-quality results.


Key Responsibilities:

Additive Manufacturing Operations

  • Operate, monitor, and maintain additive manufacturing systems, including LPBF, E-Beam, SLS, and FDM equipment, to produce high-quality parts and meet production schedules.
  • Prepare builds by reviewing files, configuring build layouts, setting up equipment, and verifying process parameters.
  • Monitor active builds, identify process deviations or equipment issues, and take appropriate corrective action or escalate as required.
  • Perform powder handling activities, including loading, sieving, recovery, and storage, in accordance with established procedures and safety requirements.
  • Support daily production activities while collaborating with manufacturing, engineering, and quality teams to achieve operational objectives.

Equipment Maintenance & Process Support

  • Perform routine and preventive maintenance on additive manufacturing equipment and related systems to maximize uptime.
  • Troubleshoot equipment and process issues, documenting observations and supporting root cause investigations and corrective actions.
  • Maintain equipment cleanliness, consumable inventories, and overall machine readiness in accordance with manufacturer recommendations and internal procedures.

Quality & Documentation

  • Follow AS9100 quality requirements, work instructions, and standard operating procedures throughout the manufacturing process.
  • Complete production documentation, including build records, maintenance logs, and inspection records, accurately and on time.
  • Use precision measuring instruments such as calipers and micrometers to perform in-process and post-build inspections.
  • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives that enhance safety, quality, efficiency, and equipment reliability.

Safety & Teamwork

  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment while complying with all health, safety, PPE, and powder handling requirements.
  • Communicate effectively with team members during shift handovers and daily production activities to ensure operational continuity.
  • Support a positive team environment by demonstrating accountability, professionalism, and a commitment to quality and safety.
  • Perform other duties as assigned that are consistent with the responsibilities of the role.

title: Site Supervisor (Escondido)
description:
Reports To: Divisional Director of Early Childhood Education and Compliance

Department: Early Childhood Education

Classification: [Exempt/Non-Exempt]

Location: San Diego, C


Position Definition

Under the direct supervision of the Divisional Director of Early Childhood Education and Compliance, the Site Supervisor is responsible for the day-to-day leadership, administration, supervision, regulatory compliance, and overall operational effectiveness of an assigned Heartbeat Music & Performing Arts Academy (HBMPAA) early childhood education site. The Site Supervisor is accountable for maintaining a safe, nurturing, developmentally appropriate, and compliant educational environment for children from infancy through kindergarten. This position is responsible for ensuring that site operations consistently meet applicable requirements established by the California Department of Social Services, Community Care Licensing Division; California Department of Education (CDE) requirements applicable to funded programs; Title 5; Title 22; and all other applicable federal, state, local, licensing, funding, and HBMPAA requirements. The Site Supervisor provides direct leadership and oversight to Teachers, Teaching Assistants, Volunteers, Interns, and other assigned site personnel. This position is expected to maintain current knowledge of applicable regulatory requirements, identify and immediately address deficiencies, hold employees accountable for performance and conduct, and ensure corrective actions are implemented and sustained. The Site Supervisor also serves as a member of the enrollment team and supports enrollment, family engagement, program quality, and student success. When designated by leadership, the Site Supervisor serves as the primary on-site contact for Community Care Licensing representatives and participates in licensing visits, inspections, audits, and corrective-action activities.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

1. Site Leadership and Regulatory Compliance

  • Provide direct leadership and oversight of daily site operations and ensure the program operates in accordance with applicable Title 5, Title 22, licensing, funding, and HBMPAA requirements.
  • Maintain current working knowledge of laws, regulations, licensing standards, funding requirements, and organizational policies applicable to the assigned program and site.
  • Ensure required staff-to-child ratios and supervision requirements are maintained at all times.
  • Maintain a safe, sanitary, organized, nurturing, and developmentally appropriate environment for children, employees, families, and visitors.
  • Conduct routine site reviews and inspections to identify potential licensing, health, safety, operational, or program deficiencies.
  • Take immediate action when a compliance or safety concern is identified. The Site Supervisor is responsible for addressing the concern, communicating expectations, initiating corrective action, verifying completion, and monitoring the issue to ensure sustained compliance.
  • Ensure required licenses, notices, emergency information, postings, inspection records, and other regulatory documentation are current and properly maintained.
  • Maintain site readiness for announced and unannounced licensing, funding, health, safety, and organizational inspections or audits.
  • Immediately escalate serious licensing, child safety, health, employee conduct, or regulatory concerns to appropriate leadership.
  • Serve as an on-site representative during licensing visits and inspections when designated by leadership and ensure identified deficiencies are addressed within established deadlines.

2. Staff Supervision, Performance, and Accountability

  • Provide direct supervision, direction, coaching, and performance management for Teachers, Teaching Assistants, Volunteers, Interns, and other assigned site personnel.
  • Clearly communicate job expectations and ensure employees follow HBMPAA policies, classroom procedures, licensing requirements, safety standards, and leadership directives.
  • Monitor employee attendance, punctuality, reliability, conduct, classroom performance, supervision practices, and compliance with assigned responsibilities.
  • Address employee performance, attendance, conduct, safety, or compliance concerns promptly and consistently in coordination with Human Resources and appropriate leadership.
  • Hold employees accountable for failure to meet established performance, conduct, attendance, safety, or regulatory expectations.
  • Document coaching, performance concerns, attendance issues, policy violations, and other matters requiring formal follow-up in accordance with HBMPAA procedures.
  • Conduct employee performance evaluations at least every six months or as otherwise required by HBMPAA.
  • Evaluate employee performance using established measures, which may include:
    • Desired Results Developmental Profile (DRDP) outcomes;
    • Parent Satisfaction Survey results;
    • kindergarten readiness and student-development measures;
    • attendance, punctuality, and reliability;
    • documented callouts affecting classroom ratios, coverage, or operations;
    • classroom management and student engagement;
    • compliance with licensing and safety requirements;
    • completion and accuracy of required documentation; and
    • overall job performance and adherence to HBMPAA standards.
  • Identify training and development needs and provide or coordinate appropriate coaching, mentoring, and professional development.
  • Model professional conduct, accountability, effective communication, and appropriate interactions with children, families, employees, and visitors.

3. Child Supervision, Education, and Program Quality

  • Ensure children receive appropriate care, supervision, education, and developmental support throughout the program day.
  • Monitor classrooms and program areas regularly to ensure active supervision and compliance with established child-safety practices.
  • Intervene immediately when unsafe, inappropriate, or noncompliant practices are observed.
  • Ensure curriculum and instructional practices are developmentally appropriate and aligned with HBMPAA program objectives and applicable early childhood education standards.
  • Monitor completion and accuracy of student assessments, including DRDP documentation and other required developmental measures.
  • Ensure individualized learning goals are informed by assessments, observations, developmental needs, and family input.
  • Support Teachers in implementing appropriate classroom management and positive guidance strategies.
  • Monitor student progress and kindergarten readiness and implement improvement strategies when program outcomes do not meet established expectations.

4. Family and Community Engagement

  • Develop and maintain professional, respectful, and collaborative relationships with parents, guardians, families, and community partners.
  • Ensure families receive timely and appropriate communication regarding student progress, classroom activities, program expectations, incidents, and other relevant matters.
  • Conduct or oversee parent/guardian conferences regarding student development, progress, goals, behavioral concerns, and kindergarten readiness.
  • Respond professionally and promptly to parent/guardian questions, concerns, and complaints and escalate significant matters when appropriate.
  • Maintain confidentiality of student, family, and employee information in accordance with applicable laws and HBMPAA policies.
  • Participate in enrollment activities and support efforts to maintain appropriate program enrollment.

title: Clean Energy Strategy Manager
description:
Con Edison, a multibillion-dollar energy utility, is leading the clean energy transition in New York City and Westchester County. We are investing hundreds of millions of dollars annually to integrate distributed resources into our electric and gas systems, support electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and scale adoption of energy efficiency and clean heating technologies across our customers.

Con Edisons Flexible Demand team develops the companys long term grid flexibility strategy and helps craft a vision for how the company will use demand side resources to achieve multiple strategic objectives.

The Flexible Demand Strategy Manager will support the Companys strategy, policy, and regulatory work related to grid flexibility and the NY Grid of the Future proceeding. The Strategy Manager will bring together internal experts and external partners to evolve policies and programs to scale and optimize flexible demand resources. To do so, they will be leading regulatory filings and studies, and design pilots that assess the value, potential, and optimal use cases for flexibility. This is a great role to exercise strategic and analytical thinking, drive results, and demonstrate application of cross disciplinary skills to the clean energy space.

Core Responsibilities
  • Collaborate on development a long-term vision and roadmap for grid flexibility to optimize value for the system, customers, the market, and policy goals, and identify the grid capabilities needed to enable this vision (including monitoring, visibility, and dispatch capabilities).

  • Lead studies to evaluate the potential of different technologies to increase flexible demand and its dependability, including energy storage, electric vehicles, electrified building load, virtual power plants, and demand response.
  • Collaborate with internal Company stakeholders including engineering, digital products, and clean energy program teams to determine the long-term strategy for flexible demand.
  • Engage with external stakeholders, including trade groups, advocacy organizations, other New York utilities, city officials, and regulatory personnel, and collaborate on joint studies and filings.
  • Lead regulatory filings relating to flexible demand including implementation plans, comments, and whitepapers.

Associate Infrastructure Engineer Position Summary

Fluke is seeking an Associate Infrastructure Engineer to support the company's enterprise infrastructure, cloud, identity, and workplace technology environments. Reporting within the CISO organization, this role provides an opportunity to build hands-on experience across systems administration, infrastructure operations, cloud technologies, and technical architecture while working alongside security, infrastructure, engineering, and business teams.

The position combines operational systems administration responsibilities with participation in architecture reviews, infrastructure planning, technology modernization initiatives, and security-focused improvements.

Fortive & OpCo Partnership

title: Junior Engineer – CIPP Operations
description:
US Infra Rehab Services, LLC (USIRS) is seeking a motivated, technically inclined Junior Engineer to support Cured-in-Place Pipe (CIPP) rehabilitation operations, with a primary focus on UV-CIPP installations.

This hands-on, field-based position offers opportunities to gain practical experience in specialized construction equipment, site preparation, quality control, and project coordination. Track, verify, and report daily labor hours and employee time records, material usage, and equipment utilization to support payroll processing, job costing, and project reporting.
  • Construction Equipment Operation: Gain hands-on experience operating construction equipment, including skid steers, winches, telehandlers (Lull), and other specialized field equipment. Assist with equipment setup and material handling under appropriate training and supervision.

Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is the leading inter-governmental organization in the field of migration and works closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all and does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.
IOM is a major actor in post-conflict recovery and reconstruction, and as such is heavily involved in livelihoods development and job creation programs. IOM’s strengths lie in its field presence around the country and operational capacity to rebuild community infrastructure, conduct vocational and other trainings, provide grant funding at local level to support business development, and support a variety of other areas key to recovery.
Under the overall supervision of the Head of Livelihoods Technical Team and the direct supervision of the Program Coordinator – Livelihoods, the incumbent will support the implementation, monitoring and coordination of livelihoods activities, including Graduation Approach (GA) interventions, within the assigned area of responsibility. The post will be based in Kirkuk, Iraq, with travel to various regions/governorates within Iraq, as required, to support livelihoods activities

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Under the supervision of the Program Coordinator – Livelihoods, and in coordination with relevant technical colleagues, support team leaders and livelihoods case managers in tracking the implementation of livelihoods activities, including Graduation Approach (GA) interventions, to help ensure timely delivery.

  • In coordination with the Program Coordinator – Livelihoods, travel to project sites across Iraq, as required, to monitor supported beneficiaries and target groups, and follow up on the implementation of livelihoods activities in line with approved guidelines, tools, policies, and procedures; document observations and share routine feedback with relevant teams.

  • In coordination with the Program Coordinator – Livelihoods, support routine quality checks and verification of livelihoods activities, including monitoring, community feedback processes, community engagement, and other relevant interventions, in line with established procedures.

  • In coordination with the Program Coordinator – Livelihoods, monitor, compile, and submit regular progress updates on livelihoods activities, including GA interventions, using established tracking tools and reporting templates.

  • Support the delivery of orientation and refresher sessions for operational teams on approved livelihoods tools, training materials, systems, and processes, including those related to GA activities.

  • In coordination with the Program Coordinator – Livelihoods, monitor program indicators and work closely with operations teams to track progress of livelihoods activities, including GA interventions, against approved workplans.

  • Support routine coordination with external stakeholders, including government entities, local authorities, NGOs, private sector partners, and other relevant actors, to facilitate implementation of livelihoods activities in line with approved program objectives and local priorities.

  • In coordination with the Program Coordinator – Livelihoods, draft routine reports, briefs, and activity overviews on trainings, sessions, and livelihoods interventions, including GA activities, for internal reporting and external information-sharing, as required.

  • Conduct regular monitoring visits, spot checks, and pre-/post-assessments of training and livelihoods activities, including GA interventions, and document findings for follow-up by relevant teams.

  • Review and check uploaded business plans, verification documents, and other relevant program documentation related to livelihoods activities, including GA interventions, for completeness and compliance with required formats and standards.

  • Support the dissemination of updated SOPs, guidance notes, tools, and implementation instructions to field teams, and assist in tracking their application in day-to-day implementation.

  • Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the supervisor.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Economics, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Administration, Psychology, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with four years of relevant professional experience; or

  • Completed high school diploma from an accredited academic institution with six years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • ​​ Experience in supporting the implementation, coordination, and monitoring of livelihoods, recovery, resilience, or community stabilization activities.

  • ​Experience in field-level operational follow-up, implementation tracking, and coordination with field teams across multiple locations.

  • ​Experience in conducting monitoring visits, reviewing activity documentation, and following up on implementation issues to support timely and quality delivery.

  • ​Experience in working with international organizations, UN agencies, NGOs, or donor-funded programs is an advantage.

  • ​Experience in coordinating with local authorities, service providers, community representatives, and other operational stakeholders is desirable.

  • ​Experience in data collection, consolidation, reporting, and use of implementation tracking tools is desirable.

  • Experience working with vulnerable individuals and communities, and applying inclusive and protection-sensitive approaches in program implementation, is an advantage.

Skills

  • Ability to work harmoniously with colleagues from varied cultures and professional backgrounds.
  • ​Good understanding of field implementation, operational follow-up, and monitoring processes.
  • ​Ability to review activity documentation, track implementation progress, and support timely reporting.
  • ​Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities under tight deadlines.
  • ​Strong communication and coordination skills, with the ability to work effectively with colleagues and stakeholders from diverse backgrounds.
  • ​Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

  • ​Knowledge of data management, reporting tools, and information tracking systems is an advantage.

title: Policy Manager – Strategic Team for Anti-Racism
description:
This is an Expression of Interest (EOI) opportunity, available on a lateral move basis only. Applications are open to Core Scottish Government employees only.

Job Title – Policy Manager – Strategic Team for Anti-Racism

Working Arrangement – Staff in roles compatible with hybrid working should aim to spend 40% of their contracted working time working in person at their contractual workplace. More information can be found within Hybrid Working Policy .

Grade – B3

Advert type – level transfer

Duration – Permanent

Eligibility - Expressions of interest are invited from substantive colleagues on level transfer from Core SG only.

Skilled Worker Sponsorship not being offered

Skilled Worker sponsorship is not available for this role. As a result, we are unable to appoint candidates who require Skilled Worker sponsorship now or in the future. Applicants must have an existing and ongoing right to work in the UK.

Overview

The Equality, Inclusion & Human Rights Directorate’s mission is to ensure equality, inclusion and human rights are at the centre of everything the Scottish Government does, promoting equality, tackling discrimination and fostering inclusion. The Mainstreaming and Inclusion Division drives actions to embed human rights and equality across government and the wider public sector, building capability and capacity to make deep and sustained progress on tackling inequality through better policy-making and service design.

The Strategic Team for Anti-Racism (STAR) leads Scotland’s cross-government work to tackle structural and systemic racism. Operating in a fast-paced, highly visible environment with significant political interest, STAR develops and delivers strategic policy to embed anti-racism across government and public services. This role requires resilience and the ability to manage complex, sensitive issues under scrutiny, balancing competing priorities while influencing diverse stakeholders. The successful candidate will play a leading role in the next phase of Scotland’s anti-racism work, implement and monitor a refreshed delivery plan aligned to the Race Equality Framework for Scotland (2016–2030), contribute to Scotland’s international treaty reporting obligations, and support wider community cohesion work, including providing reassurance and clear communication during times of uncertainty or heightened public concern. The postholder will also line-manage a B2 Policy Officer.

Role and Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the development and delivery of a public-facing anti-racism delivery plan, ensuring alignment with the Race Equality Framework for Scotland (2016–2030).
  • Provide strategic advice and support to senior leaders on anti-racism policy, including managing sensitive issues that attract scrutiny and involve balancing competing priorities.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, including community organisations, public bodies, and internal teams, to ensure meaningful engagement and co-production.
  • Monitor and report on progress against anti-racism commitments, ensuring transparency and accountability in delivery.
  • Lead on capability-building initiatives to embed anti-racism principles in policy-making and service design across Scottish Government.
  • Oversee operational delivery including ministerial briefings, PQs, correspondence and cross‑government coordination; manage risks, dependencies and milestones.
  • Lead and contribute to Scotland’s international treaty reporting obligations, ensuring accurate, timely submissions and alignment with human rights commitments.
  • Support wider community cohesion work, including offering reassurance and clear messaging during periods of uncertainty or heightened sensitivity.

Success Profile

Success profiles are specific to each job and they include the mix of behaviours, experience and technical criteria (if applicable) that candidates will be assessed on.

Experience:

  1. Demonstrable expertise in anti-racism policy and practice, with a deep understanding of structural and systemic racism and the ability to apply these principles to drive systemic change.
  2. Experience of working with Ministers and senior officials, preparing high-quality briefings, handling commissions, and managing politically sensitive issues under scrutiny.
  3. Ability to lead complex, cross-cutting policy or programmes, with strong planning, prioritisation and risk management skills, and embedding co-production with racialised communities into delivery.
  4. Ability to communicate and influence effectively across senior stakeholders, communities and delivery partners, including building trust and working effectively with racialised communities in sensitive contexts.
  5. Understanding of international human rights frameworks, with experience contributing to treaty reporting or similar compliance processes.

Behaviours:

  • Seeing the Big Picture – Level 3
  • Communicating & Influencing – Level 3
  • Delivering at Pace – Level 3
  • Leadership – Level 3

You can find out more about Success Profiles Behaviours, here: Success profiles: candidate guide - gov.scot

Working Pattern

The post is a full-time role, but staff with different working patterns are invited to apply, and we will assess proposed working patterns against the business requirements for this post.

Our standard hours are 35 hours per week and we offer a range of flexible working options depending on the needs of the role, including Flexi-leave

This directorate is based across Edinburgh and Glasgow, and in line with our current ways of working, our team follows a hybrid working approach, where colleagues use a mix of office based and remote working (working from home) depending on the requirements of the role and personal circumstances.

Further Information

Further information about this opportunity is available from Frankie McLean, frankie.mclean@gov.scot.

How to Apply

Please submit a CV and an Expression of Interest (maximum 500 words) outlining your suitability for the role, relevant skills and experience, and what you would bring to the team. Please align this to how you meet the behaviours, experience and technical skills listed in the Success Profile above.

Vacancies close at 11:59pm on the date displayed in the table, unless otherwise stated on the job advert.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can be used to support your application, but all statements and examples provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, and presented as your own) applications will be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action.

Please see our candidate guidance for more information on acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI in recruitment.

If invited for further assessment, this will consist of a light touch interview.

Discussions are to be confirmed.

Recruitment Principles

As a government organisation, we adhere to the Civil Service Commission Recruitment Principles and we investigate any complaints received in relation to recruitment cases.

About us

The Scottish Government is the devolved government for Scotland. We have responsibility for a wide range of key policy areas including: education, health, the economy, justice, housing and transport. We offer rewarding careers and employ people across Scotland in a wide range of professions and roles.

Our staff are part of the UK Civil Service observing the Civil Service Codeand working for Ministers and senior stakeholders to deliver vital public services which improve the lives of the people of Scotland.

We offer a supportive and inclusive working environment along with a wide range of employee benefits. Find out more about what we offer.

As part of the UK Civil Service, we uphold the Civil Service Nationality Rules.

Security checks

Successful candidates must complete the Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS), before they can be appointed. BPSS is comprised of four main pre-employment checks – Identity, Right to work, Employment History and a Criminal Record check (unspent convictions).

You can find out more about BPSS on the UK Government website, or read about the different levels of security checks in our Candidate Guide.

Equality statement

We are committed to equality and inclusion and we aim to recruit a diverse workforce that reflects the population of our nation.

Find out more about our commitment to diversity and how we offer and support recruitment adjustments for anyone who needs them.

Further information

Find out more about our organisation, what we offer staff members and how to apply on our Careers Website.

Read our Candidate Guide for further information on our recruitment and application processes.

description:
Position Title:

Electrical Reliability Engineer

Pay Rate:

$93,400-$124,500

Multiple factors, including Individual experience, skills and abilities will determine where an employee is ultimately placed in the pay range.

Variable pay may provide additional opportunities for financial awards. This job is eligible to participate in IP’s short –term incentive plan.

Category/Shift:

Salaried Full-Time

Physical Location:

3737 Hwy 3

Redwood, MS 39156

The Job You Will Perform:

An Electrical Reliability Engineer’s responsibility is to eliminate unscheduled downtime and increase the life of our assets. At Vicksburg, reliability engineering combines traditional maintenance engineering with process engineering for a holistic approach to address downtime liabilities on a production system. Reliability Engineers focus on making sustainable improvements to critical manufacturing systems and have secondary departmental assignments. The Electrical Reliability Engineer reports directly to the Senior Electrical Reliability Engineer and is a member of the Mill’s Maintenance and Engineering group.


Reliability Engineers must be able to interact effectively with all the levels of the organization – from maintenance craftsmen and operators through mill and corporate management. They work closely with operating and maintenance leaders to eliminate chronic problems and to support high priority area objectives. Excellent communication skills are a necessity. Reliability engineering assignments have true impact on the performance of the mill and offer a challenging and rewarding career.

A Reliability Engineer will be accountable for:

  • Working safely in an industrial environment
  • Eliminating unscheduled maintenance downtime
  • Managing asset criticalities, equipment care strategies, and maintenance policies to ensure failure prevention
  • Resolving chronic problems using RCFA or other structured problem-solving techniques
  • Leading step change improvements in key focus areas critical to the mill’s success
  • Influencing maintenance activities to achieve reliability targets and increase asset life
  • Managing repair and capital projects that directly impact the reliability of electrical equipment throughout the mill
  • Improving Reliability systems and behaviors
  • Provide electrical technical assistance to maintenance
  • Support Electrical maintenance in Leadership Role as a set up FLL when needed, weekend duty, and weekly after-hours rotation call out.
  • Core team member of the MWS Team who is required to participate in all daily MWS meetings and support the OMC and team to ensure that work from these reliability work opportunities is given the proper priority.
  • Arch Flash Mitigation
  • Electrical Power Distribution
  • Electrical Equipment Obsolescence Plans
  • Electrical Transformer Contingency Plan
  • Electrical Motor Maintenance and reliability

The Skills You Will Bring:

  • A bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical or chemical engineering is preferred with 5+ years of experience in a maintenance/reliability function required.
  • Non-degreed candidates with significant experience in a related function will also be considered
  • Pulp/Paper mill experience is preferred.

Preferred:

  • Arch flash mitigation projects
  • Electrical Motor Lubrication
  • Precision practices
  • Equipment care strategies
  • Lean Manufacturing
  • Root Cause Failure Analysis
  • FMEA
  • Project Management
  • CMMS Systems (SAP is highly preferred)
  • Transformer Predictive Maintenance
  • Electrical Power Distribution
  • Key Competencies:
    Action oriented, Functional/technical skills, Problem solving, Managing through systems, Priority Setting, Organizing, Oral and Written Communication Skills, Results Oriented, Managerial Courage, and Customer Focus

title: AI Solution Specialist
description:
At Infoblox, every breakthrough begins with a bold “what if.”
What if your ideas could ignite global innovation?
What if your curiosity could redefine the future?

We invite you to step into the next exciting chapter of your career journey. Bring your creativity, drive, your daring spirit, and feel what it’s like to thrive on a team big enough to make an impact, yet small enough to make a difference. Our cloud-first networking and security solutions already protect 70% of the Fortune 500, and we’re looking for creative thinkers ready to push that influence even further. Join us and discover how far your bold “what if” can take the world, your community, and your career.

Here, how we empower our people is extraordinary: Glassdoor Best Places to Work 2025, Great Place to Work-Certified in five countries, and Cigna Healthy Workforce honors three years running — and what we build is world-class: recognized as CybersecAsia’s Best in Critical Infrastructure 2024 — evidence that when first-class technology meets empowered talent, remarkable careers take shape. So, what if the next big idea, and the next great career story, comes from you? Become the force that turns every “what if” into “what’s next”.

In a world where you can be anything, Be Infoblox.

AI Solution Specialist

We have an opportunity for an AI Solution Specialist to join our Business Strategy team in Tacoma, Washington, reporting to the Strategic Programs Director. In this pivotal role, you will help design, deliver, and scale practical AI solutions that transform how Bloxers work — from productivity and automation to decision support and AI-indexed workflows. Collaborating closely with functional leaders, IT, operations, data and AI teams, and our AI Investment Office, you will translate real business problems into secure, production-ready AI solutions that deliver measurable value using enterprise platforms such as Glean and Microsoft Copilot.

Be a Contributor — What You’ll Do

  • Identify and prioritize high-impact AI use cases and workflows across functions that improve productivity, cycle time, quality, or decision-making
  • Translate business needs into practical AI solution designs, including agents, copilots, automations, and analytics grounded in enterprise data
  • Design and configure AI agents and workflows using platforms such as Glean, Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, and approved third-party AI tools
  • Collaborate with IT, data, and security teams to connect solutions to the right systems and data sources, aligned to Infoblox AI governance and guardrails
  • Build clear success metrics and lightweight business cases for AI solutions, and instrument telemetry to track adoption, time saved, quality, and financial impact
  • Run pilots end to end — from discovery and scoping through testing, user feedback, iteration, and production rollout
  • Use AI tools directly in your own work (e.g., GenAI copilots, RAG-based agents, analytics assistants) to accelerate analysis, content, documentation, and reporting
  • Partner with enablement and change leaders to create simple how-to guides, demo flows, and training moments that help teams adopt AI in daily work
  • Document and share reusable patterns, prompts, architectures, and checklists so future AI solutions can be built faster and more consistently

Be Prepared — What You Bring

  • 2+ years of experience in roles such as business analyst, solutions consultant, program manager, or operations analyst, including strong hands-on experience with AI, automation, or advanced analytics
  • Proven ability to take ambiguous business problems and design practical technology or AI solutions that deliver measurable outcomes
  • Hands-on experience with AI or automation platforms (e.g., Glean, Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate, low-code agents, or comparable tools)

title: Regional Specialty Services Manager
description:
Parallel Management Group is looking for a Regional Specialty Services Manager. This role leads the rollout, training, and ongoing support of Parallel's specialty resident programs — spanning memory care training, end-of-life doula support, and restorative care — across the communities they support. This role partners with building and regional leadership to determine which programs are the right fit for each community and in what order they should be introduced, then works directly with onsite teams (Life Enrichment Directors, Memory Care Coordinators, Wellness Coordinators, Restorative Aides, and End-of-Life Doulas) to launch each program and keep it running well over time.


General Responsibilities

  • Schedule and host ongoing training experiences for staff at all communities within the region.
  • Communicate with building and regional management to identify which specialty programs are appropriate for new communities, and implement programs in order of priority.
  • Provide ongoing support to the staff responsible for day-to-day program delivery, including Life Enrichment Directors, Memory Care Coordinators, Wellness Coordinators, Restorative Aides, and End-of-Life Doulas (where applicable).
