  • Send communities reminders throughout the month to keep program submissions and follow-through on track, and assist communities with carrying out resident requests as needed, with hands-on support for communities that are new to a program.
  • Collect submissions from all communities each month and compile them into a newsletter distributed across the region.

Memory Care & Dementia Training Program Responsibilities

  • Facilitate hands-on staff training experiences, including virtual dementia simulation training, meaningful engagement training, and challenging behavior training (some sessions require a co-facilitator).
  • Launch the program in new communities with memory care: complete resident cognitive assessments, install sensory/way-finding displays, and assemble staff sensory boxes.
  • Launch family education nights in new communities and attend the first several sessions until the community is ready to run them independently.
  • Follow up regularly with onsite staff to confirm the program is being maintained, and provide hands-on help to catch communities up as needed.

End-of-Life Doula Program Responsibilities

  • Complete End-of-Life Doula training/certification in order to train community-based doulas.
  • Host doula training classes — increasingly delivered virtually via Zoom to multiple communities at once, rather than spending multiple days on-site training just a few doulas at a time.
  • Help each community identify and establish a lead doula responsible for maintaining doula assignments.
  • Set up doula program binders for new communities and coach the lead doula to maintain them going forward, checking in and providing catch-up support as needed.
  • Plan periodic appreciation events for doulas and arrange ongoing education opportunities.

Restorative Care Program Responsibilities

  • Recruit and train restorative techs to launch and expand the program in additional communities.
  • Monitor restorative documentation and track resident progress.
  • Meet regularly with outside providers involved in the program.
  • Partner across departments to ensure all components of the program are being carried out consistently.
  • Collaborate with a fitness coach to elevate the program, with plans to extend fitness coach support to communities in the West region.

title: Rope/Handle Tow Operations
description:
Department: Mountain Operations
Reports To: Lift Supervisor / Area Manager
Employment Type: Winter Seasonal
Schedule: Full-Time (5+ shifts/week) or Part-Time; must be available weekends and holidays

Job Overview

The Rope / Handle Tow Operator is responsible for safely monitoring and operating Seven Oaks' surface lifts. Unlike a chair lift operator, this position is primarily stationed inside a lift shack where the operator must remain alert and continuously watch guests using the rope or handle tow.

The operator must be prepared to immediately stop the tow when a guest falls, experiences difficulty, or another unsafe condition occurs. When necessary, the operator will leave the shack after stopping the tow to assist the guest, clear the tow path, and restart the lift once it is safe to do so.

This position requires strong attention to detail, good judgment, dependability, and the ability to remain focused while monitoring guests for extended periods.

Essential Job Functions

Other duties may be assigned.

Rope / Handle Tow Monitoring & Operation

  • Remain stationed in the designated lift shack while the rope or handle tow is operating, except when assisting a guest or performing assigned operational duties.
  • Continuously and attentively monitor guests using the rope or handle tow.
  • Watch for falls, unsafe behavior, equipment concerns, obstructions, or other situations requiring the tow to be stopped.
  • Immediately stop the rope or handle tow when a guest falls, needs assistance, or an unsafe condition occurs.
  • When necessary, safely exit the shack after stopping the tow to assist guests who have fallen or are having difficulty.
  • Ensure the tow path and surrounding area are clear before restarting the rope or handle tow.
  • Restart the tow only after determining that it is safe to resume operation.
  • Learn and follow all operational, safety, emergency, stop/start, and equipment procedures associated with rope and handle tow operations.
  • Perform required safety inspections of tow paths, load areas, and unload areas.
  • Immediately report equipment concerns, unsafe conditions, accidents, or guest incidents to management.
  • Check and verify guest lift tickets and passes as required.
  • Remain attentive and ready to respond throughout the entire operating shift.

Area Maintenance

  • Maintain safe load, unload, and tow areas by shoveling, raking, leveling, and removing excess snow as needed.
  • Keep the lift shack and surrounding areas clean and organized.
  • Assist with fencing, signage installation or replacement, and other mountain projects as assigned.
  • Assist with other operational duties when the rope or handle tow is not operating or as directed by management.

Guest Service

  • Greet guests in a welcoming, positive, and professional manner.
  • Provide clear instructions on the proper and safe use of the rope or handle tow.
  • Assist guests, particularly beginners, who may have difficulty using the tow.
  • Remain patient and courteous when assisting guests who have fallen or need additional help.
  • Become familiar with Seven Oaks skiable terrain, facilities, and services to accurately answer guest questions and provide directions.

title: Consultant Communication Officer
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration


Project Context and Scope

Established in 1951, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is a Related Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all.

According to the Notre Dame Global Adaptation Initiative (ND-GAIN) index, Madagascar is among the least prepared countries to deal with climate shocks, ranking 174th out of 181 countries. Deforestation is critical: it is estimated that 30% of forests have been lost since 2001, and the province of Toamasina alone accounts for 55% of national forest losses. The municipality of Andasibe presents a strategic paradox: as a global biodiversity centre home to the endemic Indri Indri and the Andasibe-Mantadia National Park, Madagascar's leading ecotourism destination, it is facing accelerated deforestation linked to a strong dependence on wood energy.

This dynamic is compounded by the pronounced landlocked nature of many fokontany, some of which are hamlets, located up to 12 km from the communal capital, are only accessible on foot. Deprived of regular access to markets, basic services and employment opportunities, rural households are turning to charcoal and firewood as immediately accessible sources of income; internal migration flows to the park area are increasing this pressure.

In response to this challenge, IOM is implementing a pilot programme titled “Integrated Territorial Model of Andasibe: Clean Cooking, Reforestation, and Rural Roads” articulating the transition to clean cooking, ecological restoration and rural access planning. Aligned with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7 and 13, the National Clean Cooking Development Policy, the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) and the National Strategy and Action Plan for Biodiversity (NBSAP), the project aims to constitute a model that can be replicated at the national level.

Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing

Under the direct supervision of the Programme Officer in Madagascar and in close coordination with relevant units at IOM Madagascar, the Communication consultant will be responsible and accountable for developing and implementing communication, visibility and public information activities in support of IOM Madagascar’s project. The successful candidate will ensure effective dissemination of information on IOM’s interventions, strengthen the Organization’s visibility among key stakeholders, and support the production of communication materials, media engagement, digital content and advocacy initiatives.
Tasks to be performed under this contract

• Coordinate the implementation of CO’s external communications strategies related to the project in line with the Organization’s strategic communications priorities and guidelines, promoting an accurate narrative on migration-related issues with the media, general public, the UN and other key partners;
• Provide technical advice to the Senior Management Team (SMT) on strategic communications issues, including sensitive internal and external communications, and ensure the high quality and consistency of media and public outreach for the CO by building the capacity of and providing strategic communications/media advice and support to the Chief of Mission and SMT.
• Supervise and manage the CO’s Communications staff to ensure content is of the highest quality, aligned with IOM’s brand guidelines and consistent with the Organization’s strategic communications priorities.
• Supervise all external communications content produced by the CO, including stories, blogs, video and social media content; provide timely editorial advice in consultation with the Regional Media and Communications Officer on whether they are best suited for publication on national, regional or global IOM platforms.
• Support high profile visibility events and assist the Chief of Mission in preparing to represent the CO, including arranging media interviews, reviewing speeches and preparing media Lines to Take. Develop and contribute content to communications campaigns at a national, regional and international level, including for relevant UN Days.
• Manage the CO’s online presence, including through its social media accounts and website to increase the impact of CO’s digital outreach.
• Draft media key messages, Statements, talking points and other relevant background documents for IOM’s use.
• Engage with the UN Country Team’s Communication Group and other relevant actors and lead on developing media messages on key issues by working together on campaigns and issues of joint concern.
• Undertake duty travel to take photographs and video footage and gather material for multi-media content showcasing IOM field activities. Ensure that Media and Communications content is clear and concise, and that digital informed consent is secured.
• Ensure that there is appropriate gender, diversity and inclusion awareness in all IOM external communications.
• Perform such other duties as may be assigned. the implementation of CO’s external communications strategies related to the project in line with the Organization’s strategic communications priorities and guidelines, promoting an accurate narrative on migration-related issues with the media, general public, the UN and other key partners;

Performance indicators for the evaluation of results

• Project communication and visibility plan developed and implemented, with project communication products delivered in accordance with IOM branding guidelines and donor visibility requirements.
• Press releases, human-interest stories, social media content, videos and other communication materials produced and disseminated in a timely manner, with at least one visibility product developed for each major project milestone or event.
• Communication support provided for high-level events, donor visits and media engagements, including preparation of speeches, talking points, key messages and media lines-to-take, with all deliverables submitted within agreed timelines.
• Project communication inputs, visibility reports and donor communication requirements completed and submitted on time, including field missions conducted to collect multimedia content and beneficiary stories in compliance with IOM standards on informed consent, protection, gender and inclusion. Add in details xxx

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Master’s degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
  • University degree in one of the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Experience

  • Experience as a writer, editor and content producer/manager in Journalism and/or public information roles, preferably in the Region;
  • Experience in digital communications and social media;
  • Experience in corporate writing and editing;
  • Experience in managing donor visibility;
  • Experience with media liaison;
  • Experience in humanitarian communications;
  • Experience in working in UN or other International organizations.

Skills

  • Skills in graphic design, particularly using Adobe programmes an advantage;
  • Skills in photography and videography, both shooting and editing an advantage;
  • Demonstrated gender awareness and gender sensitivity;
  • High level of professionalism and ability to work under pressure and adhere to strict deadlines in a complex and fast changing environment; and,
  • Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively and harmoniously with colleagues from varied cultures and professional backgrounds.

Languages

For this consultancy, Malagasy, french and English are required.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Travel to other provinces of Madagascar to document field level activities might be required.

Required Competencies

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.

  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Notes

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Kitchen Lead
description:
Build a kitchen from zero.


Buckley’s Family Adventure opens this fall in Woodland Hills — 25,000 square feet of go-karts, laser tag, arcade, and a from-scratch kitchen that hasn’t cooked its first ticket yet. There’s no existing standard to inherit here. Whoever takes this job sets it.


Who we’re looking for


Honestly? Somewhere between Mister Rogers and Anthony Bourdain.


The Mister Rogers half: you actually care about the people on your line. You develop them. You’re the reason a nineteen-year-old prep cook decides to stay in this industry.


The Bourdain half: you have real, unembarrassed pride in the food. You care that the third order of the night looks exactly like the first. You’d rather remake it than send it.


What you’ll actually do


Run a high-volume kitchen calmly under pressure. Hold food safety and consistency to a standard nobody has to check behind you on. Build the prep systems, par levels, and opening and closing checklists from scratch. Hire, train, and develop your own team. Work directly with our GM on menu execution and cost.


Requirements


• ServSafe Manager certification — current, or obtainable before your start date. We’ll cover the cost.

• Real experience running a high-volume kitchen or leading a line

• Comfortable with allergen protocols in a kitchen that serves a lot of kids

• Available nights, weekends, and holidays

Our kitchen is pork-free and shellfish-free. Family entertainment center volume is spiky — dead at 2 PM, slammed at 6:30. If you’ve worked events, stadiums, or high-volume casual, you know the rhythm.


The honest part


This is a first location. The equipment is brand new and will occasionally be uncooperative. The menu will change in the first six months because we’ll learn things. You’ll be building the plane somewhat in flight. That’s either the appeal or the dealbreaker, and we’d rather you decide which right now.


What we offer


$24.00/hour · Free meal every shift up to $25 · 4 Adventure Passes a month · 40 hours PTO annually (90-day wait, 80-hour cap) · California paid sick leave · 1.5x holiday pay · Your birthday off, paid · $20/paycheck cell phone allowance · $20/paycheck uniform allowance · Up to $250/year toward your development


How to apply


Apply at the link. Serious candidates will be invited to cook — a paid two-hour working interview in our kitchen.

title: Senior Manager – Tax Compliance
description:

Your contribution!

Reporting to the Director, Taxation, the Senior Manager, Tax Compliance is responsible for leading and coordinating Innergex’s tax compliance activities in a high-volume, fast-growing international environment.

They are responsible for planning and coordinating tax compliance activities, ensuring that deliverables are completed on time and meet quality standards, while driving continuous process improvement. Although the role has no direct people-management responsibilities, they provide functional leadership to Tax Advisors and Senior Tax Advisors involved in tax compliance activities.

Your day-to-day!

  • Lead the annual tax compliance calendar, establish priorities, and ensure that deadlines are met.
  • Oversee and review the preparation of income tax returns and information returns, including T2, T5013, T106, and T1134 filings.
  • Coordinate, review, and, when required, prepare key tax calculations, including Foreign Accrual Property Income (FAPI), surplus account calculations, safe income calculations, and computations related to the Excess Interest and Financing Expenses Limitation (EIFEL) rules.
  • Oversee activities related to tax incentives and tax credits, from identifying eligible expenditures through to supporting tax audits.
  • Anticipate and incorporate new compliance requirements arising from Innergex’s growth and evolving tax legislation.
  • Provide functional leadership to Advisors and Senior Advisors involved in tax compliance activities and support their development of autonomy and sound tax judgment.
  • Plan and allocate work based on priorities, team members’ expertise, and deadlines.
  • Coordinate engagements assigned to external consultants and review their work, focusing their involvement on complex, high-value matters.
  • Participate in interactions with tax authorities and coordinate responses to information requests and tax audits.
  • Develop and maintain the required level of in-house expertise, particularly in international taxation.
  • Develop, prepare, and deliver internal tax training based on team needs, legislative changes, and tax matters relevant to Innergex.
  • Analyze tax rules applicable to new jurisdictions of interest to Innergex and assess the key compliance obligations arising from them.
  • Develop tools and presentations to communicate tax matters effectively to internal teams and management.
  • Provide the tax guidance required for the accounting treatment of reorganizations, acquisitions, and other tax planning transactions.
  • Propose and implement improvements to the processes and tools used by the Tax team.

Your skills, our requirements!

  • Minimum of 7 to 10 years of experience in corporate taxation or with a large public accounting firm.

  • CPA designation required.

  • Master’s degree in Taxation required.

  • Knowledge of international taxation.

  • Knowledge of tax planning and tax structure optimization is considered an asset.

  • Strong aptitude for continuous learning, combined with a practical and pragmatic mindset.

  • Excellent analytical skills and strong organizational abilities.

  • Ability to adapt in a fast-paced, international growth environment.

  • Natural and collaborative leadership style.

  • Ability to make sound decisions under pressure.

  • Strong sense of ethics and professional integrity.

  • Interest in innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

  • Sound judgment and strong critical-thinking skills.

  • Microsoft Office.

  • Advanced Excel skills and proficiency with a wide range of software applications.

  • Bilingualism (French and English, both spoken and written) is required to ensure ongoing collaboration with various stakeholders outside Québec on a regular basis.

Additional considerations!

  • The position is based at the Company’s headquarters in Longueuil, conveniently located steps from the Longueuil–Université-de-Sherbrooke metro station.
  • This position is a P4 level.

Our benefits!

  • Competitive salary and annual bonus;
  • Three weeks vacation to start and paid vacations during the holiday season;
  • 100% Innergex-funded medical insurance from day one of employment, including primary care services through dialogue (or telemedicine) for permanent positions;
  • Group retirement plans with employer participation;

  • Electric vehicle (E-VIP) incentive program;

title: Lead Full Stack Engineer
description:
About GeneralMind

We deploy AI employees that automate messy operational handovers across supply chains - processing orders, validating invoices, coordinating suppliers, and handling exceptions directly on top of enterprise systems like SAP, Oracle, JDE, and Dynamics.

title: Butcher
description:
Job Summary

The Butcher is responsible for preparing, cutting, trimming, portioning, and storing various types of meat, poultry, and seafood in accordance with hotel standards. The role ensures high-quality food preparation, proper hygiene, food safety compliance, and effective inventory control while minimizing waste and maintaining kitchen efficiency.

Key Responsibilities

1. Meat Preparation & Production

Prepare, cut, debone, trim, and portion meat, poultry, and seafood according to established recipes and hotel standards.

Ensure all meat products meet the required quality, freshness, and presentation standards.

Prepare meat portions according to daily operational requirements, banquet functions, and restaurant demands.

Maintain consistency in portion sizes to support food cost control.

Coordinate with the Executive Chef and Sous Chef regarding daily production requirements.

2. Food Safety & Hygiene

Follow HACCP standards and hotel food safety policies.

Ensure proper handling, labeling, dating, and storage of all meat products.

Maintain appropriate refrigeration and freezer temperatures.

Prevent cross-contamination by following proper sanitation procedures.

Ensure all equipment, knives, cutting boards, and working areas are cleaned and sanitized regularly.

Comply with local municipality regulations and hotel hygiene standards.

3. Inventory & Cost Control

Monitor meat inventory and report shortages to the Sous Chef.

Apply FIFO (First In, First Out) principles to minimize food waste.

Inspect incoming meat deliveries for freshness, quality, and correct quantities.

Ensure proper utilization of meat products to reduce unnecessary wastage.

Support the kitchen team in maintaining food costs within the approved budget.

4. Equipment & Workplace Safety

Operate butchery equipment safely, including meat slicers, grinders, knives, and cutting machines.

Maintain all tools and equipment in good working condition.

Report equipment damage or maintenance requirements immediately.

Follow occupational health and safety procedures.

Maintain a clean, organized, and safe butchery working environment.

5. Teamwork & Operational Support

Coordinate with other kitchen sections to ensure smooth daily operations.

Support banquet preparation and special events when required.

Assist the Executive Chef with special meat preparation requests.

Participate in departmental training and food safety programs.

Perform other duties assigned by the Executive Chef or Sous Chef.

Qualifications & Experience

Culinary certification or relevant vocational training is preferred.

Minimum 2 years of experience as a Butcher, preferably within a hotel or hospitality environment.

Strong knowledge of meat cuts, deboning, trimming, and portion control.

Knowledge of HACCP and food safety standards.

Experience operating professional butchery equipment.

Basic English communication skills.

Ability to work flexible shifts, including weekends and public holidays.

Required Skills & Competencies

Excellent knife-handling and meat preparation skills.

Strong attention to detail and quality.

Good understanding of food hygiene and sanitation.

Ability to work efficiently under pressure.

Effective time management and organizational skills.

Teamwork and communication.

Knowledge of food cost control and waste reduction.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Compliance with food safety and hygiene standards.

Consistency in meat quality and portion sizes.

Reduction of meat wastage.

Effective inventory rotation and storage.

Timely completion of daily production requirements.

Cleanliness and maintenance of the butchery section.

General Responsibilities

Demonstrate the hotel's service standards and IHG values.

Comply with all hotel policies and procedures.

Maintain professional grooming and personal hygiene standards.

Support the hotel in achieving operational excellence and guest satisfaction.

Carry out any additional duties reasonably assigned by management.

title: Case Manager (Part-Time) - Inland - Utilization Management
description:
Responsibilities:

Job Summary: The Case Manager oversees the process of care delivered to patients, works collaboratively, and provides leadership to the healthcare team, and is committed to organization goals. Case Manager examines records for medical treatments and interventions to avoid payment denial resulting in optimization in reimbursement by assessing appropriateness of treatments, effectiveness, timing, and setting. This includes observation level of care vs inpatient level of care based on medical necessity. This role also includes patient assessment for discharge planning as well as appropriateness of level of care based on medical necessity. Case Manager is integral in minimizing and assisting with barriers to discharge.

  1. Coordinates/facilitates patient care progression throughout the continuum of care.

  2. Assures the plan of care and services provided are patient focused, high quality, efficient and cost effective.

  3. Meets directly with patient/family to assess needs and develop an individualized continuing care plan in collaboration with the physician.

  4. Monitors length of stay and ancillary resource use on an ongoing basis and takes actions to achieve continuous improvement in both areas.

  5. Communicates information to the Utilization Management or Case Management team to aid in appropriate level of care determination and reimbursement by third party payors as well as working closely with Physician Advisory team on concurrent denials to ensure most appropriate level of care prior to billing.

  6. Monitors patient flow through multidisciplinary rounds and aids in implementation of processes for improvement to decrease delays.

  7. Serves as patient advocate to ED population by identifying needs, coordinating services and resources for the management of complex patients to facilitate quality care and cost efficient outcomes.

  8. Ensures that all elements critical to the plan of care have been communicated to the patient/family as well as members of the healthcare team.

  9. Ability to cover various populations across the organization, including the Emergency Department.

  10. Performs all other duties as requested by Case Manager Supervisor and/or Director.

Qualifications:

  • 1-2 years of recent acute care hospital experience required.

  • Data entry/computer experience required.

title: Branch Manager
description:
Evergreen Federal Bank is seeking talented individuals who believe in offering exceptional customer service and enjoy making a positive difference in the community where they live. Celebrating over 90 years of operation, our institution has provided many stable careers. We offer competitive pay and a community-centric culture. We are currently accepting applications for Branch Manager in our Ashland branch office.


Job Summary and Responsibilities

The Branch Manager is responsible for providing supervision and leadership direction for staff to provide efficient daily operation of a full-service branch office. This includes operations, customer service, security and safety in accordance with the Bank's objectives. The Branch Manager will ensure adequate staffing levels and staff development and actively participate in the delivery of all financial services provided by the bank. Essential functions of this position are as follows:

  • Provide friendly, courteous and professional communication support to customers in person, as well as respond to incoming telephone calls, electronic mail and voice mail.
  • Motivate and lead a high-performance branch team by setting expectations to accomplish goals and objectives of the bank.
  • Provide teller and new accounts relief as necessary to ensure excellent customer service by handling monetary transactions for customers, (i.e. deposits, withdrawals, loan payments, check cashing, opening new accounts, etc.).
  • Ensure accurate cash handling in the service to our customers and minimize time and effort to locate outages.
  • Manages the selection, placement, performance, development, and termination of branch staff.
  • Manage scheduling, prioritize workflow and assign staff to cover customer traffic and ensure timely completion of tasks.
  • Provide supervision and training for all staff in areas of operations and conduct staff meetings.
  • Provide products and services education, assistance, research, support, and problem resolution in a professional and timely manner to our customers and employees.
  • Monitor staff job performance in your area of responsibility and make recommendations regarding job performance evaluations and disciplinary actions.
  • Adhere to bank security policy and procedures and be responsible for testing, maintenance and operation of security devices.
  • Ensure that branch staff follows internal policies and procedures, Bank's CIP, BSA and related security procedures plus any pertinent State or Federal laws and regulations.
  • Attend Operational meetings as required.
  • Performs special projects or other duties as directed by senior management.
  • Maintain all required documentation to meet compliance and procedural standards.
  • Schedule and occasionally perform collateral inspections on construction loans and direct disbursement of funds.
  • Ensure the branch and surrounding area are kept clean, professional and free of unwanted trash and debris.
  • Provide support and/or work at alternate locations when requested and required to do so
  • The Branch Manager is expected to participate in community affairs to increase the Bank's visibility and to enhance new and existing opportunities.

Eligibility

Skills and Abilities

  • Thorough understanding of deposit products and bank services.
  • Strong communication (written and oral) and organizational skills.
  • Knowledge of the principles and practices of staff supervision and performance management and the ability to develop staff through coaching, training opportunities and mentorship.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and ability to develop rapport with people.
  • Ability to work within and foster a team environment.
  • Provide excellent customer service.
  • Maintain a professional image.
  • Demonstrates a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and achieve results according to branch priority.
  • Knowledge of regulatory and compliance laws and procedures.
  • Demonstrate strong attention to detail.

Education/Experience

Bachelor’s Degree preferred. Additionally, it is preferred to have a minimum four years of management experience with at least one year in banking.


Benefits

We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, life, and long-term disability insurance; paid vacation, sick leave, holidays, and volunteer time off (VTO); tuition reimbursement; and retirement benefits.


Physical demands

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position for prolonged periods.
  • Be able to move about the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, etc.
  • Be able to move/transport up to 30 lbs.
  • Operate a computer and other office machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, printer, scanner, and other standard office equipment.
  • The work primarily performed in this position is done within an indoor, climate-controlled environment.
  • Occasional work in outdoor weather conditions.

Candidates must be able to complete all essential functions and physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation.


Evergreen Federal Bank is an equal opportunity employer, including veterans and individuals with disabilities.

title: Public Affairs / Visual Information Program Manager - US Navy
description:
Oversee Force-wide public affairs and operational visual information (OPTASK VI) program support, with a focus on equipment readiness, inventory accountability, policy coordination and fleet training. · Coordinate equipment troubleshooting, warranty or depot repair, replacement purchasing support, lifecycle planning and distribution to fleet units.

· Plan or support visual information training events across fleet concentration areas, including San Diego, Pearl Harbor, Everett, Yokosuka and Sasebo.

title: Regional Channel Manager -Pacific Northwest/California
description:
Regional Channel Manager

Position Summary

The Regional Channel Manager is responsible for a variety of sales activities ranging from recruiting agents and sales channel partners, traditional cold calling campaigns to webinars, video conferences, Social Media engagement, and finally managed prospecting campaigns utilizing technology and marketing resources available from Telesystem.

The Regional Channel Manager is responsible for business development by selling Telesystem products and services, generating new business leads and achieving or exceeding a predetermined monthly revenue goal by representing the small to mid-size business segments.

The Regional Channel Manager reports directly to the Sales Manager.

There are no direct reports to this position.

The Regional Channel Manager interfaces with the following key departments and outside resources: Telesystem Agents and Customers, Sales Administration, Sales Implementation, Sales Engineering, Customer Service/Business Relations, Accounting, Billing Departments

Essential Functions

  • Increasing the business locations owned and profits of Telesystem by using the consultative sales approach with their customers in the sale of the Telesystem products and services.
  • Creating and supporting the public and partner facing side of Telesystem thru partner orientation, education and active engagement.
  • Work with National Channel Managers to coordinate and participate in local agent activities.
  • Cultivating new businesses and business locations owned targeting the small to mid-size business segment.
  • Maintaining and growing existing customer relationships/contracts/businesses/etc. through proactive communication.
  • Acting as the customers’ advocate within the Telesystem organization.
  • Promoting the benefits of Telesystem products and services to both new and existing customers.
  • Maintaining accurate and timely orders, service qualifications and any necessary paperwork that is relevant to the sales process.
  • Creating a quote that accurately depicts the customers’ existing solution with their current provider as a cost comparison and/or creating a quote that accurately depicts a customer solution based on an initial discovery.
  • Following and enforcing the Company’s policies and procedures, including the EEO guidelines and safety, at all times;
  • Performing any miscellaneous department duties as needed.

Education and Experience Requirements

  • 2 Years of previous experience with quota based sales - Required
  • A track record of successful achievement of sales goals and client satisfaction – Required
  • Telecom business to business sales experience – Strongly Preferred
  • Associates or Bachelor’s Degree General Business or Business Administration - Preferred
  • Salesforce Customer Relationship Management Experience– Preferred

Core Competencies

  • Agile – Embraces change; adaptable and flexible; sense of urgency;
  • Innovative – Uses critical thinking; Creativity; Continuous learning; Challenges the status quo;
  • Customer Focused – External/Internal; Creates the exceptional customer experience; demonstrates a sales and service mentality;
  • Collaborative – Teamwork, Proactive knowledge sharing, Constructive Conflict;
  • Accountable – See it, Own it, Solve it, Do it; Hold each other accountable.

Job Specific Competencies

  • Deliver Results – Strategic planning and execution; Makes decisions in the best interest of the Company; Knows and responds to the business climate; Manages ambiguity
  • Displays Leadership – Role Model; Communicates vision; possesses Emotional Maturity; Manages Risks; Resiliency; Business Acumen

Other Skills and Requirements

  • Background record that meets Company standards;
  • Reliable means of transportation at all times;
  • Present professional appearance and demeanor;
  • Strictly maintains confidentiality of financial and/or other information acquired in the course of work; discloses only when authorized, unless legally obligated to do so.
  • Valid driver’s license and driving record that meets company standards at all times

Working Conditions and Physical Demands

  • Physical Demands:
  • Walking, kneeling, standing, stooping, sitting, driving, hearing, talking, vision (close, distant, color, depth perception, adjust focus), and use of hands and fingers. Light lifting of XX lbs. is occasionally needed.
  • Working Conditions:
  • The Regional Channel Manager is a full time salaried exempt position. The regular work hours are 40 hours a week. These hours may vary to accommodate the needs of the department.
  • The Regional Channel Manager works in an automated business office environment with business office equipment including telephones, personal computers, copy machines, and FAX equipment.
  • The Regional Channel Manager is required to drive on the job as needed and is subject to regular MVR checks. He/she must maintain a valid driver’s license and maintain a driving record the meets Company standards for an insurable driver at all times. Any time these conditions are not met, he/she must not drive on the job and must immediately report it to his/her supervisor.
  • The Company is a drug-free workplace. All employees are required to adhere to the Company’s drug-free workplace programs and policies. Pre-employment testing is mandatory along with random testing throughout continued employment.

title: National Standardised Assessments Content Development Officer
description:
This is an Expression of Interest (EOI) opportunity, available on a lateral move basis only. Applications are open to Core Scottish Government employees only.

Job Title – National Standardised Assessments Content Development Officer

Working Arrangement – Staff in roles compatible with hybrid working should aim to spend 40% of their contracted working time working in person at their contractual workplace. More information can be found within Hybrid Working Policy .

Grade – B3

Advert type – level transfer

Duration - Permanent

Eligibility - Expressions of interest are invited from substantive colleagues on level transfer from Core SG only.

Skilled Worker Sponsorship not being offered

Skilled Worker sponsorship is not available for this role. As a result, we are unable to appoint candidates who require Skilled Worker sponsorship now or in the future. Applicants must have an existing and ongoing right to work in the UK.

Equality and Data for Improvement Unit - National Standardised Assessments Content Development Officer

This is an exciting opportunity to work at the heart of the Education Directorate, in a varied and interesting post.

The Equality and Data for Improvement Unit is part of the Workforce, Quality and Wellbeing Division. This post sits in the team responsible for delivering the National Standardised Assessments for Scotland (NSA), which support teachers’ professional judgements on learners’ progress in literacy and numeracy.

The NSA Content Development Officer will work closely with the NSA Content Manager (C1) to deliver Phase 3 of NSA content development, which includes in-housing content creation for both English and Gaelic assessments. The role will contribute to maintaining and improving the quality, inclusivity, and accuracy of assessment items, ensuring alignment with the Curriculum for Excellence and parity of provision for Gaelic Medium Education.

The postholder will have no direct line management responsibilities but will play a key coordinating role, supporting contracted writers, collaborating with Education Scotland Quality Assurance panels, and working alongside the Principal Data Scientist to ensure data-driven content decisions. The role also involves managing the content bank, overseeing metadata, and supporting the integration of images and audio into assessment items.

If you are a Gaelic speaker or have a background in Scottish Education it would be beneficial for this role.

Responsibilities

  • Maintain and update the NSA content bank, ensuring accuracy, relevance, and alignment with the Curriculum for Excellence.

  • Support the NSA Content Manager in planning and delivering the annual content development cycle for both SNSA and MCNG assessments.

  • Manage metadata for all content items and ensure accurate tagging within the content management system.

  • Oversee the integration of images and audio into assessment items, liaising with suppliers and checking outputs for quality.

  • Proofread and edit assessment items and texts to ensure quality, inclusivity, and compliance with style and accessibility standards.

  • Coordinate and provide guidance to contracted content writers, including assisting with training and reviewing drafts.

    • Contribute to bilingual document creation and support Gaelic translation tasks where required.

  • Monitor and report on content development progress, identifying risks and supporting continuous improvement.

  • Assist in the preparation and delivery of quality assurance processes, including collaboration with Education Scotland panels.

  • Participate in content-related meetings, taking minutes and tracking actions to ensure timely delivery.

Success Profile

Success profiles are specific to each job and they include the mix of skills, experience and behaviours candidates will be assessed on.

Experience:

  • Experience in assessment/examination content and or comms/copyrighting


Behaviours:

  1. Communicating and Influencing (level 3)
  2. Working Together (level 3)
  3. Delivering at pace (level 3)
  4. Making effective decisions (level 3)

You can find out more about Success Profiles Behaviours here.

Working Pattern

The post is a full-time role, but staff with different working patterns are invited to apply, and we will assess proposed working patterns against the business requirements for this post.

Our standard hours are 35 hours per week and we offer a range of flexible working options depending on the needs of the role, including Flexi-leave. Scottish Government staff in hybrid-compatible roles should work in-person 40% of the time, either in an office or other agreed work location. If you have specific questions about the role you are applying for, please contact us.

How to Apply

Please submit a CV and an Expression of Interest (maximum 500 words) outlining your suitability for the role, relevant skills and experience, and what you would bring to the team. Please align this to how you meet the behaviours and experience listed in the Success Profile above.

Vacancies close at 11:59pm on the date displayed in the table, unless otherwise stated on the job advert.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can be used to support your application, but all statements and examples provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, and presented as your own) applications will be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action.

Please see our candidate guidance for more information on acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI in recruitment.

If invited for further assessment, this will consist of a light touch interview.

Discussions are to be confirmed.

For any questions relating to your expression of interest please contact alison.macrae2@gov.scot.

Recruitment Principles

As a government organisation, we adhere to the Civil Service Commission Recruitment Principles and we investigate any complaints received in relation to recruitment cases.

About us

The Scottish Government is the devolved government for Scotland. We have responsibility for a wide range of key policy areas including: education, health, the economy, justice, housing and transport. We offer rewarding careers and employ people across Scotland in a wide range of professions and roles.

Our staff are part of the UK Civil Service observing the Civil Service Code and working for Ministers and senior stakeholders to deliver vital public services which improve the lives of the people of Scotland.

We offer a supportive and inclusive working environment along with a wide range of employee benefits. Find out more about what we offer.

As part of the UK Civil Service, we uphold the Civil Service Nationality Rules.

Security checks

Successful candidates must complete the Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS), before they can be appointed. BPSS is comprised of four main pre-employment checks – Identity, Right to work, Employment History and a Criminal Record check (unspent convictions).

You can find out more about BPSS on the UK Government website, or read about the different levels of security checks in our Candidate Guide.

Equality statement

We are committed to equality and inclusion and we aim to recruit a diverse workforce that reflects the population of our nation.

Find out more about our commitment to diversity and how we offer and support recruitment adjustments for anyone who needs them.

Further information

Find out more about our organisation, what we offer staff members and how to apply on our Careers Website.

Read our Candidate Guide for further information on our recruitment and application processes.

title: Missing From Home Worker
description:
| Salary £29,071-£33,119 , Per annum | Permanent, Full Time, 37 hours per week |

Missing from Home Worker

Full Time permanent role within the North covering the areas, Lancaster, Morecambe, Fylde and Wyre

Help Young People Be Heard, Protected and Supported

Are you passionate about making a difference to the lives of vulnerable children and young people? Do you have the confidence to build meaningful relationships, identify risks, and help young people feel safe and supported?

We're looking for a dedicated and compassionate Missing from Home Worker to join our Children's Services team in Lancashire. This is a rewarding opportunity to work directly with children and young people who have been reported missing from home, helping them share their experiences, understand the factors influencing their behaviour, and access the support they need to stay safe.

About the Role

As a Missing from Home Worker, you will play a vital role in safeguarding some of Lancashire's most vulnerable children and young people. Working both independently and as part of a multi-agency team, you will undertake Return Home Interviews with children following missing episodes, ensuring their voices are heard and their experiences inform future planning and support.

You'll meet children and young people in their homes and communities, using a relationship-based approach to build trust, explore concerns, identify risks and protective factors, and make recommendations that improve outcomes. Your work will directly contribute to safeguarding children from harm, building resilience, and helping them achieve their full potential.

This is a fast-paced and varied role where no two days are the same. You'll need to be organised, analytical, and able to work within clear timescales, completing key interventions within 72 hours of allocation.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Carrying out Return Home Interviews with children and young people following missing episodes.
  • Building positive, trusting relationships that encourage children and young people to share their experiences.
  • Identifying risks, strengths, and the push and pull factors influencing missing behaviour.
  • Producing high-quality assessments, reports, and case recordings.
  • Working collaboratively with families, carers, schools, social workers, police, health services and other partner agencies.
  • Supporting children, young people and families to access services and opportunities that meet their needs.
  • Planning and delivering group work programmes for parents and carers.
  • Advocating for children and young people, ensuring their views influence decisions that affect them.
  • Challenging barriers, discrimination and poor practice to promote positive outcomes.

What We're Looking For

We're seeking someone who:

  • Is passionate about improving outcomes for children and young people.
  • Has excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Can work independently, manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Is confident assessing risk and analysing complex information.
  • Values partnership working and understands the importance of multi-agency collaboration.
  • Is creative, resilient and committed to child-centred practice.
  • Champions diversity, inclusion and anti-discriminatory practice.

Why Join Us?

At Lancashire Children's Services, our vision is simple:

Children, young people and their families are safe, healthy and achieve their full potential.

By joining our team, you'll have the opportunity to make a genuine difference every day, helping children and young people:

  • Stay safe from harm and build resilience.
  • Have their voices heard.
  • Access the right support at the right time.
  • Enjoy healthier, happier lives.
  • Achieve positive futures within their communities.

Additional Information

  • This is an essential car user role.
  • Some evening work may occasionally be required.
  • The role is managed by the Team Manager and supported by a Senior Social Worker within a highly committed and experienced team

The post you are applying for is covered by the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975 (as amended in 2013). If successful you will be required to apply to the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) for a 'disclosure'. Further information can be found on the 'Our Recruitment Process' tab.

You will be required to provide a car for use in connection with the duties of this post and must be insured for business use. However, we may consider you if you cannot drive because of a disability.

In return Lancashire County Council offers a range of benefits, which can be found on LCC Vacancies website.We reserve the right to close down a vacancy early, before the closing date, if we receive sufficient applications.

Local Government Reorganisation

The Government has confirmed that local government across Lancashire will be reorganised, with the current 15 councils being replaced by four new unitary councils covering North, South, East and West Lancashire from April 2028.

If you are successful in your application, you will initially join Lancashire County Council. However, as part of the planned transition, your employment will transfer to one of the new unitary councils from April 2028, subject to the implementation of the reorganisation and relevant employment legislation.

Throughout this period, our focus remains on delivering excellent services to our communities. By joining us now, you'll play an important role in shaping the future of local government and helping to build a strong new organisation that will serve residents for years to come.

title: Instrument & Controls Technician
description:
Instrument and Controls Technician

This position is in the Savannah, GA area.

Georgia Power is seeking a skilled and dedicated Instrument and Controls Technician to join our team at Plant McIntosh Combustion Turbine Site. The energy industry is experiencing unprecedented growth, particularly in the Coastal Georgia region, and we are excited to be a part of the solution.

Plant McIntosh Combustion Turbine Site is in Rincon, GA just outside of the Savannah, GA area and is a “black start” resource for Georgia Power and the Southern Company electric system. McIntosh CT also serves as a quick response peaking plant that provides the necessary generation and transmission support for the area during peak load demands. The site has Eight (8) ABB 11N combustion turbines capable of running on natural gas and fuel oil. As an I&C Technician, you will play an integral role in the performance of our generating units, contributing to the production of energy that is vital to our community.

The successful candidate will be responsible for performing technical and analytical services essential to the control systems and associated equipment (electronic, pneumatic, and hydraulic) for the operation of McIntosh CT. This includes troubleshooting, maintaining, and repairing control systems and instrumentation, such as GE MarkVIe turbine control, Allen Bradley Control Logix, control circuits, power circuits, control valves, DC control circuits, and control devices. The successful candidate will also be responsible for maintaining transmitters, valves, and meters, including temperature, pressure, level, and flow devices, etc.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Perform troubleshooting, maintenance, and repair tasks on control systems, including MarkVIe and Allen Bradley Control Logix, to ensure optimal performance and reliability.

  • Maintain and repair electronic, pneumatic, and hydraulic controls, ensuring accurate monitoring and diagnostics of plant equipment.

  • Inspect, test, calibrate, and repair various electrical circuits and instrumentation, including transmitters, valves, and meters.

  • Diagnose and resolve issues related to temperature, pressure, level, and flow devices to ensure accurate readings and reliable operation.

  • Utilize MAXIMO® for tracking maintenance activities, inventory management, and work order processing.

  • Collaborate with plant operations to optimize system performance and ensure compliance with safety and environmental regulations.

  • Implement preventative maintenance programs to minimize downtime and enhance system reliability.

  • Utilize a variety of hand tools, power tools, measurement, and test equipment in the performance of duties.

  • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance plant efficiency and reliability.

  • Ensure adherence to all safety protocols and procedures while performing maintenance and troubleshooting tasks.

Qualifications:

  • Two-year technical degree from a certified technical institution or military equivalent required.

  • Proven experience as an Instrument and Controls Technician, preferably in a power plant or industrial setting is preferred.

  • Proficiency in troubleshooting and maintaining the MarkVIe turbine control system and Allen Bradley Control Logix systems is desired.

  • Strong knowledge of electrical circuits and instrumentation, including transmitters, valves, and meters. preferred

  • Familiarity with Maximo or similar maintenance management systems is a plus.

  • Experience in Combustion Turbine (CT) and/or Combined Cycle (CC) plant operation is preferred.

  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

  • Commitment to safety and adherence to regulatory standards.

  • Must be able to interpret electrical prints; functional logic diagram experience is a plus.

  • Candidate must have a working knowledge of Microsoft Office computer applications.

  • Must be able to walk and work on grating that may include high elevations.

  • Must be able to support a 24/7 work schedule, including weekend and holiday shift work when necessary.

Behavioral Attributes:

  • The successful candidate must support the Company's "Safety Excellence" philosophy.

  • Candidate must exemplify “Our Values” and be a team player with a positive attitude.

  • Incumbent must be highly motivated, value continuous learning, and be adaptable to a changing work environment.

  • Effective oral and written communication skills; demonstrates initiative and possesses the ability to multi-task.

Working Conditions:

  • Must be able to work in a power plant environment, which may include exposure to noise, heat, and other challenging conditions.

  • Ability to work flexible hours, including weekends and holidays, as required.

  • Physical ability to perform tasks that may involve lifting, climbing, and working in confined spaces.

Other Requirements:

  • Successful completion of the Technical Aptitude Test for Instrument & Controls Technicians.

  • Southern Company is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive work environment.

If this job is determined to be a critical job, limitations for transferring internally within the Company may apply for a set period of time. If applicable, details will be shared during the selection process.

title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
About GeneralMind

GeneralMind builds AI Systems of Action for complex enterprise workflows. We deploy AI employees that automate messy operational handovers across supply chains - processing orders, validating invoices, coordinating suppliers, and handling exceptions directly on top of enterprise systems like SAP, Oracle, JDE, and Dynamics.

Our platform combines AI agents, operational context graphs, and real transaction data to achieve Autopilot-grade automation in real operational environments.

We work closely with leading global companies across manufacturing, retail, and logistics to deploy AI into mission-critical workflows.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to help own and evolve the core backend architecture of the company.

You will work directly with the founders on systems that orchestrate real operational workflows across emails, documents, humans, databases, and ERP systems. The work sits at the intersection of backend engineering, workflow orchestration, AI infrastructure, and reliability engineering.

This is not a feature-factory role. We want someone who can hold large parts of the system in their head, make strong architectural decisions, and raise the quality bar for the team.

What You'll Do

Backend Ownership

  • Own the backend end-to-end: service architecture, API design, reliability posture, and long-term technical direction.
  • Be the person who knows how everything fits together - and who other engineers come to when they're not sure where something belongs.
  • Set the bar on code quality, service boundaries, and shared abstractions across the engineering team.
  • Make foundational decisions with conviction, document the reasoning, and evolve them as the system grows.

Python Services & Production Systems

  • Design for failure: retries, timeouts, graceful degradation, and recovery paths built in from the start.
  • Write code that is easy to operate - observable, testable, and straightforward to debug at 2am.
  • Understand the runtime, not just the framework. Know when the problem is the code, the config, or the infrastructure.

Workflow Engineering & Temporal

  • Design and build durable workflows using Temporal - long-running processes, async coordination, saga patterns.
  • Own workflow observability: know when a workflow is stuck, degraded, or silently wrong before a customer notices.
  • Think carefully about idempotency, failure modes, and replay semantics - not just the happy path.
  • Evolve workflows without breaking running instances; manage versioning with intention.

Reliability & Systems Thinking

  • Detect regressions before they become incidents; build the tooling to catch them early.
  • Own the operational posture of the services you build: alerting, runbooks, on-call readiness.
  • Identify structural debt before it compounds; propose refactors that are thoughtful, not just correct.

What we are looking for

  • Experience: 6+ years building and operating backend systems in Python, with clear ownership of production services - not just feature delivery.
  • Python depth: Non-negotiable. You make deliberate choices about async vs. sync, framework selection, and performance tradeoffs. You know the language well enough to have opinions.
  • Temporal or equivalent: You've used Temporal (or a comparable workflow engine) in production. You understand durable execution, not just task queues.
  • Reliability instinct: Idempotency, retries, and observability are part of how you design, not afterthoughts.
  • End-to-end ownership: You're comfortable being the person who holds the full backend picture. You identify what's broken or missing before you're asked, and you don't leave the system worse than you found it.
  • A real spike: We're a strong team with broad coverage. What we're hiring for is someone who brings a 10x improvement in an area we're currently underinvested in. That might be workflow systems, data infrastructure, AI-native backend patterns, or deep domain expertise. We don't know exactly what shape it takes - but you should know what yours is, and be able to articulate why it matters.

title: Substation Control Design – Engineer/Designer (Birmingham, AL)
description:
Substation Control Design – Engineer/Designer
Southern Company Services Technical Shared Services – Substation Engineering
This position will be located at The Energy Center in Birmingham, AL

JOB SUMMARY

The Substation Control Design Engineer/Designer is responsible for designing protective relay and control schemes utilizing AutoCad and advanced microprocessor-based relay systems for both greenfield and brownfield projects.
