title: Senior Project Associate (Livelihoods)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is the leading inter-governmental organization in the field of migration and works closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all and does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.
IOM is a major actor in post-conflict recovery and reconstruction, and as such is heavily involved in livelihoods development and job creation programmes. IOM’s strengths lie in its field presence around the country and operational capacity to rebuild community infrastructure, conduct vocational and other trainings, provide grant funding at local level to support business development, and support a variety of other areas key to recovery.
Under the overall supervision of Head of Livelihoods Technical team and the direct supervision of the National Project Officer – Livelihoods, the incumbent will be responsible for supporting programmes related to livelihoods portfolio under the area of responsibility. The post will be based in Erbil, Iraq, with travel/roving to various regions/governorates within Iraq as needed to support livelihoods activities and teams.

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Support the National Project Officer – Livelihoods through the development and updating of training materials for beneficiaries and target groups, including business development, employability, labour standards, registration, banking and other relevant livelihoods training materials.

  • Conduct regular monitoring, spot-check visits and pre/post assessments of trainings and livelihoods activities, and provide feedback to technical and operational teams on areas for improvement.

  • Conduct regular capacity-building sessions for operations teams on training materials, livelihoods tools, systems and processes.

  • In coordination with the National Project Officer – Livelihoods, support the development and updating of programme tools and coordinate with Information Management colleagues for the integration of these tools into relevant information management systems.

  • Travel to project sites across Iraq, as required, to monitor beneficiaries and target groups who have received IOM livelihoods assistance and ensure that activities are implemented in accordance with livelihoods guidelines, tools, policies and procedures.

  • In coordination with the National Project Officer – Livelihoods, conduct quality control and quality assurance of livelihoods activities, including monitoring, verification, mentorship, community feedback mechanisms, community engagement and other relevant livelihoods interventions.

  • Support coordination with external stakeholders, including government entities, local authorities, NGOs, private sector partners and other relevant actors, to facilitate alignment of livelihoods interventions with national policies and local development priorities.

  • Track and monitor conducted trainings and relevant livelihoods activities in the system, perform quality checks, identify errors, communicate them to teams, support teams to correct mistakes and report system issues or errors to relevant colleagues to improve system tools.

  • Prepare reports, briefs and overviews on trainings, sessions and livelihoods activities for internal and external use, including reporting to stakeholders, donors and other relevant entities.

  • Review and quality check uploaded business plans, verification documents and other relevant programme documentation under the livelihoods portfolio.

  • In coordination with the National Project Officer – Livelihoods, monitor, compile and submit regular progress reports on activities and tools developed by the livelihoods team.

  • In coordination with the National Project Officer – Livelihoods, monitor programme indicators and work closely with operational teams to ensure that livelihoods activities are on track and implemented in line with approved workplans.

  • Assist in the internal coordination of referrals to other units and divisions, as relevant to livelihoods programming.

  • Support field teams to mainstream gender, disability, protection, accountability to affected populations and other cross-cutting issues into livelihoods programming.

  • Document and provide feedback to field teams on updated changes in livelihoods SOPs, technical guidance, tools and implementation guidelines.

  • Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the supervisor.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Political or Social Sciences, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights, Law or related fields from an accredited academic institution with four years of relevant professional experience.

  • School diploma with six years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, national/international institutions, United Nations agencies and non-governmental organizations;

  • Experience in working with migrants, refugees, internally displaced persons, victims of trafficking and other vulnerable groups; and,

  • Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

  • Experience in coordinating with local authorities, service providers, community representatives, and other operational stakeholders is desirable.

  • Experience in data collection, consolidation, reporting, and use of implementation tracking tools is desirable.

Skills

  • Position specific skills, for example:

  • Knowledge of livelihoods, recovery, resilience, or community-based programming approaches.

  • Good understanding of field implementation, operational follow-up, and monitoring processes.

  • Ability to review activity documentation, track implementation progress, and support timely reporting.

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities under tight deadlines.

  • Strong communication and coordination skills, with the ability to work effectively with colleagues and stakeholders from diverse backgrounds.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

  • Knowledge of data management, reporting tools, and information tracking systems is an advantage.

Languages

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position,

Fluency in English is required

Arabic and Kurdish are advantage Languages

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.
  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.
  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.

Notes

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Junior Software Engineer
description:
Junior Software Engineer

Location: London or Leeds - Hybrid

Closing date: Tuesday 27/10/2026

The role..

We are looking for an enthusiastic Junior Software Engineer with at least 2 years of commercial experience to join our software engineering function in CST on a 1-year fixed-term contract to assist with an ongoing project.

In this role, you will focus heavily on cloud infrastructure and platform configuration, helping us replicate, adapt, and deploy serverless functions (e.g., AWS Lambdas), services, and deployment pipelines across our content supply chain. While the primary focus is on infrastructure and CI/CD workflows, our core services are built in Scala, so you will also work with existing codebases to replicate services, make updates, and integrate cloud components. There may also be some work to enhance our existing Scala-based product(s).

To ensure success in this role, you should have an analytical mindset and a logical approach to problem-solving. You will be supported by experienced engineers and receive guidance and mentorship to help you get up to speed quickly and deliver impactful work during your time with us.

The team..

Content Supply and Distribution (CS&D) is a key group within ITV’s Media & Entertainment business that is responsible for managing ITV’s content and data from source to screen across linear and VoD supply chains. The Content Supply Technology (CST) group develops, integrates and maintains the underpinning technology platforms, as well as the supporting functions of business analysis, architecture and project management. All this enables us to deliver ITVs famous and popular content from its multiple sources to our online platforms, to our B2B partners and to ITV’s family of linear TV channels.

As a department we work closely with our colleagues in the ITV business teams and with our closely related operational teams who are responsible for delivering our channels and content reliably, just in time, day in-day out.

Our teams build the technology that brings great content into ITV ready for broadcast, streaming and partner distribution. From handling video files and sourcing metadata for content to scheduling and checking compliance, our systems ensure millions of views get to enjoy their favourite shows.

Main responsibilities

As a Junior Software Engineer, you will:

  • Write Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using Terraform to provision and manage cloud resources on Amazon Web Services (AWS).
  • Build, update, and maintain CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions to support an ad-hoc, continuous deployment delivery model.
  • Replicate, adapt, and deploy microservices and serverless components (e.g., AWS Lambdas) across different supply chain products.
  • Troubleshoot and diagnose production issues using observability platforms such as Grafana and Prometheus.
  • Maintain high system quality and reliability with a strong testing mindset, ensuring infrastructure and service changes never break existing functionality.
  • Work directly inside existing Scala/JVM codebases using modern IDEs to update, copy, and integrate microservices alongside senior engineers.
  • Collaborate closely with team members through pair programming, knowledge sharing, and active communication within an Agile team.

Skills you’ll need (minimum criteria)

  • Minimum 2 years of commercial experience in a software or infrastructure engineering role within a production environment.
  • Hands-on experience writing and managing CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions.
  • Practical experience or clear exposure to Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) and AWS cloud services (e.g., Lambdas, IAM, ECS, S3).
  • Experience (commercial or personal projects) in functional programming concepts e.g. Scala, Java Streams API, Haskell, or similar.
  • Comfort and fluency working inside an IDE (e.g. IntelliJ IDEA, VS Code) to read, edit, and navigate codebases.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and a logical, step-by-step approach to identifying root causes.
  • A rigorous testing mindset, understanding how to verify changes safely before and after deployment.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the confidence to ask questions, take direction, and learn rapidly.

Other things we’re looking for (key criteria)

  • Hands-on experience with observability tools such as Grafana or Prometheus.
  • Understanding of CI/CD concepts and modern deployment models (e.g. ad-hoc, automated, continuous delivery vs. scheduled releases).
  • Experience or familiarity with Scala in a commercial environment, or personal projects built using Scala.
  • Familiarity with microservices architecture, serverless concepts, and event-driven systems.
  • Understanding of automated testing strategies for both code and infrastructure.

title: Senior Wellness & Fitness Specialist
description:
We are seeking a passionate and creative Senior Wellness and Fitness Trainer to design and lead an engaging, whole-person wellness program for residents in our senior living community. description:

Hormel Foods Corporation

About Hormel Foods

Hormel Foods Corporation, based in Austin, Minnesota, is a global branded food company with over $12 billion in annual revenue. Its brands include PLANTERS®, SKIPPY®, SPAM®, HORMEL® NATURAL CHOICE®, APPLEGATE®, WHOLLY®, HORMEL® BLACK LABEL®, COLUMBUS®, JENNIE-O® and more than 30 other beloved brands. For more information, visit .

JOB DESCRIPTION:

This packaging role organizes, plans, directs and conducts research in the area of packaging technologies that will lead to improved and new innovative and creative packaging applications in support of company goals and objectives. It provides technical advice and assistance to professional and non-professional personnel.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Identifies, facilitates, devises and conducts research in the area of packaging which leads to the development and implementation of new packaging systems for the company. This involves maintaining competency in cutting edge packaging technology and broad packaging theory, and researching the feasibility of using this technology in conjunction with our products.

  • Investigates, recommends and implements packaging cost saving programs by evaluating new enhancements made to packaging materials and/or new design considerations with the planned goal of minimizing the costs associated with our products.

  • Fulfills the role as a technical service/troubleshooter when more broadly defined packaging problems at our facilities are beyond the scope of the plant/corporate personnel. May serve as a resource and advisor to other Packaging Scientists and personnel within the company.

  • Develops and plans systems for improving packaging efficiencies within the corporation. This includes the entering and managing of all packaging specifications for our company’s products and may also include development of software and catalogue systems for collecting critical data regarding packaging materials and package attributes.

  • Facilitates practical applications of packaging technology requiring direct interaction with other areas of the company such as Engineering, Operations, Marketing and Purchasing etc. Oversees the development and integration of packaging technologies with the many vendors and suppliers who work with the company.

  • Coordinates and plans specific projects effectively, on a daily basis, with the group’s Research Technicians.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Level of position offered (Associate Packaging Scientist, Packaging Scientist, or Senior Packaging Scientist) will be determined based on candidate’s skill set and experience.

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Packaging Engineering or related field

  • Project management skills with the ability to lead and run projects smoothly.

  • Demonstrated self-motivation, initiative, and creativity

  • Ability to work both independently and in a team setting.

  • An understanding of basic scientific principles.

  • Strong analytical, time management, and record keeping skills.

  • Excellent interpersonal skills including good team building skills.

  • Excellent written and verbal communications skills with ability to effectively present technical concepts to a nontechnical audience

  • Must be a Citizen or National of the United States, a lawful, permanent resident, or have authorization to work in the United States

  • Applicants must not now, or in the future, require sponsorship for an employment visa

Preferred

  • Packaging Equipment and/or Processing experience

  • Knowledge in the area of Package Sustainability including Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR).

Location: Austin, Minnesota (Company HQ) OR Northbrook, IL (R&D Office Location)

The base hiring pay range for the role is between $64,400 - $137,300 per year, and your actual base pay within that range will depend upon a variety of factors including, but not limited to, job-related knowledge, skill set, level of experience, and geographic market location.

BENEFITS: Other components of Hormel Foods' total compensation package include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, discretionary annual merit increases, bonuses and profit sharing, 401(k) with employer match, stock purchase plan, paid time off, free two-year community/technical college tuition for children of employees, and more.

title: ​​ Movement Operations Associate (Beneficiary-Facing Activities)​
description:
Since the inception of IOM in 1951, Movement Operations have been and continue to be a fundamental pillar of the Organization’s work. The organized movement of persons in need of international migration assistance is a primary mandate of the Organization and a cornerstone of IOM’s operations. Movement Operations Units in various IOM Country Offices, coordinated under the Resettlement and Movement Management (RMM) Unit in the Division of Movement, Resettlement and Labour Pathways (MRLP) at IOM’s Headquarters, are responsible for all aspects of travel for migrants and refugees under IOM’s auspices, in accordance with the various framework agreements with resettlement and receiving Governments and partners across the spectrum of the Organization's programmes.

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Programmes, the direct supervision of National Protection Officer , the Movement Operations Associate, is responsible for the following duties and responsibilities.

  1. Undertake beneficiary-facing activities under the Field Support and Data Processing Pillar within IOM’s movement operations, which occur at various stages of refugee resettlement, relocation, humanitarian admissions, family reunification, voluntary repatriation, and other emergency humanitarian initiatives conducted by land, air, or water. When necessary, monitor and provide guidance to teams of Movement Operations Assistants in performing related activities.
  2. Coordinate field support activities with relevant units, agencies and service providers to assist beneficiaries in an assigned area or areas, such as at an airport, seaport, transit center, third-party facility, camp-based operations or sub-office to ensure beneficiary movements are conducted safely and appropriately. If required, provide assistance for extended periods and during overnight periods and weekends, ensuring the needs of individuals are met throughout their stay.
  3. Coordinate transportation of beneficiaries to and from designated consolidation points, locations, and facilities, working with relevant units and service providers to help ensure that vulnerable individuals are assisted in a manner that ensures their safety, security and comfort.

  4. Assist in timely and appropriate provision of food and other essential items to beneficiaries during IOM movement operations. Collaborate with the relevant IOM units and service providers to ensure that assistance meets established standards of quality.

  5. Ensure individuals with special needs or equipment receive appropriate support. In particular, ensure the proper handling of sensitive cases in accordance with IOM’s policies, and existing institutional guidance, including the assistance to unaccompanied and separated migrant children and at-risk cases.

  6. Work with units and departments and beneficiaries on pre-departure formalities such as processing of travel documents and exit permits in close coordination with relevant external partner agencies, and authorities.

  7. Enter and update relevant data in the appropriate systems and ensure vulnerable individuals are assisted in a manner that ensures their safety, security and comfort. Report all issues immediately to the appropriate supervisor(s).

  8. Provide selection mission support and/or interpretation services for individuals at

    airports, in transit centers, camps, consolidation points and third-party facilities or during transport by air, ground or water.

  9. Upon request from government agencies, provide visa applicants with application assistance such as initiating contacts, scheduling appointments, capturing biometrics, filling the relevant forms, and collecting relating documents.

  10. Undertake duty travel as required and delegated to participate in meetings, trainings and other programme activities.

  11. Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of applicable SOPs, related systems and databases, and IOM Standards of Conduct. Maintain and ensure the confidentiality and integrity of all relevant paperwork in line with SOPs, Standards of Conduct and relevant data protection rules.

  12. Uphold RMM Protection Mainstreaming Minimum Standards while carrying out all duties and responsibilities and demonstrate the ability to remain professional, impartial and unbiased during all interactions with migrants and colleagues per the IOM Standards of Conduct and instruction on the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA). Alert the supervisor or management of any non-compliance to SOPs, RMM Protection Mainstreaming Minimum Standards or IOM Standards of Conduct by IOM personnel or partners.\

  13. Perform other related duties as assigned.

EDUCATION

  • High School diploma with five years of relevant experience; or,

  • Bachelor’s degree in Social Science, International Relations, Regional Studies or a related field from an accredited academic institution with three years of relevant professional experience.

EXPERIENCE

  • Prior Movement Operations, transportation-related and/or management experience

  • Work experience in programs including movement operations component, particularly in resettlement programs

  • Experience with communicating with beneficiaries.

  • Past experience with Movement Operations-related databases and systems (including iGATOR, MiMOSA, SAR and Amadeus) is a strong advantage.

Demonstrated knowledge with handling sensitive information and personal data.

  • Experience with guiding and leading junior staff members.

SKILLS

  • Computer/software literate with good knowledge in Microsoft Office.

  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills.

  • Attention to detail and ability to organise.

  • Self-motivated, objective driven and able to use own initiative and work under pressure with minimum supervision.

title: Reliability Technician, Condition Monitoring
description:

Sedgman is proud to offer the position of Reliability Technician, Condition Monitoring to join our team in Mackay. Working within our Reliability and Asset Management team, you will play a key role in supporting clients across the mining and resources sector through the collection, analysis and interpretation of condition monitoring data to improve asset performance, reliability and operational efficiency.

This position offers a balanced mix of field and office-based work, typically involving three days per week on client sites and two days in the Mackay office, allowing you to combine hands-on condition monitoring activities with technical analysis and reporting. To support regular travel to site, a fully maintained company vehicle and fuel card are provided for work-related travel.

Key Accountabilities

  • Conduct condition monitoring activities including vibration analysis, thermography and oil analysis across client sites.
  • Collect, analyse and interpret condition monitoring data to identify equipment defects, failure trends and reliability risks.
  • Prepare high-quality technical reports and recommendations for clients within established timeframes.
  • Work closely with site maintenance personnel, supervisors and client representatives to support reliability improvements.
  • Provide technical insights to assist clients in improving equipment performance and reducing unplanned downtime.
  • Maintain accurate records and reporting through company systems and condition monitoring platforms.
  • Ensure all activities are completed in accordance with safety, quality and operational requirements.
  • Operate autonomously in the field whilst maintaining a high level of professionalism and customer service.

What You Bring

  • VCAT Level 1 Certification (minimum requirement) - VCAT Level 2 Certification highly regarded.
  • Previous experience as a Condition Monitoring Technician, Reliability Technician or similar role.
  • Demonstrated experience in vibration analysis and condition monitoring data interpretation.
  • Experience with thermography and oil analysis programs.
  • Strong technical reporting and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and effectively manage site-based activities.
  • Proven relationship-building skills and a client-focused approach.
  • Experience working within mining, mineral processing, heavy industry or fixed plant environments will be highly regarded.

What We Can Offer You

  • Flexible work arrangements with a balance of site and office-based work, typically averaging three days on site and two days in the office.

  • Company vehicle and fuel card provided for work-related travel, including travel between home, the office and client sites.

  • Overtime opportunities during periods of increased workload.

  • A focus on your professional development and opportunities to grow your career within Sedgman.

  • A collaborative focus on continuous improvement, innovation and safety.

  • A friendly, supportive and social team environment with regular team events and activities.

How to Join Our Team

If this sounds like an opportunity you would be interested in, please submit your CV by clicking "Apply" now.

Please note you must hold a current Australian Driver's Licence and have the right to work in Australia.

title: Peoples Bank Fraud Analyst
description:
Fraud Analyst

Barkley Financial Center- Laurel Building | Hybrid Work from Home (3 days per week in office)

Bellingham, WA

Monday – Friday 8:00 am to 5:00 pm | 40 hours per week


A Day in Your Life at Peoples Bank:

As a Fraud Analyst, you will be responsible for completing daily fraud monitoring and fraud investigations. You will maintain record keeping for the prevention and reaction to fraud and losses and evaluate the effectiveness of the fraud monitoring process and reporting. You will be providing fraud support to the entire Bank by responding to notifications of suspicious activity and directing actions to limit losses. In addition, you will be accountable to report fraud risk and escalate fraud events to the Fraud Investigations Manager daily.


Your Primary Responsibilities Would Include:

  • Monitoring and acting on daily transaction alerts to mitigate customer or bank losses and complying with the Bank Secrecy Act as well as providing direct support to customers who are victims of fraud.
  • Completing daily Currency Transaction Reporting (CTR), OFAC and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) processing.
  • Responding to the department helpdesk in accordance with the established service level agreement.
  • Supporting security device management, granting access requests, and being a resource for branch questions.
  • Completing research for fraud related subpoenas, primarily production of surveillance pictures, and acting as a liaison for law enforcement on fraud cases.
  • Acting in a timely manner to reported fraud or suspicious account activity, directing branch or other staff on specific actions to limit loss.
  • Working with customers, branches, and when appropriate, Adult Protective Services in instances of suspected elder financial abuse.
  • Maintaining fraud records according to established criteria including fraud communications, BSA retention, and reporting of Verafin case files.
  • Analyzing effectiveness of current fraud processes against actual events and providing input to the department manager.

title: National Project Officer (Livelihoods)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates as well as external women candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Division, PRSD and the direct supervision of the Livelihoods Senior Programme Coordinator, the Livelihoods National Project Officer will lead the technical teams implementing the Individual Livelihoods Assistance (ILA) programme, the Employment for Public Works (EPW) programme, the Graduation Approach (GA) programmes. The Livelihoods National Project Officer closely coordinates with the Operations teams for implementation activities.

  1. Coordinate the overall technical implementation of the project including the oversight of the financial, logistical, administrative and technical aspects in accordance with IOM’s policies, practices and global standards as well as relevant requirements, guidelines and grant agreements.

  2. Monitor project implementation according to the work plan; document and evaluate results; identify the causes of deviations and bottlenecks and recommend and implement corrective actions.

  3. Promote and contribute to the integration and mainstreaming of gender, protection, human rights and other pertinent cross-cutting issues into programme implementation.

  4. Develop monitoring, evaluation, and reporting tools. Contribute to information management including awareness raising and visibility, press releases, website updates and other relevant information-sharing materials.

  5. Identify potential areas for project development and contribute to the development of new projects by selecting and summarizing background information, assessing the local context and drafting segments of project proposals.

  6. Participate in the development and adjustment of methodologies, contingency plans, approaches and standard operations procedures to respond to emerging challenges in the county through a consultative process with other relevant parties in the office.

  7. Coordinate the elaboration and dissemination of reports for donors, government and other relevant stakeholders ensuring timely submission and compliance with donor and IOM requirements.

  8. Liaise and coordinate with government entities, implementing partners, United Nation agencies, civil society, donors and other stakeholders.

  9. Plan, develop, organize and deliver capacity building activities to build capacity of staff, partners, government officials, and other humanitarian actors.

  10. Participate in relevant conferences, working groups, workshops, steering committees, working groups, and other forums

  11. Supervise, train, and guide project staff.

  12. Undertake duty travel as required related to project implementation and monitoring.

  13. Perform other related duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Political or Social Sciences, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights, Law or related fields from an accredited academic institution with four years of relevant professional experience; or,

  • Master’s degree in the above-mentioned fields with two years of relevant professional experience;

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Prior work experience leading livelihoods initiatives for international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organisations;

  • Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, national/international institutions, United Nations agencies and non-governmental organizations;

  • Experience in working with migrants, refugees, internally displaced persons, victims of trafficking and other vulnerable groups; and,

  • Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

Skills

  • In depth knowledge of the broad range of livelihoods related subject areas dealt with by the Organization; and,

  • Knowledge of Governmental livelihoods programmes

  • Knowledge of financial rules and regulations.

Languages

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position,

Fluency in English is required

Arabic and Kurdish are advantage Languages

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.
  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.
  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.

Notes

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Product Owner
description:

While the role is primarily internally focused, some aspects of the role do support client-facing activity., including client meetings and presentations and dealing with an extended stakeholder landscape.

Our engineering team is diverse in people, technology, and processes, offering a dynamic environment for an experienced leader to drive technical excellence, innovation, and best practice within the internal product portfolio.

A snapshot of your day

  • Acting as the primary interface to funnel both business and technical enhancements and be the key point of contact to analyse requirements for work and communicate with the business agreed pathways and details around the products.
  • Incorporating new working practices, standards and policies introduced by Howden and ensuring maturity and standards are kept, maintained and reportable (in conjunction with the Engineering Managers and senior management)
  • Analyse queries received and manage workload and tickets according to complexity, business priority and team priorities. Where complex issues are raised, analyse and document solutions for resolutions.
  • Agree, assign and raise tickets for features and epics (in ADO) and maintain roadmaps using Product Plan. Resolve fewer complex issues within agreed SLAs
  • Agree and request resource allocation as required with a view to delivering against agreed metrics and KPIs
  • Oversee the design, development, testing and release of software using engineering best practices, and coordinate work with other managers, across different areas and domains
  • Work close with Product Owners and delivery leads to build roadmaps that the teams will deliver against
  • Take an active role in the implementation of key business project developments and process improvement.
  • Drive design and planning activities by removing ambiguities, resolving dependency questions and work with the team to provide engineering estimates and delivery

We would love to hear from you if you have:

  • Previous experience in a similar role e.g., Product Owner, QA Analyst etc with experience with back-end products
  • Experience in a Microsoft tech stack and be proficient using ADO (Azure DevOps)
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and oral and able to seek and deliver clarity and transparency
  • Ability to build great relationships with the engineering team and the wider stakeholder group and engineering organisation to contribute to company-wide best managerial and technical practices and standards
  • Ability to manage complex requirements with a complex set of internal stakeholders.
  • Ability to positively challenge and influence.
  • Good organisational skills and be adaptable to change and the unforeseen
  • Ability and desire to grow the understanding of Agile within the product set you manage and own

Desirable but not essential:

  • Previous experience working in the pensions space, consulting or another highly complex back-end environment is desirable

title: Manager, Laboratory
description:
Manages, plans and coordinates all activities within a laboratory. Maintains quality and timeliness of all laboratory operations within budgetary guidelines.
  • Manages laboratory services, including workflow, administrative procedures, operations and strategic planning in order to maintain an efficient laboratory environment.
  • Ensures appropriate lab compliance with accrediting agency regulations.
  • Develops and implements quality control procedures and ensures documentation are in compliance and up to date with ISO guidelines.
  • Establishes goals, and schedules for the laboratory.
  • Oversees laboratory safety policies, implements training, and monitors department for compliance.
  • Coordinates laboratory administration; manages and authorizes all purchasing expenditures for supplies and equipment; ensures that all required equipment is maintained and properly functioning.
  • Management duties include interviewing, selecting and training of employees; planning and directing work; appraising productivity and efficiency for the purpose of recommending promotions or other changes in their status; handles complaints and grievances and administers discipline when necessary.
  • Performs all other duties as assigned.
  • Knowledge of molecular biology techniques, with an emphasis on protein expression and purification from a variety of recombinant sources is required. Experience with membrane protein expression and purification is preferred.

  • Experience with sample preparation for structural biology techniques, including cryo-electron microscopy (single-particle analysis and/or tomography) and X-ray crystallography, is preferred but not required.

  • Experience with laser operation, alignment, and safety is preferred but not required.

  • Comfortable with the changes associated with evolving research requirements and the need to learn and troubleshoot new approaches to solve key problems.

  • Knowledge of laboratory techniques.
  • Experience documenting and following procedures/protocols.
  • Knowledge of procedures, instruments in use, and quality control measures within the laboratory.
  • Experience operating and maintaining laboratory equipment and conducting regular assessments to record the lab equipment's performance.
  • Ability to operate in a fast paced environment with established time constraints.
  • Ability to maintain strict protocols of all confidential or sensitive information.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Bachelors degree is required.

title: Snow Tube Park Attendant
description:
Department: Snow Tube Park Operations
Reports To: Snow Tube Park Supervisor / Area Manager
Employment Type: Winter Seasonal
Schedule: Full-Time (5+ shifts/week) or Part-Time; must be available weekends and holidays

Job Overview

The Snow Tube Park Team Member helps provide a safe, fun, and positive experience for guests visiting the Seven Oaks Snow Tube Park. This outdoor, high-energy position assists with the operation of the tubing lanes and handle tow system while maintaining safe loading, unloading, and tubing areas.

Team members interact directly with guests, provide instructions, monitor tubing activity, maintain snow conditions, check tickets, and assist with daily setup and maintenance of the park. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys working outdoors, interacting with people, and staying active throughout their shift.

Essential Job Functions

Snow Tube Park Operations & Guest Safety

  • Greet guests in a welcoming, positive, and professional manner.
  • Provide clear instructions regarding tubing procedures, park rules, and safe use of the tubing area.
  • Safely control the flow of guests and tubes down assigned tubing lanes.
  • Ensure guests are properly positioned in their tubes before being dispatched.
  • Assist guests with entering and exiting tubing lanes and runout areas.
  • Assist guests with loading and unloading the conveyor surface lift.
  • Monitor tubing lanes and runout areas to ensure guests have safely cleared the area before dispatching the next tuber.
  • Perform lane speed and condition checks as directed to ensure tubing lanes are operating safely.
  • Enforce Snow Tube Park rules consistently and professionally.
  • Check guest tickets and/or passes as required.
  • Monitor changing weather, snow, and tubing conditions and promptly communicate safety concerns to the supervisor or manager.

Rope/Handle Tow Operations

  • Assist guests on and off handle tow as needed.
  • Become knowledgeable of operational, safety, emergency, and equipment procedures related to handle tow operations.
  • Monitor load and unload areas and assist with maintaining safe guest flow.
  • Perform routine safety inspections of handle tow load and unload areas.
  • Maintain load and unload areas by shoveling, raking, and removing excess or uneven snow as necessary.
  • Immediately report equipment concerns, unsafe conditions, or operational issues to management.
  • Become familiar with Seven Oaks' skiable terrain, facilities, and operations in order to accurately answer guest questions.

Park Maintenance & Equipment

  • Maintain smooth and safe tubing lanes and operational areas using shovels, rakes, and other appropriate tools.
  • Remove snow chunks, debris, and other potential hazards from tubing lanes, lift areas, and guest traffic areas.
  • Assist with daily setup and tear-down of the Snow Tube Park, including fencing, signs, pads, barriers, tubes, and other equipment.
  • Inspect tubes, lifts, fencing, signage, and other Snow Tube Park equipment and report damaged or improperly functioning equipment.
  • Assist with projects such as fencing installation or repair, sign replacement, snow removal, and other operational needs.
  • Use shovels, rakes, electric drills, and other appropriate tools as needed.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.

Guest Service & Teamwork

  • Provide exceptional guest service in a friendly, courteous, and enthusiastic manner.
  • Answer guest questions and provide information about Seven Oaks Recreation, its facilities, and available activities.
  • Work cooperatively with other team members and departments to provide a positive guest experience.
  • Rotate between assigned Snow Tube Park positions and responsibilities throughout the shift.
  • Remain attentive and safety-focused while working in a busy, noisy, and fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrate dependability and the ability to perform assigned duties with limited supervision.
  • Assist with other duties and operational projects as assigned.

title: Policy Officer – Strategic Team for Anti-Racism
description:
This is an Expression of Interest (EOI) opportunity, available on a lateral move basis only. Applications are open to Core Scottish Government employees only.

Job Title – Policy Officer – Strategic Team for Anti-Racism

Working Arrangement – Staff in roles compatible with hybrid working should aim to spend 40% of their contracted working time working in person at their contractual workplace. More information can be found within Hybrid Working Policy. This directorate is based across Edinburgh and Glasgow.

Grade – B2

Advert type – level transfer

Duration - Permanent

Eligibility - Expressions of interest are invited from substantive colleagues on level transfer from Core SG only.

Skilled Worker Sponsorship not being offered

Skilled Worker sponsorship is not available for this role. As a result, we are unable to appoint candidates who require Skilled Worker sponsorship now or in the future. Applicants must have an existing and ongoing right to work in the UK.

Overview

The Equality, Inclusion & Human Rights Directorate’s mission is to ensure equality, inclusion and human rights are at the centre of everything the Scottish Government does, promoting equality, tackling discrimination and fostering inclusion. The Mainstreaming and Inclusion Division drives actions to embed human rights and equality across government and the wider public sector, building capability and capacity to make deep and sustained progress on tackling inequality through better policy-making and service design.

The Strategic Team for Anti-Racism (STAR) leads Scotland’s cross-government work to tackle structural and systemic racism. Operating in a fast-paced, highly visible environment with significant political interest, STAR develops and delivers strategic policy to embed anti-racism across government and public services. This role requires resilience and the ability to handle complex, sensitive issues under scrutiny, balancing competing priorities while influencing diverse stakeholders. The successful candidate will support the team with the next phase of Scotland’s anti-racism work, implement and monitor a refreshed delivery plan aligned to the Race Equality Framework for Scotland (2016–2030), contribute to Scotland’s international treaty reporting obligations, and support wider community cohesion work, including providing reassurance and clear communication during times of uncertainty or heightened public concern.

Responsibilities:

  • Supporting the development and delivery of a public-facing anti-racism delivery plan, ensuring alignment with the Race Equality Framework for Scotland (2016–2030).

  • Provide support to colleagues on anti-racism policy, including on sensitive issues that attract scrutiny and involve balancing competing priorities.

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, including community organisations, public bodies, and internal teams, to ensure meaningful engagement and co-production.

  • Monitor and report on progress against anti-racism commitments, ensuring transparency and accountability in delivery.

  • Support on capability-building initiatives to embed anti-racism principles in policy-making and service design across Scottish Government.

  • Support operational delivery including ministerial briefings, PQs, FOIs, correspondence and cross‑government coordination.

  • Support and contribute to Scotland’s international treaty reporting obligations, ensuring accurate, timely submissions and alignment with human rights commitments.

  • Support wider community cohesion work, including offering reassurance and clear messaging during periods of uncertainty or heightened sensitivity.

Success Profile

Success profiles are specific to each job and they include the mix of behaviours, experience and technical criteria (if applicable) that candidates will be assessed on.

Experience:

  1. Demonstrable understanding of anti-racism policy and practice, including structural and systemic racism, and ability to apply these principles to support systemic change.
  2. Experience of working with Ministers and officials, preparing high-quality briefings, handling commissions, and managing politically sensitive issues under scrutiny.
  3. Ability to independently manage operational delivery, while also supporting colleagues in handling cross-cutting policies or programmes, demonstrating proactivity and strong prioritisation skills.
  4. Ability to communicate and influence effectively across internal and external stakeholders, including communities and delivery partners, building trust and working effectively with racialised communities in sensitive contexts.

Behaviours:

  • Seeing the big picture - Level 3

  • Working together - Level 3

  • Delivering at pace – Level 3

  • Communicating and influencing – Level 3

You can find out more about Success Profiles Behaviours, here: Success profiles: candidate guide - gov.scot

Working Pattern

The post is a full-time role, but staff with different working patterns are invited to apply, and we will assess proposed working patterns against the business requirements for this post.

Our standard hours are 35 hours per week and we offer a range of flexible working options depending on the needs of the role, including Flexi-leave. Scottish Government staff in hybrid-compatible roles should aim to work in-person 40% of the time, either in an office or other agreed work location. If you have specific questions about the role you are applying for, please contact us.

Further Information

Further information about this opportunity is available from Davide Bargna, davide.bargna@gov.scot.

How to Apply

Please submit your CV and an Expression of Interest (maximum 500 words) outlining your suitability for the role, relevant skills and experience, and what you would bring to the team. Please align this to how you meet the behaviours, experience and technical skills listed in the Success Profile above.

Vacancies close at 11:59pm on the date displayed in the table, unless otherwise stated on the job advert.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can be used to support your application, but all statements and examples provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, and presented as your own) applications will be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action.

Please see our candidate guidance for more information on acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI in recruitment.

If invited for further assessment, this will consist of a light touch interview.

Discussions are to be confirmed.

Recruitment Principles

As a government organisation, we adhere to the Civil Service Commission Recruitment Principles and we investigate any complaints received in relation to recruitment cases.

About us

The Scottish Government is the devolved government for Scotland. We have responsibility for a wide range of key policy areas including: education, health, the economy, justice, housing and transport. We offer rewarding careers and employ people across Scotland in a wide range of professions and roles.

Our staff are part of the UK Civil Service observing the Civil Service Codeand working for Ministers and senior stakeholders to deliver vital public services which improve the lives of the people of Scotland.

We offer a supportive and inclusive working environment along with a wide range of employee benefits. Find out more about what we offer.

As part of the UK Civil Service, we uphold the Civil Service Nationality Rules.

Security checks

Successful candidates must complete the Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS), before they can be appointed. BPSS is comprised of four main pre-employment checks – Identity, Right to work, Employment History and a Criminal Record check (unspent convictions).

You can find out more about BPSS on the UK Government website, or read about the different levels of security checks in our Candidate Guide.

Equality statement

We are committed to equality and inclusion and we aim to recruit a diverse workforce that reflects the population of our nation.

Find out more about our commitment to diversity and how we offer and support recruitment adjustments for anyone who needs them.

Further information

Find out more about our organisation, what we offer staff members and how to apply on our Careers Website.

Read our Candidate Guide for further information on our recruitment and application processes.

title: Rental Equipment Technician
description:
POWER UP YOUR CAREER WITH LOUISIANA CAT


Louisiana Cat has been proud to represent Caterpillar® for 4 continuous generations in the state of Louisiana. We have been providing our customers with the highest quality Cat® equipment, service, and parts since 1933. We serve to build and power our community for a better future. We are always searching for high energy, ambitious candidates who are ready to join our team. You can build your future here!


THE OPPORTUNITY


We are looking for a RENTAL EQUIPMENT TECHNICIAN to join our growing operations (Louisiana Rents) at our Bossier City, Louisiana location.


SALARY POTENTIAL


60,000 - $72,000 yearly range

The yearly range indicated is representative of the hourly rate, including typical overtime. This range is based on a technician’s experience, skills, education and training. For technicians, overtime is typically calculated on a daily basis after 8 hours worked.


YOUR VALUE


The person in this role will be responsible for servicing and repairing construction rental heavy equipment.


YOUR CONTRIBUTION

  • You will diagnose, troubleshoot, repair, and perform preventative maintenance on all components of heavy rental equipment including engines, power trains, hydraulics and fuel systems.
  • You will read and interpret equipment manuals, mechanical and electrical schematics, and other specifications to determine the repair method on failed components.
  • You will replace or repair defective components, using hand tools, gauges, and testing equipment.
  • You will assemble and install electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic equipment using hand or power tools.
  • You will rebuild install and align pump assemblies utilizing safe rigging methods using hand or power tools.
  • You will create, track and formalize work order documents on a timely basis
  • You will have the ability to be flexible with changing priorities in a fast-paced environment

YOUR VALUE

  • You will promote positive customer service for Louisiana Cat Rental Stores according to Caterpillar and Louisiana Cat expectations
  • We will give you the tools and building blocks to MAKE A CAREER here at Louisiana Cat
  • You'll become so much more than a mechanic

MOST IMPORTANT QUALIFICATIONS

  • REQUIRED: High School Diploma or (GED) equivalent
  • REQUIRED: Minimum of 3 years of field experience
  • REQUIRED: Strong mechanical Aptitude
  • REQUIRED: Basic understanding of hand tools
  • REQUIRED: Strong attention to detail and problem solving skills
  • REQUIRED: Ability to work in a team environment
  • Must own required tool inventory. Louisiana Cat offers exclusive Tooling Program (specific discussed during interviews)
  • Strong customer service skills, mechanical aptitude, professional demeanor and always "safety-first" mentality every hour of every day

JOB FACTS

  • SHIFT SCHEDULE: Monday - Friday 7am - 5pm; may require working hours outside standard work schedule (specifics discussed during interviews)
  • WORK ENVIRONMENT: Requires physical movement, lifting, squatting, bending, climbing, and working with mechanical rotating parts in the Louisiana climate

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to stand; use hands to finger, handle, or feel and reach with hands and arms. The employee must be able to occasionally lift 75 pounds from floor to chest. The employee must have the ability to reach and use the arms within a full range of motion in order to retrieve stocked parts. The employee must have the ability to endure prolonged stooping, kneeling, crouching and squatting while performing mechanical operations. The employee must be able to exert push/pull forces with the arms in order to use various wrenches and tools. The employee must be able to endure prolonged forward and overhead arm positions while performing mechanical operations. The employee must be able to use the hands to grasp hand tools and parts. The employee must have the ability to climb onto and operate equipment. The employee must have the ability to operate and maintain a field service vehicle with GVW of less than 26,000 lbs.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Employee regularly works indoors around moving mechanical parts. May be exposed to weather extremes when working outside in conditions that include inclement weather, heat, cold, and humidity. The noise level may be loud at times. Exposure to small quantities of chemicals, dust, steam, high-pressure water, and high speed rotating equipment. Requires wearing common protective or safety equipment. Required to perform work in cramped spaces and/or high places. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate, with occasional loudness when equipment is running.

LOUISIANA CAT BENEFITS

  • Health, Dental, Vision, $50,000 Company Funded Life Policy (if enrolled in Health)
  • Short- and Long-Term Disability Insurance
  • Voluntary Accident, Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity, Cancer, Supplemental Life and additional voluntary policies
  • 401K Plan with Company Match
  • Paid Holidays & Vacation
  • Technician Tool Loan Program up to $2,000
  • Safety Boot / Safety Prescription Glasses Allowances
  • Employee Discounts
  • Credit Union
  • Technician Career Development Program - Shop & Field Service Training

SAFETY IN ALL WE DO

  • We require strict compliance with PPE (personal protective equipment) safety regulations.
  • We maintain compliance with all Federal, State and Local safety and company regulations.
  • All employees must follow all Company Health, Safety & Environmental (HSE) procedures.
  • Louisiana Cat is a drug-free workplace, including marijuana and THC products.

WHY PEOPLE JOIN LOUISIANA CAT

  • We are dedicated to fostering a safe and meaningful work environment that empowers our employees and customers.
  • We are known for creating lasting partnerships, guided by our strong company values, customer experience culture and safety standards.
  • We are committed to the long-term growth and success of both our employees and customers.
  • We have energy, focus and passion delivering results because what we do impacts our customers each and every day.
  • We work across Construction, Electrical Power, Industrial, Marine Engines and Oil & Gas industries.
  • We invest in training and development programs for our employees to build their toolkit and career paths here at Louisiana Cat.
  • We offer competitive pay and benefits, paid holidays and vacation, employee incentive programs and 401(k) company match programs.

WHO WE ARE

  • We are a growing organization focused on creating a positive impact on our employees, customers and communities in which we operate. We seek out employees who are inspired by our values, thrive in a collaborative environment, and want to become a part of a dynamic company backed by 90+ years of success. We have 23 locations across Louisiana and the Gulf South with Corporate HQ located in Reserve, LA and Power Systems HQ located in New Iberia, LA.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

  • Louisiana Cat (Louisiana Machinery Co, LLC) and its affiliates are an Equal Opportunity Employer (EEO). All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age (40 and over), national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. We proudly hire U.S. Veterans.

  • Equal Employment Opportunity Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal: click here for more information
  • Pay Transparency Nondiscrimination Provision: click here for more information

Shipping Lead

Ellenwood Warehouse

5490 GA-42

title: Community Health Workers
description:
Bronx Community Health Network (BCHN)

Job Description

Position Title: Community Health Worker (CHW)

Supervisor: Asst. Director of Population Health

Job Type: Full-Time (37.5 hours weekly)

Department: Population Health

Schedule Shift: Monday- Friday 9:00am-5:30pm and weekends as needed.

FLSA: Exempt

Salary: $55,000 - $65,000


Come join our amazing team of dedicated healthcare workers!


Bronx Community Health Network (BCHN): was founded in 1996 to ensure that the socio-economically depressed and medically underserved residents of the Bronx have access to high-quality and comprehensive healthcare services, Bronx Community Health Network (BCHN) is a not-for-profit, community-based organization and Federally Qualified Health Center. The organization provides a wide range of comprehensive, coordinated primary medical, oral, and mental health care and related diagnostic, pharmacy, social support, and enabling services for medically underserved/uninsured residents. BCHN’s service area includes the entire borough of the Bronx, including all 25 zip codes.


BCHN mission: To improve the health of people and families in the Bronx; provide access to affordable, quality health care, especially for uninsured persons; promote disease prevention, early treatment and healthful lifestyles; and obtain financial and other resources for programs and services.


About the Role: The Community Health Workers serves as a trusted member of the community and a key part of the care team. The CHW promotes health, encourages healthy behaviors, supports patients in accessing services, and reduces barriers to care. The CHW works closely with clinical providers, care coordinators, and external partners to improve health outcomes, address social determinants of health, and support patients in navigating the healthcare system. The CHW reports directly to the CHW Supervisor.

  • Conduct outreach to patients in the clinic, community, home settings, or by phone to promote engagement in care.
  • Assist patients in scheduling medical, behavioral health, and preventive appointments.
  • Provide follow-up outreach related to chronic disease management, preventive care, and care-plan adherence.
  • Help patients understand their care plans and support them in following provider instructions.
  • Assist with referrals to community services, including housing, food assistance, mental health resources, transportation, and social support.
  • Support patients in navigating health insurance enrollment, benefits, and health system processes.
  • Deliver basic health education on prevention, wellness, chronic disease management, and healthy lifestyle practices.
  • Provide culturally responsive education that reflects the needs of the population.
  • Reinforce provider-directed education using appropriate teaching tools and health literacy methods.
  • Document patient interactions, referrals, and outreach efforts in the electronic health record (EHR) and other data-tracking systems.
  • Maintain accurate, timely, and confidential records in compliance with HIPPA and organizational policy.
  • Assist in reporting outcomes and participating in quality improvement activities.
  • Participate in community events, health fairs, and outreach campaigns.
  • Build relationships with local organizations, agencies, and social service providers.
  • Represent the organization in community partnerships and coalitions as assigned.
  • Work with care teams, population health staff, and behavioral health providers to address patient needs.
  • Attend team meetings, conferences, and training sessions.
  • Communicate patient barriers or concerns to the appropriate clinical or supervisory staff.
  • Maintains knowledge of and compliance with FQHC, HRSA, Article 28, HIPPA, OSHA, infection control, patient privacy, and applicable federal, state, and local regulatory requirements. Supports audit readiness, survey preparation, documentation standards, and organizational policies as applicable to the role.
  • Performs other duties as assigned based on organizational needs, including support for new site openings, mobile health operations, emergency preparedness, and special projects.

Qualifications and Skills

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate degree preferred.
  • 2+ years of CHW experience or comparable education/training experience preferred
  • CHW Certificate (Preferred)
  • Lived experience, cultural knowledge, or community familiarity is strongly valued.
  • Experience in community outreach, case management, health education, or social services preferred.
  • Bilingual English and Spanish.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Required:

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trust and rapport.
  • Knowledge of community resources, social determinants of health, and health system navigation.
  • Ability to work with diverse populations using culturally competent and trauma-informed approaches.
  • Basic computer literacy, including the ability to use EHR systems and documentation tools.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of an interdisciplinary team.
  • Ability to maintain effective professional and trusting relationships with patients, families, community partners, and clinical teams.

Salary Range: The base salary range for this position $55,000 – $65,000 annually.


The total compensation for the finalist selected for this role will be determined based on various factors, including but not limited to scope of role, level of experience, education, accomplishments, internal equity, budget, and subject to Fair Market Value evaluation. The base salary range listed above is a good faith determination of potential base compensation at the time of this job advertisement and may be modified in the future.


IMPORTANT NOTICE REGARDING RECRUITMENT FRAUD


BCHN has become aware of fraudulent recruitment activities being conducted by individuals or organizations falsely claiming to represent BCHN. Please be advised that BCHN never requests payment or fees from job applicants at any stage of the recruitment process. All legitimate job openings are posted exclusively on our official career website at www.bchnhealth.org, and all email communications from our recruitment team will come only from actual email addresses ending in bchnhealth.org. If you receive any suspicious communications, we strongly advise you not to engage or provide any personal information, and to report the incident to your local authorities.


Bronx Community Health Network is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer committed to diversity and inclusion in all aspects of recruiting and employment. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration without regard to race, color, gender, gender identity or expression, sex, sexual orientation, transgender status, gender dysphoria, national origin, age, religion, disability, military, and veteran status, martial or prenatal status, citizenship status, genetic information or any other factor which cannot lawfully be used as a basis for an employment decision.

title: Academic Sessional Supervisor - Psychology
description:
About VU
At VU, we aim to be one of the leading impact universities in the world. VU is an impact driven university committed to equity, excellence and opportunity. Based in Melbourne’s west and connected globally, we put students first through the VU Block Model®, dual sector pathways and strong industry partnerships. We are a values led, inclusive workplace where diverse talent is supported to make a real difference.

About the Team
The Victoria University Psychology Clinic delivers high quality psychological therapy and assessment services to clients across the lifespan. The Clinic plays a central role in training postgraduate students in the Master of Clinical Psychology and Master of Professional Psychology programs. The team consists of experienced clinicians and supervisors committed to supporting student development, client wellbeing, and evidence based practice.

About the Role
As an Academic Sessional Supervisor, you will provide high quality clinical supervision to provisional psychologists completing placements within the Clinic. You will guide students through therapeutic work, case formulation, intervention planning, and/or cognitive and educational assessments. Supervision is aligned with AHPRA guidelines and may be delivered in-person or online. This role offers the opportunity to shape the next generation of psychologists while contributing to a supportive and collaborative clinical training environment.

Key Responsibilities
• Provide individual supervision to provisional psychologists with a particular focus on therapy and/or cognitive assessment.
• For applicants with a focus on therapy: guide supervisees in completing case formulation, treatment planning, therapy, and intervention
• For applicants with a focus on cognitive assessment: guide supervisees in conducting, scoring, interpreting, and reporting on cognitive and educational assessments (e.g., WISC-V, WAIS-5, WRAT-5). Rating scales and questionnaires such as the BASC-3, CBCL, Conners-4, CAARS2, ASRS, SRS-2, Vineland-3, and ABAS-3 may be included as part of an assessment alongside a WISC-V, WAIS-5, and/or WRAT5 but are not offered as a standalone assessment.
• Support the development of clinical reasoning, ethical practice, and professional identity.
