title: Senior Production Planner
description:
Job Summary

The Senior Production Planner is responsible for developing, maintaining, and executing the assembly production schedule within an Engineer-to-Order (ETO) manufacturing environment. The role aligns customer orders, engineering releases, material availability, and plant capacity to meet delivery commitments.

This role serves as the primary planning liaison between the Site Master Scheduler, Project Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, Production, and the Fabrication Planning team, translating complex project requirements into executable shop-floor schedules.


Job Duties and Responsibilities

Assembly Scheduling & Execution

  • Translate the SIOP-driven master schedule into a rolling 12-week production plan aligned with plant capacity, ramp-ups, customer orders, engineering releases, and lead times.
  • Monitor shop-floor progress and schedule adherence, adjusting priorities as needed.
  • Own performance metrics, including schedule attainment, on-time delivery to customer commitments, and WIP levels.
  • Maintain accurate scheduling data within Epicor.
  • Recommend / Propose plans & actions to mitigate at-risk delivery commitments.

Master Schedule Alignment

  • Act as the primary link between the Site Master Scheduler and shop-floor execution.
  • Manage the schedule impact of engineering changes (ECOs), customer revisions, and supply disruptions, and coordinate master schedule updates with the Master Scheduler and other stakeholders.

Capacity & Constraint Management

  • Proactively identify bottlenecks and constraints (capacity, material, fabricated components, and engineering releases) and coordinate cross-functional actions to resolve them.
  • Escalate risks to delivery commitments and recommend recovery or mitigation plans when needed.

Cross-Functional Planning & Communication

  • Coordinate with Engineering, Supply Chain, Production, Quality, and Project Management to align design releases, material availability, and manufacturing execution.
  • Lead daily and weekly production scheduling reviews with production supervisors, PMO, and the fabrication team.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve assembly flow, resource utilization, schedule adherence, and planning processes.
  • Support and Drive the development and standardization of production planning and scheduling processes.
  • Mentor and develop production coordinators as the team grows.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree with 4+ years of experience in production planning, scheduling, or manufacturing operations; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • Advanced ERP/MRP proficiency with a strong understanding of BOM structures, routings, master scheduling, and capacity planning.
  • Experience coordinating across Engineering, Supply Chain, Project Management, and Manufacturing.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and make effective decisions in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and production scheduling tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in an Engineer-to-Order (ETO), Make-to-Order (MTO), or project-based manufacturing environment.
  • Experience with SIOP/S&OP and master scheduling processes.
  • Epicor ERP experience.
  • APICS CPIM or CSCP certification.

  • Paid holidays
  • $100 individual deductible and $300 family deductible health insurance
  • Paid Weekly
  • Vision and Dental Insurance
  • 401K / Life Insurance / STD

title: Senior Backend Engineer (all genders)
description:
About GeneralMind

GeneralMind builds AI Systems of Action for complex enterprise workflows. We deploy AI employees that automate messy operational handovers across supply chains - processing orders, validating invoices, coordinating suppliers, and handling exceptions directly on top of enterprise systems like SAP, Oracle, JDE, and Dynamics.

Our platform combines AI agents, operational context graphs, and real transaction data to achieve Autopilot-grade automation in real operational environments.

We work closely with leading global companies across manufacturing, retail, and logistics to deploy AI into mission-critical workflows.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Backend Engineer who is both broad and deep - someone who can hold the whole backend in their head and make good decisions across it, while also bringing a genuine spike that makes us meaningfully better in an area we're not yet strong in. That spike is the differentiator. Great engineering fundamentals get you to the interview. The thing you're unusually good at is what gets you the role.

This role sits at the intersection of two things that are rarely mastered together: building robust, production-grade Python services and designing durable, observable workflow systems with tools like Temporal. But more than the specific technologies, we're looking for someone with the ownership instinct and the range to become the de facto owner of our entire backend - its architecture, its reliability, and its evolution.

You will be a senior individual contributor working directly with the founders. The person in this role won't be handed a roadmap - they'll help define it, and build the team around it.

What You'll Do

Backend Ownership

  • Own the backend end-to-end: service architecture, API design, reliability posture, and long-term technical direction.
  • Be the person who knows how everything fits together - and who other engineers come to when they're not sure where something belongs.
  • Set the bar on code quality, service boundaries, and shared abstractions across the engineering team.
  • Make foundational decisions with conviction, document the reasoning, and evolve them as the system grows.

Python Services & Production Systems

  • Design for failure: retries, timeouts, graceful degradation, and recovery paths built in from the start.
  • Write code that is easy to operate - observable, testable, and straightforward to debug at 2am.
  • Understand the runtime, not just the framework. Know when the problem is the code, the config, or the infrastructure.

Workflow Engineering & Temporal

  • Design and build durable workflows using Temporal - long-running processes, async coordination, saga patterns.
  • Own workflow observability: know when a workflow is stuck, degraded, or silently wrong before a customer notices.
  • Think carefully about idempotency, failure modes, and replay semantics - not just the happy path.
  • Evolve workflows without breaking running instances; manage versioning with intention.

Reliability & Systems Thinking

  • Detect regressions before they become incidents; build the tooling to catch them early.
  • Own the operational posture of the services you build: alerting, runbooks, on-call readiness.
  • Identify structural debt before it compounds; propose refactors that are thoughtful, not just correct.

What we are looking for

  • Experience: 6+ years building and operating backend systems in Python, with clear ownership of production services - not just feature delivery.
  • Python depth: Non-negotiable. You make deliberate choices about async vs. sync, framework selection, and performance tradeoffs. You know the language well enough to have opinions.
  • Temporal or equivalent: You've used Temporal (or a comparable workflow engine) in production. You understand durable execution, not just task queues.
  • Reliability instinct: Idempotency, retries, and observability are part of how you design, not afterthoughts.
  • End-to-end ownership: You're comfortable being the person who holds the full backend picture. You identify what's broken or missing before you're asked, and you don't leave the system worse than you found it.
  • A real spike: We're a strong team with broad coverage. What we're hiring for is someone who brings a 10x improvement in an area we're currently underinvested in. That might be workflow systems, data infrastructure, AI-native backend patterns, or deep domain expertise. We don't know exactly what shape it takes - but you should know what yours is, and be able to articulate why it matters.

title: Consultant for Development and Piloting of a Methodology to Assess Return, Readmission and Reintegration Systems in North Africa
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration


Project Context and Scope

This consultancy is part of the Migrant Protection, Return and Reintegration Programme in North Africa (MPRR-NA), funded by the European Union, as well as the governments of Italy, Norway, Denmark and Sweden. It builds on a consultancy to map return and reintegration systems in Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco and Tunisia and is aimed to develop and pilot a standardized institutional methodology that IOM can maintain, replicate and adapt. The methodology will cover legal and policy frameworks, institutional mandates, coordination, referral pathways, services, data collection and analysis guidance protection and operational practices. The consultant will develop and pilot the methodology in one country, provide training and quality assurance, and consolidate the institutional guidance and training package, while RDH will lead primary data collection, analysis, and country drafting for the remaining four countries, in coordination with Country Offices.


Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing
IOM MENA Regional Office for North Africa and Middle East, Regional Data Hub, in close coordination with Migrant Protection, Return and Reintegration Programme (MPRR-NA), relevant IOM Country Offices and relevant thematic units
Tasks to be performed under this contract
First deliverable – Submission of Inception Report and Draft Standard Methodology:

  • Develop a draft standard methodology, assessment dimensions, research questions, evidence standards and analytical approach.

  • Prepare standardized tools and guidelines, including the country profile template, template interview guide for KIIs by set of stakeholder, stakeholder mapping tool, data analysis methodology (incl coding, thematic analysis, and triangulation), quality assurance checklist and ethical and data-protection guidance.

  • Provide a detailed workplan confirming responsibilities, dependencies and timelines.

Tentative timeline: November 2026, to be completed by 5 November

First instalment payment (24% of the total contract value, i.e., USD 9,063) - payable within 15 days of receipt and approval of the required deliverable.

Second deliverable – Submission of Pilot Application and Template Country Chapter :

  • Pilot methodology through data collection and drafting of country level chapter

  • Apply the methodology and produce a complete country chapter serving as the template for the remaining profiles.

  • Document lessons from the pilot and propose revisions to the methodology and tools.

Tentative timeline: November 2026, to be completed by 10 November

Second instalment payment (32% of the total contract value, i.e., USD 12,500) - payable within 15 days of receipt and approval of the required deliverable.

Third deliverable -Submission of Training and Methodology Roll-out:

  • Prepare a practical training package and supporting materials on the application of the methodology, KII guide, evidence documentation, stakeholder mapping tool, template country chapter, quality assurance checklist and ethical and data-protection guidance as well as lessons learned from the pilot

  • Deliver a virtual regional training following the training package developed.

  • Revise the tools based on feedback from the training, if any.

Tentative timeline: November 2026, to be completed by 15 November

Third instalment payment (8% of the total contract value, i.e., USD 3,125) - payable within 15 days of receipt and approval of the required deliverable.

Fourth deliverable -– Submission of Technical Review, Quality Assurance of Four Remaining Country Profiles and Validation Support:

  • Provide technical guidance to IOM staff during primary data collection and drafting for Algeria, Egypt, Libya and Tunisia.

  • Review the four draft chapters for methodological consistency, evidence, data limitations and comparability.

  • Provide consolidated comments and support final revisions.

  • Support country and regional validation and document substantive feedback.

Tentative timeline: December 2026, to be completed by 31 December

Fourth instalment payment (11% of the total contract value, i.e., USD 4,375) - payable within 15 days of receipt and approval of the required deliverable.

Final deliverable -– Submission of Final Standard Methodology, Guidelines and Training Package:

  • Produce final implementation guidance with annexed tools, templates, evidence standards and quality assurance procedures.

  • Prepare a final reusable training package for future application by IOM teams.

  • Support technical validation with relevant Regional Office and Headquarters counterparts, incorporate consolidated feedback, and take part in a dissemination webinar for the final package.

  • Submit all final products and editable source files in an organized handover package.

Tentative timeline: February-April 2027, to be completed by 30 April

Final instalment payment (25% of the total contract value, i.e., USD 9,687) - payable within 15 days of receipt and approval of the required deliverable.

Performance indicators for the evaluation of results
  • Timely submission of all deliverables.
  • Quality and depth of analysis in the research report.
  • Practicality and relevance of recommendations.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Advanced university degree in migration, social sciences, international relations, or a related field.

Experience

    • At least 10 years of experience in migration, return, and reintegration, including work with IOM or similar international organizations.

    • Proven experience in developing guidance, conducting feasibility/risk assessments, and supporting policy operationalization in migration contexts.

    • Regional expertise in the MENA region and experience with comparative research.

Skills

Languages

title: Analyst
description:
ABOUT YOU

The position requires a practical, quality-focused individual who is comfortable working safely with chemicals and takes pride in producing reliable results and maintaining accurate records.

You may be a recent science or chemistry graduate, or you may have gained relevant experience in a laboratory, scientific or industrial setting. Previous experience of ICP-MS, ICP-OES, XRF or IC would be useful, but it is not essential because full training will be provided.

You'll join a small, close-knit and supportive team where everyone contributes. A positive attitude, willingness to learn and readiness to complete both technical and routine laboratory duties are important.

Required skills and experience:

  • A degree in Chemistry or another relevant scientific discipline, or suitable experience gained within a scientific or industrial setting
  • Basic chemistry knowledge and an understanding of safe chemical handling
  • Good practical laboratory skills, or a clear interest in developing these within an analytical laboratory
  • Strong numeracy skills, including the ability to calculate and tabulate results accurately
  • Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accurate laboratory records and documentation
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to build effective relationships with colleagues and, once trained, clients
  • A collaborative, reliable and hands-on approach, with a willingness to support the team and complete routine laboratory duties
  • Ability to organise your workload, meet agreed deadlines and maintain good communication with relevant stakeholders
  • Experience of ICP-MS, ICP-OES, XRF, IC, ISO 17025 or the chemical and polymer industry would be advantageous

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

As an Inorganic Analysis Analyst, you'll prepare and analyse chemical samples using a variety of analytical techniques, generate reliable data and report your results accurately.

You'll begin with a bespoke programme of internal, on-site training based on your existing knowledge and experience. Even if you have used similar equipment elsewhere, you'll be trained in the specialist methods and procedures used at Wilton.

As your knowledge develops, you'll learn to recognise unusual results or analytical artefacts, support laboratory investigations and gain greater exposure to clients' products, processes and technical questions.

There may also be an opportunity, once established in the role, to join the Scientist Development Programme and learn additional techniques within or across teams. Participation and any associated pay progression are subject to performance, business need, an approved business case and available funding.

Key activities:

  • Prepare and analyse chemical samples using a range of inorganic analysis techniques
  • Train in multiple analytical techniques and develop the ability to generate useful data and recognise artefacts
  • Follow approved methods, procedures and instructions, applying basic interpretation skills to analytical results
  • Calculate, tabulate, interpret and accurately report laboratory results
  • Support laboratory investigations, troubleshoot analytical issues and contribute to effective problem-solving
  • Maintain accurate laboratory records and comply with relevant quality, safety and COSHH requirements
  • Plan and manage your workload, meeting agreed deadlines and keeping stakeholders informed
  • Work to priorities agreed with the Project Manager and Delivery Manager
  • Develop an understanding of clients' products, processes and technical requirements and, once trained, communicate with clients effectively
  • Support colleagues, contribute positively to the team and complete shared routine duties, including cleaning laboratory equipment
  • Take an active interest in personal development and opportunities to broaden your scientific skills

WHAT WE OFFER

Join Intertek and become part of our global network of inspiring and entrepreneurial colleagues. We are a global family that values diversity and we thrive working together with precision, pace, and passion. We are working to make the world Ever Better, ensuring the quality, safety and sustainability of products and services used by millions of people around the world.

  • Competitive salary/benefits
  • Development and career opportunities around the Globe
  • Structured laboratory training within a highly motivated, close-knit team and dynamic working environment

title: Reconciliation Analyst - 12 month contract
description:
Who we're looking for

Within this role you will work to ensure the integrity of custody and cash position data and the complete reconciliation, investigation and allocation of all breaks in cash and securities.

You will also liaise with an array of operational teams to ensure that breaks are investigated and resolved and that issues are tracked to resolution.

You will thrive in a fast-paced environment with an emphasis on meeting tight deadlines and a strong interest in learning and harnessing technology.

Your experience will allow you to independently carry out processes, whilst also working with the team, as well as challenge current processes to ensure continuous development by helping create and implement enhancements to processes / systems.

About Us

Schroders is a global investment manager which provides active asset management, wealth management and investment solutions. We aim to provide excellent investment performance to clients through active management. We serve a diverse client base that includes pension schemes, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, foundations, high net worth individuals, family offices, as well as end clients through partnerships with distributors, financial advisers, and online platforms.

Established in 1804, we have around 5,500 people across 36 global locations. Schroders' success can be attributed to its diversified business model, spanning different asset classes, client types and geographies.

The base

At Schroders, we're known for doing things differently. That's why we’re building a home for the ambitious in Horsham, West Sussex. You’ll get the all the benefits of being part of a world-leading asset manager. But you’ll also get the support of being part of a genuine local community. If you’re looking for opportunities that match your ambitions, you’ll find them right here in Horsham.

What you'll do

  • Accountable for allocated portfolios, proactive investigation and timely follow up of queries arising from internal stakeholders, clients, counterparties, custodians and administrators

  • Perform custody transaction and position reconciliation against internal records

  • Maintain ownership of daily cash and stock breaks by conducting investigation on differences, and monitoring through timely resolution with processing teams and custodians/administrators

  • Validate and update internal records with relevant transactions, such as fees and income

  • Daily reconciliation of Treasury trade confirmation

  • Requesting statements of holdings and balances from custodians and fund transfer agents

  • Managing the accuracy and continuity of data within the supported systems

  • Work through high volumes, prioritise, and manage workload according to risk or deadlines

  • Escalate potential problems before they become a risk

  • Meet all deadlines and ensure procedures and controls are fully implemented

  • Assist reviewing and update procedures, implement improvements and enforce stringent controls

  • Escalate potential problems before they become a risk

  • Meet the needs of our business partners and internal clients establishing and maintaining strong working relationships with internal functions and external counterparts

  • Contribute to department initiatives and projects.

The knowledge, experience and qualifications you need

  • Broad experience in asset or wealth management operations, specifically Securities Administration and reconciliation;

  • Investment Operations Certificate (IOC) or equivalent;

  • A strong attention to detail is required;

  • Good at analysing and solving problems;

  • Experience in using Temenos platform (T24) desirable;

  • Experience is using Smart Stream Corona;

  • Intermediate experience of Microsoft applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint;

The knowledge, experience and qualifications that’ll help

  • Focused on clients and delivery, taking ownership of tasks and seeing them through to completion;

  • Dedicated to your role, the success of the team and business through a proactive approach to ensure a positive client experience;

  • Excellent time management, recognising the importance of being punctual to support team reliability and productivity;

  • A strong collaborator and a good communicator with people skills who takes a wider interest in other activities on the team and business, offering support wherever possible;

  • Open to feedback, receptive to change, continually looks out for team and self improvement opportunities.

  • Able to navigate through change and maintain an innovative culture.

We Recognise Potential, Whoever You Are

We believe diverse perspectives and an inclusive culture help us make better decisions and achieve better outcomes for our clients. That's why inclusion is a strategic priority for us, and we are an equal opportunities employer. title: Maintenance Trainee-CLMB
description:
The Maintenance Trainee will learn to work with all plant personnel to support improved equipment and process reliability as well as efficient and cost effective use of plant resources. This position requires the development of a solid background in mechanical and electrical systems as well as training in maintenance reliability to be advanced to the industrial maintenance technician position. This position requires excellent technical writing and verbal communications skills. In addition, the ability to read and work from Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) technical manuals, Process and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), and control schematics must adequately demonstrated prior to advancement to the industrial maintenance technician position. The incumbent must demonstrate the ability to learn and effectively use various software programs including the company’s Enterprise Asset Management System (EAMS).

The incumbent must demonstrate satisfactory performance and knowledge in all of the key areas described below, in addition to completing formal education requirements assigned by the Company. The Engineer will review current OTJ performance, and review Competency List completion. In addition, the Trainee will have an annual performance review that is tied to the annual merit increase. The trainee must be making progress toward the completion of the courses listed in the Development Programand must be successfully performing the role of the Maintenance Craftsman Trainee. Both of these factors also will be reviewed during the formal quarterly performance review process. Failure to progress in the program (grade “C” or better in each course; rated “meet expectations” on performance reviews) may result in dismissal from the Development Program.

The Maintenance Trainee will be required to attend a minimum of two classes per semester but no more than 9 credit hours per semester. Columbus MFG will pay the Trainee their hourly wage while in class. Mileage to and from school will be at the expense of the Trainee. Tuition and books will be paid by Columbus MFG. The Trainee will be required to refund Columbus MFG 100% of costs, excluding wages paid by Columbus MFG, should their employment end for any reason within 3 years from the completion date of the Industrial Automation and Machine Maintenance program. Also, the Trainee agrees to pay 100% of Columbus MFG costs for any class in which they do not receive a “C” or higher. The Trainee agrees to make a onetime payment for the costs paid by Columbus MFG or agrees to authorize payroll deductions for the amount equivalent to the costs paid by Columbus MFG.

Selection Criteria

Qualified personnel who express interest in participating in the industrial Maintenance Craftsman Development Program will be selected for participation based on the following criteria, in order of precedence as follows:

  1. Previous Experience: preference will be granted to those who have work experience related to electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic and process systems. Knowledge in these areas will be assessed through formal testing administered by Columbus MFG (maintenance and/or electrical exam).
  2. Formal Training: preference will be granted based on the number completed courses within the Maintenance Craftsman Development curriculum or equivalent (if applicable).
  3. Job performance in current position at Columbus MFG.
  4. Length of Service: all other criteria equal between candidates, preference will be granted to the individual with greatest length of service.

title: Customer Experience Specialist
description:
Job Title: Customer Experience Specialist
Location: Remote
Type: Full-Time
Starting Salary: $65,000 (potential adjustments based on experience)
Reports to: Customer Experience Manager

Associations create change. We amplify it.

Novi AMS helps associations amplify the impact they create for their members and industries. We started in an association boardroom, and everything we build is designed with our association partners in mind.

About the role

Our Customer Support team is small, close-knit, and evolving in how we work.

We’ve embraced AI and smarter technology to handle more of the repetitive work, giving our team more time to focus on what matters most: solving complex problems, building customer confidence, and creating better experiences.

Support at Novi is about much more than answering questions or closing tickets. We’re technical problem-solvers, educators, advocates, and partners to our customers. We investigate challenging issues, help customers make the most of Novi, develop resources that make learning easier, and turn what we learn from customers into meaningful product improvements.

You’ll join a collaborative, curious team that enjoys turning complicated problems into clear, approachable solutions. We care about getting the answer right, but we care just as much about how we get there and how the customer feels along the way.

Our goal isn’t simply to resolve the issue. It’s to leave customers more confident, capable, and excited about what they can accomplish with Novi.

What you’ll do

  • Own the customer experience. Manage support conversations in Pylon across chat, email, phone, and screen-share sessions, from initial response through resolution, balancing technical accuracy, thoughtful communication, and timely follow-through.

  • Solve challenging problems. Investigate issues involving customer configurations, data relationships, integrations, and unexpected system behavior. Connect the dots across available tools and resources to identify root causes and practical solutions.

  • Work alongside AI. Use AI agents as part of your daily workflow to research, troubleshoot, draft, and analyze. Apply your own judgment to validate results, improve outcomes, and help shape how our team uses AI.

  • Collaborate across teams. Partner with Onboarding, Success, developers, and other internal teams to investigate escalations, communicate findings, advocate for customers, and move issues toward resolution.

  • Teach and empower customers. Help customers understand not just how Novi works, but how to use it effectively. Lead or co-host live Office Hours, webinars, and training sessions that build confidence and encourage adoption.

  • Make knowledge accessible. Create and maintain clear, useful Help Center articles, internal documentation, and educational resources. Keep content current as the product evolves.

  • Turn insights into improvements. Identify recurring questions, friction points, and opportunities to improve the product, documentation, or support experience. Take initiative to turn those observations into action.

  • Help us work smarter. Experiment with new tools, workflows, and approaches that make our team more effective and create more time for meaningful customer interactions.

What you’ll need to be successful

Exceptional written communication

You communicate clearly, warmly, and with purpose. You know how to make technical concepts understandable, adapt your approach to different audiences, and provide answers that feel both personal and actionable. Because much of our support happens asynchronously, your writing is one of your most important tools.

Technical curiosity and independent troubleshooting

You enjoy figuring out how things work and why they sometimes don't. You approach problems methodically, ask thoughtful questions, and use available resources to investigate before escalating. You're comfortable saying "I don't know yet" because you're confident in your ability to find out.

Practical AI fluency

You have hands-on experience using AI tools to research, solve problems, or improve workflows, with the ability to evaluate their output and recognize when human judgment is needed.

A creative, customer-focused mindset

You look beyond the immediate question to understand what the customer is trying to accomplish. When the original approach isn't possible, you explore alternatives and help them find a path forward. You want customers to walk away not just with a solution, but with new ideas and a better understanding of what's possible.

Ownership and good judgment

You take responsibility for moving things forward while balancing thoroughness with efficiency. You know when a question needs a quick answer, when to dig deeper, when to ask for help, and when to escalate. You manage competing priorities, advocate for customers, and follow through on commitments without needing to be reminded.

Initiative and adaptability

You're comfortable trying new approaches, learning from what works (and what doesn't), and adjusting as you go. You welcome feedback, embrace change, and aren't afraid to challenge an existing process when you see an opportunity to make it better.

Systems thinking

You recognize that individual support conversations often reveal bigger opportunities. You notice patterns, connect information across different sources, and think about how solving a problem once could prevent it from happening again.

What success looks like

Within your first six months, you'll have developed the product knowledge and confidence to independently manage support conversations, troubleshoot complex issues, and guide customers toward effective solutions.

You'll be actively contributing to customer education, collaborating with teammates across departments, and using AI and other tools to work efficiently without sacrificing quality.

Beyond resolving individual issues, you'll be finding ways to make the experience better for everyone – whether that's improving a resource, simplifying a process, or identifying a recurring problem worth solving.

Most importantly, customers will leave their interactions with you feeling heard, supported, and more capable of getting the most out of Novi.

What you'll bring

  • 2+ years of experience in technical SaaS support, software customer success, or a comparable customer-facing role involving technical troubleshooting.

  • Experience investigating and resolving complex software issues, with the ability to explain technical findings to nontechnical audiences.

  • Confidence leading one-on-one or group customer conversations, explaining concepts clearly, answering questions, and helping customers feel comfortable learning something new.

  • Experience working remotely and collaborating asynchronously through tools like Slack, Zoom, and Jira.

  • Comfort working independently, managing competing priorities, and taking ownership in a fast-moving environment.

  • Strong fundamentals, genuine curiosity, and the drive to become an expert.

  • Authorization to work in the United States and availability to work 8 AM – 5 PM in your local time zone (Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific).

Bonus points for experience with:

  • QuickBooks Online, Pylon, association management software (AMS), CRM platforms, or the association industry.

  • Strongly preferred: Experience using Novi AMS

Why join Novi?

  • Remote-first, for over a decade. We've been fully remote for more than 10 years. Work from your home office anywhere in the United States, with the equipment and support you need to succeed.

  • Benefits that matter. Fully paid family health, dental, and vision insurance, generous PTO, paid holidays, family-friendly leave policies, and a 401(k) match.

  • Life outside of work matters. We believe great work and a full life should go hand in hand. Family, friends, flexibility, and work-life balance are part of our culture.

  • Room to grow. We invest in professional development, certifications, continuing education, and opportunities to take on new challenges and advance within Novi.

  • A team that has your back. We value different perspectives, share what we learn, help each other succeed, and celebrate wins big and small.

  • The opportunity to make an impact. On a small team, your ideas matter. You'll have a real voice in how we support customers, improve our tools, and shape the future of the customer experience.

Compensation

The starting salary for this position is $65,000, with adjustments based on experience and qualifications.

title: Sr. Engineering Manager
description:

description:

Please note that we are unable to offer sponsorship for this role

An exciting new role within Lancashire County Council's Accessible Transport Service

We're recruiting two Transport Eligibility Officers (SEND) to join our expanding Accessible Transport Service. This is a newly created role that will play a vital part in ensuring children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) can access education through appropriate travel assistance arrangements.

The Accessible Transport Service works with families, schools, transport providers and partner services to deliver safe and effective transport solutions for children, young people and vulnerable adults across Lancashire. As our service continues to develop, we're creating a dedicated assessment function to strengthen decision-making and improve outcomes for SEND passengers.

Job Role/Key Responsibilities

You'll be responsible for assessing applications for home to school transport assistance, determining eligibility in line with legislation and council policy, and ensuring decisions are fair, consistent and evidence based.

Working closely with our Eligibility and Needs Assessment Team and Safer Travel Team, you'll also undertake passenger risk assessments to identify the right level of transport support, helping to ensure children and young people travel safely and successfully to education.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Assess applications for home to school transport assistance for children and young people with SEND.
  • Evaluate complex medical, educational and disability-related evidence to determine eligibility.
  • Produce clear, evidence-based decisions that can withstand appeals and scrutiny.
  • Complete passenger risk assessments and develop safety plans to ensure appropriate levels of support are provided.
  • Work collaboratively with the Eligibility and Needs Assessment Team and Safer Travel Team.
  • Investigate and respond to transport appeals.
  • Liaise with families, schools, transport providers and partner agencies.
  • Contribute to service improvement and the development of best practice across the Accessible Transport Service.

About You

We're looking for individuals who have experience working with children and young people with SEND and who can confidently assess needs and make balanced decisions based on evidence.

You will have:

  • Experience of carrying out assessments and making recommendations.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building abilities.
  • The ability to interpret policy, guidance and legislation.
  • A commitment to delivering high-quality customer-focused services.
  • A passion for achieving positive outcomes for children, young people and families.

Why join us?

This is a unique opportunity to help shape a brand-new role within a service that makes a real difference every day. You'll join a supportive and forward-thinking team committed to innovation, collaboration and delivering positive outcomes for Lancashire residents.

What we offer:

  • A rewarding role with genuine purpose.
  • Opportunities for professional development and progression.
  • Flexible and hybrid working arrangements where appropriate.
  • Supportive management and team environment.
  • Local Government Pension Scheme.
  • Generous annual leave entitlement.
  • Access to a range of employee wellbeing benefits.

Join us

If you are looking for a challenging and rewarding opportunity where your expertise can help ensure children and young people with SEND receive the right travel support to access education, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and help us deliver safe, effective and person-centred transport solutions for Lancashire's children and young people.

Closing Date: 01/11/2026

Please ensure you upload a supporting statement demonstrating how you meet the criteria for the role.

The post you are applying for is covered by the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975 (as amended in 2013). If successful you will be required to apply to the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) for a 'disclosure'. Further information can be found on the 'Our Recruitment Process' tab.

We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications.

Local Government Reorganisation

The Government has confirmed that local government across Lancashire will be reorganised, with the current 15 councils being replaced by four new unitary councils covering North, South, East and West Lancashire from April 2028.

If you are successful in your application, you will initially join Lancashire County Council. However, as part of the planned transition, your employment will transfer to one of the new unitary councils from April 2028, subject to the implementation of the reorganisation and relevant employment legislation.

Throughout this period, our focus remains on delivering excellent services to our communities. By joining us now, you'll play an important role in shaping the future of local government and helping to build a strong new organisation that will serve residents for years to come.

title: Senior Frontend Engineer (all genders)
description:
About GeneralMind

GeneralMind builds AI Systems of Action for complex enterprise workflows. We deploy AI employees that automate messy operational handovers across supply chains - processing orders, validating invoices, coordinating suppliers, and handling exceptions directly on top of enterprise systems like SAP, Oracle, JDE, and Dynamics.

Our platform combines AI agents, operational context graphs, and real transaction data to achieve Autopilot-grade automation in real operational environments.

We work closely with leading global companies across manufacturing, retail, and logistics to deploy AI into mission-critical workflows.

About the role

We are looking for an exceptional Senior Frontend Engineer to join our Berlin team. This is not a role for someone looking to execute tickets handed down from above. You will own technical decisions end to end, shape how we build our product interfaces, and directly influence our product trajectory.

You will operate primarily as an individual contributor (80%), while also stepping up to lead and mentor a small squad of engineers (20%). We expect you to bring strong opinions, hold them loosely, and always optimize for what's right in the long run.

What You'll Do

Engineering & Architecture

  • Take full ownership of frontend systems from scoping through delivery - you ask the right questions early, cut through ambiguity, and drive things to completion.
  • Make and defend architectural decisions that balance shipping velocity with long-term maintainability; you know when to build a custom component and when to reach for a proven pattern.
  • Build fast, accessible, and reliable interfaces with React and Next.js as your primary stack, with enough full-stack range to collaborate effectively across Python-based backend services.
  • Evaluate AI tooling critically - you use it daily to move faster, but you understand that vibe coding is a liability, and you hold your AI-generated output to the same standard as everything else.

Technical Leadership

  • Lead your squad during planning cycles: go deep on each ticket, challenge scope where needed, and make sure the team ships with clarity.
  • Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through code review, pairing, and design discussions - not by micromanaging, but by setting a high bar.
  • Proactively identify bottlenecks, technical debt, and systemic risks before they become emergencies.

What we are looking for

  • Experience: 8+ years of hands-on frontend engineering experience, with a consistent track record of shipping production applications at scale.
  • Technical depth: TypeScript and React are non-negotiable. Deep experience with Next.js (App Router, server components, data fetching patterns) is expected. Familiarity with modern styling (Tailwind CSS), state management (Zustand, TanStack Query), and component architecture (Radix UI, headless patterns) is a strong plus.
  • Judgment: You understand the trade-off between a pixel-perfect custom component and a pragmatic library solution - and you know which the situation actually calls for.
  • Ownership: You don't wait to be told. You identify what needs doing, flag it, and drive it to completion.
  • Discipline: Detail-oriented to a fault. You can take over sprint and cycle planning for a squad and make it better - tighter tickets, cleaner scoping, fewer surprises.
  • AI-native, not AI-dependent: You integrate AI tools naturally into your daily workflow for speed and leverage, but you review, reason about, and take full responsibility for everything you ship.
  • Independent thinker: You form your own technical views, push back when something doesn't make sense, and don't need consensus to act.
  • Supply chain domain experience: A meaningful plus - we work in a space where understanding warehouse workflows, inventory logic, or ERP-adjacent systems translates directly into better engineering decisions.

title: Manager, Risk Management and Insurance
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

This Manager will lead a significant business function and is accountable for strategic planning, operational execution, risk oversight, talent development and achievement of business objectives. The role requires leadership through others, strong business acumen, enterprise collaboration and the ability to make sound decisions in complex and uncertain environments.

The individual acts as Manager for Southern Company’s Risk Management & Insurance Department (Atlanta) working alongside, directing and overseeing the work efforts primarily associated with designated liability coverage lines, including surety, and the captive. This position is responsible for: providing professional and technical expertise in assessing corporate property & casualty risks; determining appropriate risk management strategies; designing and negotiating risk transfer, risk financing and loss control plans and integrating those plans into the broader Southern Company enterprise - wide risk management philosophy and practice; administering corporate risk & insurance programs; and supporting Alternative Risk Transfer (ART) arrangements, on behalf of Southern Company (SoCo) and subsidiaries.

JOB REQUIREMENTS:

Education:

BBA (MBA and/or CPCU/ARM preferred) with emphasis in risk management, commercial property and casualty insurance & risk finance or related field. Demonstrated commitment to continuing professional development is a plus.

Job Experience:

13 years or more years’ relevant work experience (depending on academic background) in corporate risk management, insurance brokerage, captive management and/ or commercial lines underwriting and include Management/supervisor experience. Must have experience managing 3rd party vendors

Job Knowledge, Skills:

  • Extensive knowledge and demonstrated expertise & experience (minimum 13 years), in the following areas:

  • Corporate property and casualty insurance policies (broad spectrum); emphasis in commercial liability insurance

  • Finance (particularly risk financing applications)

  • Contractual risk transfer and insurance techniques

  • Strategic leadership: Develop and execute functional strategies aligned with enterprise objectives

  • Think holistically about business operations and broader organizational impacts

  • Identify emerging risk, opportunities and trends

  • Lead transformation, process improvement and innovation initiatives

  • Anticipate changing conditions and adjust priorities accordingly

  • Operational & Financial Management: Direct the activities of staff, establish clear goals and expectations , manage budgets, forecast and resource allocation as well as monitor performance and ensure delivery of results. Ensure compliance with policies, requirements and governance standards. Role requires:

  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail

  • Strong aptitude for problem solving and negotiations; ability to constructively handle occasional conflict situations

  • Strong organizational & time management skills including ability to prioritize and manage multiple task

People Leadership:

  • Foster collaboration internally and across departments and operating companies, promote an inclusive and high performing work environment, lead and ensure development of staff including providing constructive feedback of performance and development plans. Develop and maintain a leadership pipeline.

  • Risk Management and Insurance:

  • Superior knowledge of property and casualty insurance

  • Working knowledge of construction risk management & insurance tools and techniques

  • Working knowledge of alternative risk finance techniques (including large retentions, captive facilities, & capital markets/ hybrid solutions)

  • Working knowledge and expertise in claims handling and negotiations and risk management information systems

  • Working knowledge of generally accepted loss control principles and practices

  • Working knowledge of electric, gas and renewables projects and the major contracts which comprise them through course of development, construction, operations and maintenance; and the related risks and insurance tools and/ or loss control measures to address those risks is preferred

  • General knowledge of enterprise risk management principles and practices

  • General knowledge of utility industry insurance property and casualty insurance markets is preferred, particularly industry mutual insurers such as AEGIS and Energy Insurance Mutual

Stakeholder Management:

  • Strong interpersonal communications (oral and written), teaming and negotiating skills; ability to establish a rapport, inspire confidence and effectively interact with personnel of varying backgrounds/ position levels within the company and with external service providers

  • Ability to influence decisions through data driven recommendations and business insight

  • Broad, general knowledge of Southern Company and subsidiaries’ (core and non-core) operations is preferred.

  • Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel & PowerPoint; prefer experience with (or commitment to soon acquire) ChatGPT, Claude Enterprise, 365 CoPilot/Studio and other AI related tools with current and potential RMI applications; experience with DXC’s Assure/RiskMaster is a plus

MAJOR JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Act as Manager for the SCS Risk Management Atlanta Section working alongside, directing and overseeing the work efforts of designated personnel

  • Identify and assess corporate property and casualty exposures arising from current and planned operations, with particular emphasis on commercial liability risks. Works with staff and management at levels across SoCo as well as a variety of external resources.

  • Provide strategic leadership of the property and casualty insurance and risk transfer program

  • Senior level experience in counterparty contractual risk transfer and insurance provisions.

  • Ability to advise supply chain and contracts administration personnel, project development coordinators, legal counsel and operations management on techniques which will minimize risk to Southern Company and subsidiaries; provide support for contract negotiations and/ or lead in relevant portions of those negotiations, as requested.

  • Design, negotiate, place and administer insurance or other risk financing techniques which will minimize the adverse financial impact of fortuitous loss and produce the long-term lowest cost of risk (sum of insurance costs, self-insured claims costs and certain loss-control expenses)

  • Manage the captive operations and the staff that support the captive ensuring effective operations including State and regulatory compliance

  • Design, implement and manage designated liability lines, including captive and alternative risk financing/ insurance plans. Responsibilities include budget and accounting reconciliation, compiling underwriting information, negotiating excess insurance and reinsurance plans, premium allocation among subsidiaries, claims settlement and recordkeeping, and interface, as and where required, with captive management and broker activities.

title: Restorative Aide
description:

title: Global Mobility Data & Reporting Analyst
description:
Are you ready to launch your HR career at one of the most dynamic organizations in the world? IBM’s HR Delivery Operations (HRDO) Early Professional Hire Program is built for bold, curious, and driven early professionals who want more than a job — they want to make an impact from day one. As a Global Mobility Data & Reporting Analyst, you won’t be on the sidelines. You’ll be embedded in the heart of HR Delivery Operations working alongside experienced HR professionals, analyzing real data, solving real problems, and contributing to the employee experience for IBMers around the world. This is an opportunity to develop the skills the future of HR demands — data fluency, analytical acumen, AI-native thinking, and the judgment to challenge the status quo — while building a career with depth, purpose, and trajectory. From your first week, you will be immersed in IBM’s culture, tools, and ways of working. Over the course of the role, you will grow from learner to contributor to subject matter expert — developing functional expertise, owning meaningful work, and building the foundation for a long-term career within IBM HR. The Global Mobility team is a critical function within IBM that supports the movement and deployment of IBMers across the globe. Whether this is cross border travel, immigration, relocation, or international assignment, we ensure that IBMers (and their families) get to the right place at the right time to perform critical work for the company. Key Responsibilities Program Learning Journey:

  • Week 1 — Foundation: Orientation to IBM culture, ways of working, and core productivity tools (Outlook, Slack, Monday.com, and more)
  • Week 2 — HRDO Immersion: Grounding in HR I&O leadership, the HRDO operating model, KPIs, end-to-end experience measurement, and the PMO
  • Months 1–3 — Immersion: Embedded alongside the cross-functional delivery squad, learning through direct exposure and structured coaching
  • Months 4–6 — Accountability: Leading data and analytics deliverables with structured oversight, building confidence through ownership
  • Months 7–12 — Impact: Developing deep functional expertise and independently proposing actions to improve employee experience and operational performance
  • Months 12+ — Elevation: Transitioning from developer to driver — owning strategic initiatives, influencing outcomes across HRDO, and building the credibility to grow into broader roles Function-Specific Responsibilities: The Global Mobility Data & Reporting Analyst will perform detailed reporting and analysis in support of the Global Mobility team. This will include research, performance reporting, analytics, operations management, audit, and departmental operations. In this role, you will plan, design, and execute reporting and analysis by accessing and consolidating data from multiple sources. You will collaborate with departmental managers to help produce meaningful analysis in a comprehensive format which includes dashboards, charts, graphs, and presentations. You will help to summarize data and provide your commentary or observations based on your analysis. Sources of data may be enterprise systems, complex spreadsheets, vendor/supplier databases. Shared Responsibilities Across All ELH Roles:
  • Analyze operational and employee experience data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for process improvement
  • Translate data into clear, actionable insights and recommendations for HR leaders and operations teams
  • Develop and maintain dashboards, ad hoc analyses, and standardized reporting to monitor HR performance and service health
  • Develop executive-ready presentations and narratives that communicate complex insights in a compelling and concise manner
  • Partner cross-functionally with HRDO teams, and HR professional across the organization to drive alignment and deliver outcomes
  • Contribute to a culture of continuous improvement by proactively surfacing ideas and acting on feedback
  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Data Analytics, Finance, or a related field
  • Strong analytical mindset with a genuine curiosity for working with data
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present ideas clearly and confidently
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Word)
  • Ability to manage competing priorities with strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive employee information with discretion
  • Exposure to data visualization tools
  • Familiarity with AI tools and an eagerness to adopt emerging technologies
  • Experience with enterprise HR or business systems (e.g., Workday, SAP, Concur)
  • Requires general financial capabilities to calculate and conduct basic financial analysis. title: Lead Mobile Software Engineer
description:
We are seeking a hands-on technical leader to define mobile architecture, build modern full-stack commerce capabilities, and turn emerging technologies into measurable customer and business value.

This role combines Lead Mobile Architect, Senior Full-Stack Engineer, and Innovation Lead responsibilities. You will guide engineers, make pragmatic architecture decisions, write production code, and partner with product, design, security, platform, and enterprise teams. You will balance mobile-specific excellence with reusable, API-first services that power experiences across channels.

JOB DUTIES:

  • Define and own the mobile architecture and technical roadmap for our iOS and Android apps, built with React Native and TypeScript
  • Build fast, reliable, secure, and accessible mobile experiences
  • Own the mobile release process, from CI/CD to App Store and Google Play delivery
  • Design and build backend services and APIs that power both mobile and web commerce

YOU MUST HAVE:

WE VALUE:

  • Familiarity with composable/headless commerce, ERP/PIM/CMS integrations, BigCommerce or similar platforms, and complex omnichannel commerce workflows
  • Experience with native Swift/Kotlin, React Native New Architecture, Expo where appropriate, Firebase, push notifications, analytics, crash reporting, and mobile experimentation
  • Practical delivery of AI-enabled product features, LLM integration, retrieval-augmented generation, tool-using agents, evaluation frameworks, and responsible AI safeguards
  • Knowledge of WCAG accessibility, mobile accessibility testing, privacy regulations, payments-related security boundaries, and software supply-chain controls
  • Experience scaling distributed engineering teams, setting engineering standards, and balancing innovation with operational stability.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience

  • Flexible working hours

title: Nevada Gold Mines - Manager, Total Rewards
description:
Position Description

Owns and leads the design, governance, and delivery of U.S. Total Rewards programs, translating the organization’s Total Rewards strategy into competitive, equitable, compliant, and cost-effective compensation and benefits programs. Provides strategic leadership across U.S. compensation, benefits, retirement, wellness, and related rewards programs, while ensuring alignment with regional and global Total Rewards philosophy, frameworks, and governance.

Leads a team of Total Rewards professionals and manages external consultants, brokers, carriers, and other service providers as appropriate. Partners with HR and business leaders to provide expert guidance, enable effective decision-making, and continuously improve the employee Total Rewards experience

Responsibilities

  • Lead U.S. Total Rewards strategy and governance, ensuring alignment with regional and global frameworks while addressing U.S.-specific business, market, and regulatory requirements.
  • Own U.S. compensation programs and practices, including market benchmarking, salary structures, annual compensation processes, incentive programs, pay equity, recognition, and related governance.
  • Own the design, governance, and administration of U.S. benefit programs, including health and welfare, retirement, wellness, and other employee benefit programs.
  • Lead annual benefits planning and open enrollment, including program design, vendor coordination, communications, implementation, and ongoing evaluation.
  • Manage Total Rewards vendors, consultants, brokers, carriers, and service providers, ensuring effective performance, appropriate controls, and value.
  • Ensure compliance and appropriate governance of U.S. compensation and benefits programs, including applicable legal and regulatory requirements, audits, reporting, and internal controls.
  • Monitor Total Rewards costs and financial performance, develop and manage budgets, and identify opportunities to improve cost effectiveness while maintaining competitive employee programs.
  • Provide Total Rewards analytics and insights to support program evaluation, workforce decisions, compensation decisions, and recommendations to HR and business leadership.
  • Drive continuous improvement and process optimization, leveraging technology, automation, and data to improve program administration, accuracy, efficiency, and employee experience.
  • Partner with HR, business leaders, Finance, Legal, Payroll, HRIS, and other stakeholders to deliver effective Total Rewards programs and resolve complex issues.
  • Provide expert guidance and education on U.S. compensation and benefits practices, market trends, regulatory developments, and Total Rewards programs.
  • Represent U.S. Total Rewards in applicable regional and global forums, providing U.S. expertise and ensuring effective integration of global initiatives within the U.S.
  • Lead, develop, and coach the Total Rewards team, establishing priorities, objectives, and accountability while building functional capability.
  • Promote organizational Health, Safety & Environment expectations and address relevant performance or compliance issues within the area of responsibility

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Finance, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience; advanced degree and/or relevant professional certification preferred.

Experience

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in Compensation, Benefits, or Total Rewards, with demonstrated breadth across compensation and benefits.
  • 3+ years of experience leading and developing professionals and managing external vendors or consultants.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex U.S. benefits programs, including self-funded plans, retirement programs, vendor relationships, and significant budgets.
  • Strong knowledge of U.S. compensation practices, benefits programs, and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
  • Strong analytical, project management, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate Total Rewards strategy into practical programs and effectively balance business, employee, financial, and regulatory considerations.

title: Senior Sales Engineer - West Region
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The Senior Sales Engineer supports the Sales Department by providing pre/post-sales technical support to target channel partners, direct sales, account management and wholesale clients. The Senior Sales Engineer will function as a technical liaison for channel partners, direct sales, account management, and wholesale clients. The Senior Sales Engineer will provide expert consulting, design and engineering of all voice, network access, managed Wifi, Security as a Service, SD-WAN and complex sales solutions. The Senior Sales Engineer is also responsible to manage a queue of all new business proposals to ensure all RFPs include the proper CPE per the outlined solution.

The Senior Sales Engineer reports directly to the Manager, Sales Engineering.

There are no direct reports to this position.

The Senior Sales Engineer interfaces with the following key personnel within the Company, though is not limited by this list: Sales, Service Delivery, Network Operations Engineering, Account Management, Sales Engineering and Sales Support.


ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

The Senior Sales Engineer is accountable for

· Demonstrate and apply an advanced level of product knowledge when working with customers and partners.

· Assist sales personnel, engineering team and external partners to approve proposals for sales opportunities.

· Gather and analyze data and author design of potential solutions that are relevant, valued and compelling to the client while being profitable for the company.

· Manage ICB process for technical requests outside of standard product catalog.

· Discover and qualify prospective and current customer’s business needs, and then design solutions that leverage Telesystem’s product portfolio and network assets.

· Provide virtual and field support as required to assist Sales team with product presentation and solution design.

· Assist Manager, Sales Engineering in conducting monthly trainings for Sales Team on new products, data networking, telecommunications technology and more.

· Contribute to technical responses required for RFPs and other enterprise opportunities as needed.

· Assist with product development initiatives as needed and serve as one of the subject matter experts for sales training once the product is release by Product Development.

· Assist other Sales Engineers in the day-to-day tasks and provide training as needed.

· Monitor and oversee the task approval process in the CRM system for the sales engineering team to ensure order accuracy and follow up with appropriate parties as needed for changes.

· Prepare and present internal and external training programs on new products and features.

· Attend industry events, partner workshops/expos/symposiums, and trade shows as delegated for the purpose of supporting the Sales Team, improving solution design, competitive intelligence gathering and industry trend analysis.

· Following and enforcing the Company’s policies and procedures, including the EEO guidelines and safety at all times.

· Performing any miscellaneous department duties as needed.


JOB REQUIREMENTS

Education and Experience

· High School Diploma or equivalent - required

· 4 years of Sales Engineering experience or similar role - required

· 7 years in the telecommunications industry in a technical role or similar industry experience - required

· Proficiency in Microsoft Office: Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Visio products – required

· 2 years of sales with Cybersecurity products/solutions - preferred


*Must be obtained within the first year of employment*

· Fortinet NSE level 4 or higher certification – required

· Obtain a CCNA Certification level or higher – required


Core Competencies

· Agile – Embraces change; adaptable and flexible; sense of urgency.

· Innovative – Uses critical thinking; Creativity; Continuous learning; Challenges the status quo.

· Customer Focused – External/Internal; Creates the exceptional customer experience; demonstrates a sales and service mentality.

· Collaborative – Teamwork, Proactive knowledge sharing, Constructive Conflict.

· Accountable – See it, Own it, Solve it, Do it; Hold each other accountable.

Leadership Competencies

· Deliver Results – Strategic planning and execution; Makes decisions in the best interest of the Company; Knows and responds to the business climate; Manages ambiguity.

· Displays Leadership – Role Model; Communicates vision; possesses Emotional Maturity; Manages Risks; Resiliency; Business Acumen.


Other Requirements

· Background record that meets Company standards.

· Reliable means of transportation at all times.

· Strictly maintains confidentiality of financial and/or other information acquired in the course of work; discloses only when authorized, unless legally obligated to do so.

· Valid driver’s license and driving record that meets company standards at all times.


WORKING CONDITIONS

· The Senior Sales Engineer is a salaried, exempt position. The regular work hours are 40 hours, Monday – Friday. These hours may vary to accommodate the needs of the company.

· The Company is a drug-free workplace. All employees are required to adhere to the Company’s drug-free workplace programs and policies. Pre-employment testing is mandatory.

· The duties assigned, the hours worked, and the status of this position is subject to change as the needs of the company changes.

USE OF COMPANY RESOURCES, EQUIPMENT AND CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION

Company resources, equipment, and information are provided to employees to facilitate work. They may not be used for purposes other than work without proper authorization. Any unauthorized use of Company resources, equipment, or information is strictly prohibited. Any unauthorized use of customer data or any other company information gained via any company resource is a breach of confidentiality and is strictly prohibited. Any unauthorized use of company resources, equipment information, and/or breaches of confidentiality may be cause for termination of employment.

The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this job. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required.

title: Assistant Director, Sallyport Fellows Program
description:
Position Summary:

The Assistant Director of Sallyport Fellows Program (SFP) provides hands-on advising, coaching, and other support to Rice first generation/limited income (FGLI) undergraduate students. Using a relationship- centered, proactive advising model, this position will work closely with FGLI students, guiding them in making the transition to college and achieving student-determined goals at and beyond Rice. Through holistic, student-centered advising approaches, the Assistant Director will be expected to employ various proactive advising, innovative learning strategies, and coaching techniques to engage students, connect them with critical university resources, and facilitate their successful retention at the University. The Assistant Director will also be responsible for tracking student progress and designing interventions to proactively support student success.

Special Instructions to Applicants: All interested applicants must attach a cover letter and resume in the Supporting Documents section of the application, in PDF format. Please note that the applicant tracking system does not convert attachments in Word format successfully.


Ideal Candidate Statement:

An ideal candidate has a proven track record of success in advising high-need undergraduate students during their transition to college. Successful candidates possess strong communication skills, the ability to build and sustain rapport with students, and an understanding of the unique stressors for FGLI students in a competitive academic environment. Attention to detail, strong problem-solving capabilities, and the desire to be an individual contributor within a cohort of advisors are among the optimal skill sets for this position.

Workplace Requirements:

The role is largely M-F, 9:00 am-5:00 pm however, occasional limited nights and weekends may be required during busy periods.

Workplace Location:

This position is offered as a hybrid role, combining both in-office and remote work to provide flexibility and support collaboration. This role requires working 4 days on campus and the option of one remote day per week. Per Rice policy 440, work arrangements may be subject to change.

Hiring Range: This is a full-time, benefits-eligible position with a hiring range of $60,000 – $65,000 annually, depending on qualifications and experience.

Exempt (salaried) positions under FLSA are not eligible for overtime.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 2 years of related professional experience in a four-year college or university setting with previous advising or coaching experience
  • Skills:
    • Coaching and instructional skills, organizational abilities, attention to detail, and the ability to quickly assess the effectiveness of an intervention
    • Knowledge of theories, including student development, learning, and identity development, and experience applying those frameworks professionally
    • Able to problem-solve and support/advise students in personal and/or academic crisis;
    • Strong communication and rapport-building skills and experience collaborating with faculty, staff, students, alumni, families, and administration
    • Experience and comfort working with diverse student populations, including but not limited to first-generation college students, limited-income students, first and second year students, and underrepresented student populations

Preferences:

  • Master's degree (preferably in college student personnel, counseling, student affairs, or a related field)
