Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration.

Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process.

For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates:

  1. Internal candidates
  2. Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories:

Bahamas, Barbados, Cabo Verde, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu

Second tier candidates include:
All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM.

Organizational Context and Scope

With support from the United States Government’s (USG) Department of State Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration, IOM has developed Community Stabilisation (CS) interventions in multiple countries in the West and Central Africa region. These linked large-scale initiatives seek to address under-development, social cohesion, stabilisation, and public service access challenges in post-conflict and transitioning countries with complex migration and displacement dynamics. To enhance social stability and improve access to essential services and community infrastructure, IOM will utilise an evidence-based, participatory, and area-based programming approach supported by data, analysis, and community-based planning to deliver tangible benefits to local communities in support of government.

To ensure the successful launch and implementation of these initiatives, in support of Country Offices (COs), the IOM Regional Office (RO) and its Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery (DHRR), the Regional Thematic Unit (RTU) will provide strategic oversight, coordination, and technical support, work closely with the CO to provide programmatic guidance, quality assurance, and operational backstopping, and ensure that interventions are aligned with IOM standards, donor requirements, and best practices.

Based in the IOM RO for West and Central Africa in Dakar, Senegal, under the overall supervision of the Regional Director (RD) for West and Central Africa and the direct supervision of the DHRR Regional Thematic Specialist (RTS), and in close coordination with IOM Headquarters (HQ) and IOM Global Office (GO) in Washington, DC, the Regional Community Stabilisation Officer will be responsible and accountable for monitoring and supporting the implementation and coordination of community stabilisation programming, providing technical guidance for regional coherence in methodology, implementation approach and reporting, offer technical support to IOM COs on the application of community stabilisation principles and provide recommendations to improve regional coherence, and collect, collate, and disseminate lessons learned across IOM’s community stabilisation community of practice.

  1. Provide technical guidance to COs on their application of IOM CS guidance and methodologies, in close coordination with the Regional Thematic Unit (DHRR-RTU) in the RO for West and Central Africa and HQ Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery (DHRR).
  2. Facilitate regional coherence in implementation of cross-border CS initiatives across COs, in coordination with the DHRR-RTU, to produce a harmonised implementation approach across shared operational areas.
  3. Support IOM CO to facilitate high-level quality of deliverables by providing technical guidance and remote monitoring of programme partners’ compliance, technical advisers, programme staff, surge personnel, Implementing Partners (IP) and service providers, as needed, enabling COs to achieve consistently high-quality programme deliverables.
  4. Monitor operational, administrative and budgetary performance of regional CS initiatives and programming, identifying risks and efficiency gaps early enough to inform corrective decision-making.
  5. Analyse progress against projected expenditure forecasts and implementation plans, including collecting regular updates of implementation in the areas of intervention, drafting regular reports for the DHRR RTS to determine and propose remedial action to CO where challenges are encountered.
  6. Collaborate with IOM CO, in close coordination with the DHRR-RTU, to gather and disseminate lessons learned from community stabilisation programming, specifically in cross-border and high-instability programming contexts.
  7. Disseminate consolidated lessons learned and replicable practices more broadly across IOM’s CS Community of Practice, DHRR-RTU and regional CS project units to promote the region's contribution to global community stabilisation practice.
  8. Assist the DHRR RTS with the analysis of crisis situations, coordination, prioritisation and operational planning, and recommend areas of intervention to the DHRR-RTU, RO Operations pillar, relevant donor coordination structures and Project Committees, and to CO.
  9. Review regional reporting on community stabilisation programming, checking on required revisions and harmonisation of the monthly and interim reporting for timely submission to relevant government and donor coordination and oversight bodies.
  10. Validate the capture and contextualisation of outcome-level results, monitor lessons learned and identify challenges, bringing issues or gaps to the attention of the supervisor or relevant CO as appropriate, to safeguard the integrity of regional results reporting.
  11. Compile and produce an annual report, in close coordination with COs, on community stabilisation under CS initiatives within the region.
  12. Support the DHRR-RTU in providing capacity building, training and general support to COs implementing community stabilisation programming in the region to strengthen regional programme delivery capability.
  13. Participate in DHRR-RTU’s capacity-building activities on community stabilisation, social cohesion and peacebuilding to improve IOM staff proficiency across the region.
  14. Contribute to the development, review and implementation of complementary regional projects and multi-country community stabilisation, social cohesion, resilience and peacebuilding programmes and projects.
  15. Provide technical inputs, as requested by CO and relevant donor and government coordination bodies, to support the DHRR-RTU’s liaison with the USG representing multi-country portfolio on community stabilisation programming.
  16. Participate in relevant regional working group meetings, related fora, and other stabilisation-related events – including meetings, presentations, discussions, visits, negotiations, etc. – as requested by the DHRR RTS, to position IOM as a credible subject matter expert in regional stabilisation coordination.
  17. Undertake frequent travel to countries to provide information and support, project/programme monitoring and reporting, liaison with counterparts, and project implementation.

  18. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Master's degree in International Relations, Development Studies, Development Planning, Political Science, Social Sciences, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
  • University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Relevant experience in programme management in complex environments;

  • Relevant experience in the design and implementation of area-based and community-driven approaches;
  • Relevant experience in project implementation in crisis, post-crisis, and recovery contexts;
  • Relevant experience in supporting government, partner, and stakeholder coordination in the domain of recovery, peacebuilding, and stabilisation; and,
  • Relevant experience in project and program reporting.

Skills

  • Strong technical expertise in stabilisation, peacebuilding, and resilience programming;

  • Recognised expertise in one or more of these fields: community stabilisation, community violence reduction, preventing violent extremism, local peacebuilding or social cohesion;

  • Good verbal and written communication skills including capabilities to present to diverse audiences;

  • Proven abilities relating to implementation (budgets, human resources, procurement, and so forth) for large-scale programming in complex environments;

  • Thorough understanding of donor processes and regulations; and,

  • Knowledge of financial rules and regulations.

Languages

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Notes

Internationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to all clearances, including medical and security as well as accreditation, any residency or visa requirements. Vacancies close at 23:59 local time Geneva, Switzerland on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and any forms of discrimination. IOM is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children.

IOM conducts reference checks and background verification, including through system wide databases such as ClearCheck, to help ensure that candidates have no record of misconduct, including on sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, or fraud. Candidates are expected to uphold these standards and principles at all times.

IOM does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process—whether for application, interview, processing, training, or otherwise—and does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM WAVE system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies.

title: SLPA
description:
Speech-Language Pathology Assistant (SLPA) – Home Health (Part Time)
Thrive Therapy of Kansas
Serving the Hutchinson, KS Area

About Thrive Therapy of Kansas

At Thrive Therapy of Kansas, we help patients improve communication, independence, and quality of life through compassionate, evidence-based therapy services delivered in the comfort of their homes. Our mission is to provide high-quality, patient-centered care while supporting our clinicians with flexibility, teamwork, and opportunities for professional growth.

If you’re a caring, motivated Speech-Language Pathology Assistant who enjoys helping others thrive, we’d love to have you on our team!

Position Summary

We’re seeking a Part-Time Home Health Speech-Language Pathology Assistant (SLPA) to join our growing therapy team in the Hutchinson area. The SLPA will work under the supervision of a licensed Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) to provide individualized therapy services that support patients with communication, speech, language, cognitive, and swallowing needs in the home health setting.

Key Responsibilities

• Implement treatment plans developed by the supervising Speech-Language Pathologist
• Provide speech and language therapy services to patients in their homes
• Assist patients in improving communication, cognitive, and swallowing skills as directed by the SLP
• Monitor, document, and report patient progress and condition changes in a timely manner
• Educate patients and caregivers on therapy techniques, home exercises, and communication strategies
• Maintain accurate patient documentation in accordance with company and regulatory standards
• Collaborate with the therapy team and other healthcare professionals to ensure coordinated patient care
• Maintain a professional, compassionate, and patient-centered approach during all visits

Qualifications

• Associate’s degree from an accredited Speech-Language Pathology Assistant program (required)
• Active Kansas SLPA license/certification (required)
• Minimum 1 year of SLPA experience preferred
• Previous pediatric or adult therapy experience preferred
• Home health experience preferred but not required
• Strong communication, organization, and time management skills
• Dependable, self-motivated, and compassionate
• Reliable transportation and valid driver’s license

Schedule

• Part time
• Flexible Schedule

Benefits

• Competitive pay and mileage reimbursement
• Flexible scheduling and manageable caseloads
• Supportive, team-focused work culture
• Opportunities for professional development and continuing education
• Meaningful work that makes a difference in patients’ daily lives

Work Location

• In the field and throughout the community (home health visits throughout the Wichita area)

How to Apply

Join a team that helps others thrive — and grow your career while doing it!

Send your resume to melissae@thrivetherapyofkansas.com

title: Case Manager
description:
Perimeter Behavioral of Forrest City has an opening for a Case manager position. We are a residential certified facility licensed and Joint Commission accredited. Perimeter Behavioral of Forrest City offers adolescents residential services. We are seeking individuals to join our team who are committed to improving the lives of who are impacted by mental illness.

Perimeter Healthcare is one of the leading behavioral health care providers in the country for children, adolescents, adults, and senior adults. We deliver hope to our patients through the delivery of comprehensive and dedicated treatment programs. Our focus and commitment to service excellence are available across several states and in different care settings. Our team ensures our patients receive the required care that they or their loved ones need. We offer several programs for our patients including inpatient acute treatment and residential treatment. We are seeking staff who exhibit daily the following values: C- Compassion A- Accountability R – Respect and E- Empowerment.

If you would like to learn more about joining our team, please apply on our website at https://perimeterhealthcare.com/ careers.

The Case Manager's responsibilities include the following:

A. POSITION SUMMARY: Provides case management and support services to the Treatment Team to facilitate clinical management of the cases to which assigned.

B. SUPERVISOR: Director of Clinical Services

C. PERSONNEL SUPERVISED: None

D. WORKDAYS/HOURS: The regular workweek is Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

3. 2. Demonstrates the ability to work closely with the assigned therapist and the doctor to coordinate necessary documentation, discharge planning, therapeutic passes, etc.

3. 14. Demonstrates the ability to recognize and report suspected abuse and neglect according to policy, procedure, and law.

title: Chair Lift Operations
description:
Department: Mountain Operations
Reports To: Lift Supervisor / Area Manager
Employment Type: Winter Seasonal
Schedule: Full-Time (5+ shifts/week) or Part-Time; must be available evenings, weekends, and holidays

Job Overview

The Chair Lift Operator is responsible for the safe, efficient, and friendly operation of Seven Oaks' aerial chairlift and for assisting guests with safely loading and unloading. This position plays an important role in creating a positive guest experience while keeping safety the highest priority.

This is primarily an outdoor position requiring employees to work for extended periods in cold and changing winter weather conditions. Chair Lift Operators must be attentive, dependable, able to make quick decisions, and comfortable interacting with guests of all ages and skiing/snowboarding ability levels.

Essential Job Functions

Chair Lift Operations & Safety

  • Safely operate the chairlift according to established operating and safety procedures.
  • Perform proper procedures for starting, slowing, stopping, and emergency stopping of the chairlift.
  • Remain alert and attentive while the lift is operating and make quick decisions when necessary to protect guest safety.
  • Assist guests with safely loading onto and unloading from the chairlift.
  • Provide additional assistance to children and other guests when needed or requested.
  • Inspect guest lift tickets and season passes prior to boarding as required.
  • Follow all established operational, safety, and emergency procedures.
  • Immediately report equipment concerns, unsafe conditions, injuries, or other safety issues to management.

Loading & Unloading Areas

  • Prepare chairlift loading and unloading ramps before opening each day.
  • Maintain proper snow surfaces at loading and unloading areas throughout the day by shoveling, raking, grooming, and adding or removing snow as necessary.
  • Regularly inspect loading and unloading areas for hazards or unsafe conditions.
  • Maintain clean, organized, and safe work areas.
  • Perform end-of-day duties to properly close and secure chairlift areas.

Crowd Control & Hill Maintenance

  • Set up stanchions, ropes, and lift mazes to maintain safe and orderly guest flow.
  • Install required safety signs and barriers before opening and remove or secure them after closing.
  • Assist with snow fencing, sign placement or replacement, and basic trail and hill maintenance as needed.
  • Work with other departments and assist with general mountain operations when needed.

Guest Service

  • Greet guests in a friendly, professional, and helpful manner.
  • Provide courteous assistance to guests regardless of their skiing or snowboarding ability.
  • Become familiar with Seven Oaks' skiable terrain, facilities, and basic operations to accurately answer guest questions.
  • Help create a positive, fun, and safe experience for all Seven Oaks guests.

title: Project Manager/Broker or Agent – Maine & New Hampshire
description:
LandVest is seeking a qualified and motivated Project Manager/Broker/Agent to support our Land Investments team in Maine and New Hampshire. This client-facing role leads the marketing and brokerage of resource and recreational properties and manages assignments from onboarding through closing. The Project Manager/Broker/Agent partners closely with LandVest’s in-house specialists and external advisors to deliver a high-touch client experience while building regional relationships that drive new opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage the end-to-end listing and transaction process for timberland, agricultural, and recreational properties, from onboarding to closing.
  • Develop pricing, positioning, and marketing strategies informed by market conditions, comparable sales, and property attributes.
  • Coordinate due diligence and assemble property information (maps, exhibits, photography, narratives, and supporting documentation).
  • Oversee the creation and distribution of marketing materials, including offering packages, presentations, web listings, and outreach campaigns.
  • Conduct property tours and site visits with prospective buyers; represent LandVest professionally in the field and in client meetings.
  • Maintain clear, proactive communication with clients and buyers; track activity, milestones, and deliverables across multiple active assignments.
  • Support negotiations and transaction execution, including offers, contracts, and coordination with attorneys, surveyors, foresters, and lenders as needed.
  • Build and maintain relationships with landowners, investors, forestry professionals, consultants, and other referral sources to generate new business.
  • Collaborate with LandVest team members (foresters, GIS/cartography, marketing, analytics, and operations) to deliver best-in-class service.
  • Perform other duties as assigned in support of team and company objectives.

title: Casual Archive Assistant
description:
Salary £13.45 per hour | Casual Hours | Lancashire Records Office | Preston

Please note that we are unable to offer sponsorship for this role

At Lancashire Archives and Local History, we are looking for a reliable and adaptable Archive Assistant to join our team on a casual basis. In this role, you may support our daily operations during peak periods, events, or to cover staff absences. This position offers excellent flexibility, making it ideal for anyone balancing studies, freelance work, or other commitments.

Lancashire Archives is an accredited archive service based in Preston, which looks after millions of historic documents – from medieval parchment charters to digital images of everyday life during the COVID pandemic - that together help tell our county's story over the last 900 years.

About the role:

Are you someone who is fascinated by history? Do you enjoy working as part pf a team to help customers? Are you able to handle irreplaceable archives with care?

If so, we have an ideal opportunity for you!

As a Casual Archive Assistant at Lancashire Archives and Local History, you will be part of a team that welcomes customers and volunteers to our public searchroom and supports them during their visit; responds to written, telephone and face to face enquiries from customers about our collections and the service we offer; uses our collections management database to find information about our collections; takes part in outreach activities; supports other Lancashire Archives teams deliver a range of services; produces archives from our strongrooms and returns them after use (we have 8 strongrooms containing a total of 10 miles of shelving); taking care of unique historical material.

As a casual member of the team, you will provide support during times when we are particularly busy and may be focussed on specific tasks. An example is sending quotations to customers who would like to receive a digital copy of a document in our collections.

Our ideal candidate will:

  • Be able to deliver a customer- focussed service
  • Have excellent communication and digital skills
  • Be able to work in a team and work with limited supervision
  • Be able to lift and carry

How to apply:

Applications must be submitted online via the Lancashire County Council website. Please ensure you upload a supporting statement, with examples of how you meet the criteria for the role. Details about the role and the criteria can be found on the linked Job Description and Person Specification document.

Further information:

If you would like an informal discussion about the post or any further information not listed on the advert, please contact Kathryn Newman on 01772 533039 or Alex Miller on 01772 539076.

Why join us?

  • A competitive salary and access to the Local Government Pension Scheme with generous employer contributions.
  • A great holiday entitlement of 26 days annual leave (pro rata), rising with length of service, plus Bank Holidays.
  • Weekend pay enhancements.
  • Employee Assistance Programme, credit union, counselling, and discounts on phone contracts, gym and lots more!

We reserve the right to close a vacancy early, before the closing date, if we receive sufficient applications.

Local Government Reorganisation

The Government has confirmed that local government across Lancashire will be reorganised, with the current 15 councils being replaced by four new unitary councils covering North, South, East and West Lancashire from April 2028.

If you are successful in your application, you will initially join Lancashire County Council. However, as part of the planned transition, your employment will transfer to one of the new unitary councils from April 2028, subject to the implementation of the reorganisation and relevant employment legislation.

Throughout this period, our focus remains on delivering excellent services to our communities. By joining us now, you'll play an important role in shaping the future of local government and helping to build a strong new organisation that will serve residents for years to come.

title: Principal Analyst, ERP
description:
Principal Analyst, ERP POSITION PROFILE

As a Principal Analyst, you will scope and lead large projects, working closely with the architecture and development teams to deliver solutions that enable our Sales and Enterprise Service Delivery teams to continue growing and evolving Ricoh's business. You will work under the general direction of a Director or Senior Technology Manager, providing expertise and technical guidance that is backed up by an in-depth cross functional understanding of the applications and/or architecture.

JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Leads functional analysis, gap identification and requirements definition for large sized projects in the assigned function.
  • Provides in depth functional/application expertise within the assigned function including conducting in depth quality reviews on design and testing.
  • Provides in depth cross functional expertise around the assigned function.
  • Recommends / suggests alternatives on solutions to business challenges.
  • Partners with functional business leaders to understand the business strategy and challenges, define business requirements and implement new business processes.
  • Communicates and coordinates with other team leads, business leadership, and Project Manager to ensure appropriate integration of processes and modules across the enterprise.
  • Leads and executes projects and initiatives in full compliance with defined processes and controls.
  • Oversees, defines and monitors critical path activities and resolves issues or escalates issues to the Project Manager as needed.
  • Drives the design and implementation of new business processes with organizational structure and required system configuration.
  • Stays abreast of the latest tools / applications / techniques in the assigned area.
  • Proactively recommends alternatives, approaches to business problems in the assigned area, consults on technology challenges, system issues and implementing cross functional solutions.
  • Participates in the decision making process around technology strategy, conducts analysis on technical viability of solutions and provides guidance on delivery of complex projects.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
QUALIFICATIONS (Education, Experience and Certifications) Typically Required:
  • Bachelors or Masters Degree in Information Technology or related field.
  • Minimum of 9 years of experience in Information Technology.
  • Minimum of 7 years experience with gathering requirements and documentation.
  • Minimum of 7 years experience with testing and defect management.
  • Minimum of 5 years experience leading complex IT projects.
  • Experience managing large to medium size projects that span the company enterprise, defining milestone dates and managing delivery.
  • Experience managing multiple large projects simultaneously.
  • Proven ability to coordinate and drive cross-functional discussions as necessary.
  • Experience establishing and maintaining relationships with various senior level stakeholders.
  • Solid knowledge of ERP and eCommerce Platforms: Oracle eBusiness Suite, CPQ and Fusion/OSC, Agentic AI and eCommerce such as Spryker.
  • Hands on experience gathering requirements, driving design, and owning solutions from end to end.
  • Should be familiar with Sales, Order to Cash lifecycle.
  • Experience negotiating competing or conflicting business requests.
  • PMP/Agile/Product Owner certification is plus.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES
  • Possesses ability to interpret business needs and translate them to create complex solutions.
  • Conducts research around best practices and has ability to adequately document created solutions.
  • Possesses ability to effectively communicate with people at multiple levels. Requires excellent negotiation skills.
  • Possesses facilitation skills including ability to organize, conduct and document effective meetings.
  • Possesses ability to clearly communicate technical and procedural information verbally and in written documentation form.
  • Possesses ability to recognize conflict situations and resolve many; escalates those that cannot be resolved.
  • Possesses ability to determine resolution for routine and non-routine issues; recognizes issues for escalation.
  • Possesses very good customer service and interpersonal skills; is motivated and team oriented.
  • Possesses ability to prioritize multiple tasks and projects, is organized and dependable.
  • Possesses ability to work in a fast paced and changing environment with minimal supervision.
  • Possesses ability to create, modify and execute complex project plans and participate in plan implementation with little direction.
  • Strategic thinker with courage to challenge requests and inspire collaboration for more innovative solutions.
  • Strong delegation skills, and quick decision making.
WORKING CONDITIONS, MENTAL AND PHYSICAL DEMANDS
  • Typically, an office environment with adequate lighting and ventilation, and a normal range of temperature and noise level.
  • Work assignments are diversified. Interpret, comprehend and apply complex material, data and instruction; prepare, provide and convey diversified information.
  • Minimal physical effort required. Work is mostly sedentary but does require walking, standing, bending, reaching, lifting or carrying objects that typically weigh less than 10 lbs. (e.g., papers, books, files and small parts, etc.). Moderate dexterity; regular application of basic skills (calculator, keyboard, hand tools, eye/hand coordination).

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, skills, efforts or working conditions associated with a job.

title: Para I Speech - Millbrooke
description:
POSITION TITLE: Para I – Speech

STATUS: Classified – Nonexempt

STARTING SALARY: $15 hourly

Benefits:
  • Health• Dental • Vision • insurance
  • Kansas Public Employee Retirement System (KPERS)
  • Employee assistance program
  • Paid time off
  • Pay dates on the 15th and 30th
POSITION SUMMARY: The job of Para l – Speech was established for the purpose/s of assisting with the provision of speech and language services to identified students by providing instructional lessons under the direction of the Speech/Language Pathologist either in the special education or general education setting; monitoring student behavior; providing information to appropriate school personnel; and performing clerical tasks as determined by the Speech/Language Pathologist.

PRIMARY DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:
  • Provides individual or small group instruction, either in the general or special education classroom under the direction of the Speech/Language Pathologist for the purpose of assisting special education students to develop speech and language, or social skills to appropriately participate in classroom activities.
  • Aids students in and out of classroom (e.g. packing backpacks, note taking, relationship building, field trips, social skills, etc.) for the purpose of providing assistance to students’ speech-language needs and social growth.
  • Occasionally assists students requiring support in addressing personal care needs due to medical condition and/or physical limitations (e.g. restroom, nutritional, etc.) for the purpose of allowing students to function in the school environments.

  • Occasionally implements behavioral plans for students as designed by the IEP team for the purpose of assisting in meeting special education students’ needs and providing a consistent environment under the direction of certified staff.

  • Primarily works with and supports students on the Speech/Language Pathologist’s caseload but may be asked to assist with other students from time to time.
  • Assists students and staff in the use of augmentative and alternate communication devices.
  • Implements education and behavioral programming under the supervision of the classroom certified staff for the purpose of developing new speech/language or social skills for students.
  • Instructs students in a variety of activities in individual and group settings (e.g. articulation, phonology, social skills, language skills, etc.) for the purpose of meeting Individual Educational Program goals under the direction of certified staff.
  • Maintains instructional materials and data sheets for the purpose of ensuring availability of instructional materials and/or providing reliable information regarding student progress under the direction of certified staff.
  • Monitors students during assigned periods within a variety of school environments (e.g. Rest rooms, playgrounds, hallways, bus loading zones, fire drills, assemblies, cafeteria, parking lots, etc.) for the purpose of providing a safe and positive environment conducive to learning.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned for the purpose of ensuring the efficient and effective functioning of the educational team.
Education and Experience Requirements:
  • Job related experience is desired.
  • High school diploma or equivalent. If the school building is classified as Title I, 48 hours of college credit or the ability to pass the Title I assessment test is required.
Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
SKILLS are required to perform multiple tasks with a potential need to upgrade skills in order to meet changing job conditions. Specific skill-based competencies required to satisfactorily perform the functions of the job include: adhering to safety practices; operating standard office equipment including using pertinent software applications; preparing and maintaining accurate records; and using district approved crisis intervention techniques.
KNOWLEDGE is required to perform basic math; read and follow instructions; and understand complex, multi-step written and oral instructions. Specific knowledge-based competencies required to satisfactorily perform the functions of the job include; instructional procedures and practices; age appropriate student activities; safety practices and procedures; conflict resolution; and stages of child development/behavior; and safe handling of blood-borne pathogens and crisis de-escalation techniques.
ABILITY is required to schedule activities, collect data; and use basic, job-related equipment. Flexibility is required to work with others; work with data utilizing defined and similar processes; and operate equipment using standardized methods. Ability is also required to work with a diversity of individuals. Problem solving is required to identify issues and create action plans. Specific ability-based competencies required to satisfactorily perform the functions of the job include: communicating with diverse groups; maintaining confidentiality; setting priorities; working as part of a team; and working with constant interruptions.
Responsibilities include: working under direct supervision using standardized practices; providing student, classroom and building information to certified/classified staff when necessary.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The usual and customary methods of performing the job's functions could occasionally require some of the following physical demands: some lifting, carrying, pushing, and/or pulling; climbing and balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and/or crawling; and fine finger dexterity. Generally, the job requires a combination of sitting, walking and standing.

title: Provisioning & Asset Management Specialist
description:
JOB TITLE: Provisioning & Asset Management Specialist


JOB SUMMARY:

The Provisioning & Asset Management Specialist is responsible for the provisioning of network and voice equipment — including routers, switches, LTE gateways, voice gateways, and HPBX endpoints — and for the tracking, warehousing, and lifecycle management of that equipment through its full lifecycle. The role receives equipment and provisioning requests via ticketing system from Support, Order Admin, and Service Delivery Network Engineers, and executes those requests based on the specifications provided.


This position reports to the Supervisor, Warehouse Operations.


There are no direct reports to this position.


This position regularly supports: Support, Order Admin, and Service Delivery Network Engineering teams.


Work Arrangement: On-site.


Key Responsibilities

Provisioning

  • Provision routers, switches, LTE gateways, voice gateways, and HPBX endpoints per specifications received via ticket from Support, Order Admin, and Service Delivery Network Engineering teams.
  • Validate device configurations against ticket requirements prior to deployment or shipment.
  • Maintain provisioning documentation and standard configuration templates.
  • Escalate incomplete or ambiguous ticket requests back to the originating requester for clarification.

Asset Management

  • Receive, inspect, and log incoming equipment shipments.
  • Assign and track equipment by serial number/asset tag across inventory locations, customer accounts, and deployment status.
  • Maintain accurate real-time inventory records across the equipment lifecycle — receiving, staging, deployment, return, and retirement.
  • Perform periodic inventory audits and reconciliations.
  • Prepare, package, and ship equipment to field locations or customers.
  • Process returns and RMAs, including vendor coordination for defective equipment.
  • Maintain organized, labeled warehouse and staging areas.

License Administration

  • Track software, maintenance, and subscription renewals.
  • Coordinate renewals with vendors and stakeholders.
  • Maintain renewal calendars and records.

Ticket Workflow

  • Receive provisioning and equipment requests via the ticketing system from Support, Order Admin, and Service Delivery Network Engineers.
  • Prioritize and process tickets according to SLA/turnaround targets.
  • Update ticket status and close out completed requests with confirmation details (serial numbers, configuration notes, ship tracking, etc.).

Service Delivery Metrics & KPIs

  • Inventory Accuracy: 98%+
  • Provisioning Accuracy: 98%+
  • Shipping Accuracy: 99%+
  • Ticket SLA Compliance: 95%+

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Required Qualifications:

  • Highschool diploma or GED – required
  • 2+ years of experience in telecom, IT operations, provisioning, logistics, or inventory management. – required
  • Comfort working from a ticketing system and following documented configuration specs. – required
  • Strong organizational and documentation skills. – required
  • Forklift certification - required; must be obtained within 6 months of employment.
  • Working knowledge of routers, switches, LTE gateways, voice/SIP gateway devices, and HPBX endpoints. – highly preferred

Core Competencies

  • Agile – Embraces change; adaptable and flexible; sense of urgency;
  • Innovative – Uses critical thinking; Creativity; Continuous learning; Challenges the status quo;
  • Customer Focused – External/Internal; Creates the exceptional customer experience; demonstrates a sales and service mentality;
  • Collaborative – Teamwork, Proactive knowledge sharing, Constructive Conflict;
  • Accountable – See it, Own it, Solve it, Do it; Hold each other accountable.

Job Specific Competencies

  • Deliver Results – Strategic planning and execution; Makes decisions in the best interest of the Company; Knows and responds to the business climate; Manages ambiguity
  • Displays Leadership – Role Model; Communicates vision; possesses Emotional Maturity; Manages Risks; Resiliency; Business Acumen

Career Progression

Provisioning & Asset Management Specialist I

Performs equipment provisioning, inventory transactions, and shipping/receiving activities under established processes and documented specifications.

Provisioning & Asset Management Specialist II

Handles complex provisioning activities across router, switch, LTE, voice gateway, and HPBX endpoint deployments; owns inventory reconciliation, exception handling, and process improvement initiatives.


PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Standing, walking, bending, and reaching required for warehouse and staging activities. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds.


WORKING CONDITIONS

  • This is a full-time, non-exempt on-site position based at Telesystem’s warehouse/operations facility.
  • The Company is a drug-free workplace. All employees are required to adhere to the Company’s drug-free workplace programs and policies. Pre-employment testing is mandatory and subject to random testing throughout employment.
  • The duties assigned, the hours worked, and the status of this position is subject to change as the needs of the company changes.

USE OF COMPANY RESOURCES, EQUIPMENT AND CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION

Company resources, equipment, and information are provided to employees to facilitate work. They may not be used for purposes other than work without proper authorization. Any unauthorized use of Company resources, equipment, or information is strictly prohibited. Any unauthorized use of customer data or any other company information gained via any company resource is a breach of confidentiality and is strictly prohibited. Any unauthorized use of company resources, equipment information, and/or breaches of confidentiality may be cause for termination of employment.

The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this job. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required.

title: Senior Project Associate (Livelihoods)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is the leading inter-governmental organization in the field of migration and works closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all and does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.
IOM is a major actor in post-conflict recovery and reconstruction, and as such is heavily involved in livelihoods development and job creation programs. IOM’s strengths lie in its field presence around the country and operational capacity to rebuild community infrastructure, conduct vocational and other trainings, provide grant funding at local level to support business development, and support a variety of other areas key to recovery.
Under the overall supervision of Livelihoods Senior Programme Coordinator and the direct supervision of the Program Coordinator – Livelihoods, the incumbent will be responsible for supporting programs related to livelihoods portfolio under the area of responsibility. The post will be based in Baghdad, Iraq, with travel/roving to various regions/governorates within Iraq as needed to support livelihoods activities and teams.

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Support the Program Coordinator in planning, coordinating, and implementing livelihoods activities across the assigned governorates in line with approved workplans, donor requirements, and IOM policies and procedures.

  • Support the Program Coordinator in the day-to-day operational follow-up of livelihoods interventions, including tracking implementation milestones and identifying delivery gaps.

  • Provide day-to-day guidance and operational follow-up to the team leaders and relevant field teams to promote harmonized, timely, and quality implementation across locations.

  • Support the Program Coordinator in beneficiary targeting, verification, prioritization, and selection processes to ensure transparent, criteria-based, and well-documented implementation.

  • Undertake regular travel to field locations to monitor implementation progress, check the quality and timeliness of activities, identify operational bottlenecks, and support field teams in addressing implementation challenges.

  • Support the Program Coordinator in strengthening the capacity of field teams through regular field presence, including on-the-job coaching, mentoring, troubleshooting, and reinforcement of standard operating procedures and tools.

  • In coordination with the Program Coordinator, review field-level documentation, case files, activity records, and implementation updates to ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance prior to onward submission and action.

  • Track implementation progress against agreed plans, targets, and timelines, and followi up with relevant units on delays, payment issues, procurement actions, contractual matters, and other operational bottlenecks affecting delivery.

  • Support and monitor timely and accurate data collection, consolidation, and reporting from field teams, and contribute to updates in relevant information management systems, trackers, and reporting tools.

  • Conduct monitoring visits, spot checks, and validation exercises to verify implementation quality, reported progress, and strengthen compliance with agreed methodologies and standards.

  • In coordination with the Program Coordinator, participate in internal and external coordination meetings with local authorities, partners, community representatives, service providers, and other stakeholders to support effective implementation and problem-solving.

  • Support the Program Coordinator, when specifically delegated during the Program Coordinator’s absence, in maintaining routine operational continuity and day-to-day follow-up of livelihoods activities, while referring strategic, sensitive, supervisory, and higher-level management matters through the appropriate reporting lines.

  • Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the supervisor.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Economics, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Administration, Livelihoods, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or

  • School diploma with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Experience in supporting the implementation, coordination, and monitoring of livelihoods, recovery, resilience, or community stabilization activities.

  • Experience in field-level operational follow-up, implementation tracking, and coordination with field teams across multiple locations.

  • Experience in conducting monitoring visits, reviewing activity documentation, and following up on implementation issues to support timely and quality delivery.

  • Experience in working with international organizations, UN agencies, NGOs, or donor-funded programs is an advantage.

  • Experience in coordinating with local authorities, service providers, community representatives, and other operational stakeholders is desirable.

  • Experience in data collection, consolidation, reporting, and use of implementation tracking tools is desirable.

  • Experience working in complex or post-conflict environments is an advantage.

Skills

  • Position specific skills, for example:

  • Knowledge of livelihoods, recovery, resilience, or community-based programming approaches.

  • Good understanding of field implementation, operational follow-up, and monitoring processes.

  • Ability to review activity documentation, track implementation progress, and support timely reporting.

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities under tight deadlines.

  • Strong communication and coordination skills, with the ability to work effectively with colleagues and stakeholders from diverse backgrounds.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

  • Knowledge of data management, reporting tools, and information tracking systems is an advantage.

Languages

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position,

Fluency in English is required

Arabic is an advantage Language

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.
  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.
  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.

Notes

Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Case Technician-Night Shift
description:
The Case Tech assists in the preparation of the surgical room prior to procedures, transporting patients to specific operating areas as needed, and in maintaining an adequate supply of sterilized equipment, instruments and supplies necessary during surgical procedures. Ensures that all instruments and equipment are in good working condition at all times and promptly facilitates their repair when needed.

    1. Performs other duties as assigned or requested.

title: Resource Spending Lead - C1
description:

The Resource Spending Unit plays a central role in shaping the Scottish Government’s resource budget, reporting and scrutiny of spending places, supporting strategic decision-making and ensuring effective allocation of public funds. The postholder will lead work across the budget cycle, working closely with portfolios, Public Service Reform colleagues, and senior leaders to drive improved outcomes and value for money.

This is a high-profile role at the centre strategic spending analysis, stakeholder engagement, and delivery of key fiscal outputs including supporting the Budget, Medium Term Financial Strategy, and Spending Review processes.

Key responsibilities:

  • Drive improved understanding of public spending, this could include areas such as supporting place-based and preventative budgeting approaches
  • Support cross-government decision making, aligning resources to priorities such as Public Service Reform and Programme for Government commitments

Experience:

Technical/Professional Skills

  • provide clear communication at varying levels of seniority and audiences, including drafting concise briefings and submissions

Working pattern

Our standard hours are 35 hours per week and we offer a range of flexible working options depending on the needs of the role, including Flexi-leave. title: Senior Product Manager
description:
About GeneralMind

GeneralMind builds AI Systems of Action for complex enterprise workflows. We deploy AI employees that automate messy operational handovers across supply chains - processing orders, validating invoices, coordinating suppliers, and handling exceptions directly on top of enterprise systems like SAP, Oracle, JDE, and Dynamics.

Our platform combines AI agents, operational context graphs, and real transaction data to achieve Autopilot-grade automation in real operational environments.

We work closely with leading global companies across manufacturing, retail, and logistics to deploy AI into mission-critical workflows.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager who can operate at the intersection of enterprise operations, AI systems, and platform product strategy.

You will work closely with customers, founders, and engineering teams to understand how large enterprises actually operate: ERP systems, supply chain workflows, approvals, exceptions, emails, spreadsheets, and fragmented operational processes.

This is not a traditional roadmap-management role. A core part of the job is identifying the reusable platform hidden underneath customer-specific operational problems. You will help determine what becomes a platform capability and what stays customer-specific, where configuration ends and engineering begins, where AI can reliably automate workflows, and where humans should remain in the loop.

What You'll Do

  • Work directly with enterprise customers to deeply understand operational workflows and pain points.

  • Translate customer realities into scalable product and platform decisions.

  • Define roadmap priorities across platform, workflow, and AI capabilities.

  • Collaborate closely with engineering teams on architecture and product tradeoffs.

  • Drive product thinking around AI agents, workflow orchestration, and enterprise operations.

  • Identify recurring patterns across customers and turn them into reusable product abstractions.

  • Help define the long-term platform strategy of the company.

  • Improve how we capture, operationalise, and learn from customer feedback.

What we are looking for

  • Strong product thinking and systems intuition.

  • Deep understanding of enterprise operations, supply chain workflows, or ERP systems.

  • Ability to operate effectively in highly technical environments.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.

  • Ability to balance customer needs with long-term platform strategy.

  • A strong ownership mentality and execution focus.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-moving startup environments.

  • Fluency in English.

  • Excitement about AI-native products and autonomous systems.

Children's Home Assistant Manager

Accrington

Salary up to £42,123

We are currently recruiting…

Children's Homes Assistant Manager to work within our expanding Children's Residential at Lancashire County Council.

At Lancashire County Council, we believe that every child deserves more than just a place to stay – they deserve a loving home filled with compassion, understanding, and endless possibilities. If you're a passionate and dedicated individual with a heart for children's well-being, we want to welcome you to our growing family!

To ensure that there is adequate management cover in the home, you will be expected to work within the core hours of 7am – 7pm and therefore undertake alternating shifts of 7am – 3pm and 11am 7pm.

We are keen to hear from both experienced Assistant Managers and those looking to take that next step where we can support you into your first management position. Are you a residential, youth or social worker wanting to progress your career? Then this could be the opportunity you have been waiting for. We would love to hear from you!

What we are looking for…

Passion – You'll be passionate about young people and the difference that you can make to their lives and outcomes for the future. You'll be dynamic and inspirational with ethics, values and integrity at the heart of what you do. Your enthusiasm and dedication will play a pivotal role in creating a positive and enriching experience for the amazing children in our care, and creating a strength based, positive culture for our workforce.

Creative & Innovative – For some posts, the staff team will be a brand-new so you'll have the opportunity to shape and define the culture from the start, encouraging those in your team to "think outside the box" when it comes to connecting and supporting children and young people who will potentially have personal challenges to overcome. You'll also find creative solutions to your own leadership challenges working closely with social work teams, and professionals from health, education, police, and the community.

Inspirational & Supportive Leadership– There's no doubt that this is an emotionally difficult and challenging role so you'll be personally resilient and appreciate the impact that those challenges can have upon your team - empowering them on a regular basis and providing additional support where required. One of the benefits of working for a local authority is the additional support that's easily and readily available for you. You will have access to psychological support for you and your team; regular supervision with your Registered Manager, opportunity to engage in reflective learning circles with our Practice Development Managers and a whole suite of informal and formal training opportunities.

Why join us…

Benefits: There's fabulous flexibility and the opportunity to create a work life balance you'll love - with up to 32 days annual leave plus bank holidays, 2 additional days at Christmas plus 20 additional days leave that you can purchase. We also have a generous local authority pension with shared contribution AVC's available, and a benefits package that will exceed your expectations, from a 24/7 Employee Assistance Program to a range of discounts with our new Vivup benefits platform including retail, leisure and entertainment discounts, plus salary sacrifice for white goods, electronics, cars, bicycles and much more!

Development: We are an expanding service, and with this comes an expanding variety of opportunities. In addition to our 50+ free training courses, we also offer professional qualifications (to degree level) as part of our apprenticeship scheme. There will be time for supportive reflection and supervision for yourself, and opportunities to carve out your individualised and defined career pathway. We offer multidisciplinary initiatives, mentoring, the opportunity to make a difference, feel valued and achieve the job satisfaction you've always wanted.

Inclusivity: We don't have a "one size fits all" idealism, we embrace diversity and that includes around personal and family requirements so we're happy to offer an array of flexible working opportunities. We are committed to creating and sustaining a diverse and inclusive working environment for all of our team. Our aim is to ensure that everyone is equally valued and respected and that our organisation is representative of all members of society, working in an environment where individual differences are celebrated. To support this, we would especially welcome applications from those from a diverse background who would enhance our service by joining us and we have some great support groups and forums available for anyone to join.

How to apply …

We would love to hear from you so please feel free to contact us for an initial informal and confidential chat…

Email Senior Manager, Claire Rose Dudley on claire.dudley@lancashire.gov.uk.

If successful you will be required to apply to the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) for a 'disclosure'. Further information can be found on the 'Our Recruitment Process' tab.

title: Policy Manager
description:
This is an Expression of Interest (EOI) opportunity, available on a lateral move basis only. Applications are open to Core Scottish Government employees only.

Job Title - Policy Manager

Business Area/Directorate - Mental Health and Incapacity Law Unit

Location - St Andrews House

Working Arrangement – Staff in roles compatible with hybrid working should spend 40% of their contracted working time working in person at their contractual workplace. More information can be found within Hybrid Working Policy

Grade - B3

Advert type - Level Transfer

Duration - The post is for maternity cover for just under one year (from early November 2026 to October 2027).

Eligibility - Expressions of interest are invited from substantive colleagues on level transfer from core SG only.

Sponsorship: Skilled Worker sponsorship is not available for this role. As a result, we are unable to appoint candidates who require Skilled Worker sponsorship now or in the future. Applicants must have an existing and ongoing right to work in the UK.

Job description

This post offers the unique opportunity to drive policy that will deliver real benefit for some of the most vulnerable people in society. The work of the Mental Health and Incapacity Law Unit is focussed on improving people’s lives through its focus on the rights and protections of people with mental ill health and those adults that lack capacity. The Unit has a range of policy functions which centre around human rights, ethics, social welfare and ensuring equality.

The work of the unit has been shaped by the Scottish Mental Health Law Review (SMHLR) which reported in 2022. The strong recommendation of this review was that a new overall approach to mental health and capacity law was required. The law should have a new purpose, namely, to ensure that the human rights of people with mental or intellectual disability are respected, protected and fulfilled. It was recognised in the final report, however, that such a radical change would take several years to achieve. The Scottish Government published its initial response to the review in June 2023 (Scottish mental health law review: our response - gov.scot (www.gov.scot)).

This post provides a leading role in driving forward our ambition to embed human rights across our policies through reform of the Adults with Incapacity Act. This work focuses on developing policy intent to inform legislative change to be introduced in the next parliamentary term.

It is important that work is taken forward collaboratively across SG and with wider stakeholders. The successful candidate must therefore be experienced in this approach. An Expert Working Group and a Ministerial Oversight Group was established in September 2025 to bring both pace and priority to this work and the postholder will be expected to work constructively with both to build consensus on reform proposals.

The work of the AWI team is framed around a number of workstreams including:

  • ​Powers of Attorney

  • Deprivation of Liberty

  • Guardianships

  • Medical Treatment, Forced Detention and Covert Medicine

  • Managing Residents' Finances

  • Access to Funds

The postholder will be expected to work with a degree of autonomy in driving forward workstreams.

The work of the unit is dynamic and fast-paced. The post-holder will be expected to be flexible in responding to changing and emerging priorities.

Responsibilities

  • Work collaboratively and constructively with the AWI Expert Working Group and Ministerial Oversight Group to develop and drive consensus on reform proposals.

  • Lead on project management including risk assessment.

  • Develop and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with key partners.

  • Work with SGLD to assess policy proposals against human rights requirements to support readiness for future legislation.

  • Undertake ongoing impact assessments in relation to emerging policy proposals.

  • Line management responsibility for 1xB2.

Success Profile
Success profiles are specific to each job and they include the mix of skills, experience and behaviours candidates will be assessed on, you should provide evidence of how you meet these in your statement.

Behaviours:
  • Making Effective Decisions – Level 3
  • Working Together - Level 3
  • Delivering at Pace - Level 3
You can find out more about Success Profiles on gov.scot.

Working pattern
This role is a temporary position with an expected commitment of 11 months.
This post is a full-time role, but we welcome applications from staff with different working patterns, proposed working patterns will be assessed against the business requirements for this post.
Our standard hours are 35 hours per week and we offer a range of flexible working options depending on the needs of the role, including Flexi-leave. Scottish Government staff in hybrid-compatible roles should aim to work in-person 40% of the time, either in an office or other agreed work location.

Further Information

Further information about this opportunity is available from gill.scott@gov.scot.

How to Apply

Please submit an Expression of Interest (maximum 500 words) outlining your suitability for the role, relevant skills and experience, and what you would bring to the team. Please align this to how you meet the behaviours, experience and technical skills listed in the Success Profile above.

Vacancies close at 23:59pm on Tuesday 27 October.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can be used to support your application, but all statements and examples provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, and presented as your own) applications will be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action.

Please see our candidate guidance for more information on acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI in recruitment.

If invited for further assessment, this will consist of a light-touch interview, scheduled for w/c TBC.

Recruitment Principles

As a government organisation, we adhere to the Civil Service Commission Recruitment Principles and we investigate any complaints received in relation to recruitment cases.

About us

The Scottish Government is the devolved government for Scotland. We have responsibility for a wide range of key policy areas including: education, health, the economy, justice, housing and transport. We offer rewarding careers and employ people across Scotland in a wide range of professions and roles.

Our staff are part of the UK Civil Service observing the Civil Service Code and working for Ministers and senior stakeholders to deliver vital public services which improve the lives of the people of Scotland.

We offer a supportive and inclusive working environment along with a wide range of employee benefits. Find out more about what we offer.

As part of the UK Civil Service, we uphold the Civil Service Nationality Rules.

Security checks

Successful candidates must complete the Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS), before they can be appointed. BPSS is comprised of four main pre-employment checks – Identity, Right to work, Employment History and a Criminal Record check (unspent convictions).

You can find out more about BPSS on the UK Government website, or read about the different levels of security checks in our Candidate Guide.

Equality statement

We are committed to equality and inclusion and we aim to recruit a diverse workforce that reflects the population of our nation.

Find out more about our commitment to diversity and how we offer and support recruitment adjustments for anyone who needs them.

Further information

Find out more about our organisation, what we offer staff members and how to apply on our Careers Website.

Read our Candidate Guide for further information on our recruitment and application processes.
