title: Client Group Risk and Controls Director, Asia Pacific
description:
Who we’re looking for
We’re looking for a Client Group Risk and Controls Director, as part of the Global Client Group Risk and Controls Team. The role has two key elements of responsibility and requires an individual with the willingness and ability to support, oversee and challenge business activities from a risk and regulatory perspective, whilst adopting a commercial mindset.

The two key areas of responsibility are as follows:
1) Support the Head of Client Group, Asia and their management team by:
• Providing a governance framework which ensures the Client Group in Asia’s activities are carried out in a way which demonstrably meets regulatory obligations;
• Acting as an internal SME and escalation point for risk events, regulatory issues and regulatory change;
• Helping to identify and manage both ongoing and emerging risks within the business; and
• Supporting the management and governance of regulated entities in Asia.

2) Support the Global Head of Client Group Risk and Controls by:
• Helping with the development and leadership of global client group programs in areas including risk event management, risk and control assessments, conduct and conflicts of interest;
• Deputising for the Global Head of Client Group Risk and Controls where required; and
• Ensuring a consistent governance framework is applied globally.

About Us
Schroders is a global investment manager which provides active asset management, wealth management and investment solutions. We aim to provide excellent investment performance to clients through active management. We serve a diverse client base that includes pension schemes, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, foundations, high net worth individuals, family offices, as well as end clients through partnerships with distributors, financial advisers, and online platforms.

Established in 1804, we have around 5,500 people across 36 global locations. Schroders' success can be attributed to its diversified business model, spanning different asset classes, client types and geographies.


The base
The position is based in Singapore, at our Capita Green office.

The team
You will sit in the Client Group Risk and Control team, reporting to the Global Head of Client Group Rick and Controls. The team is led by the Global Head of Client Group Risk and Controls, with regional support provided by the wider team. The team will be managed from a UK hub, as the largest region and headquarters of Schroders Plc. This role will be based in Singapore, as a local specialist will be required given the unique nature and complexity of the market in Asia. The business in Asia is involved with a wide range of client types and investment strategies, as well as being subject to different regulatory regimes facing differing scrutiny country to country.


This team sits more broadly within Shroders’ Client Group, which is responsible for business development, client service, product development, marketing and communications. The Risk and controls team enables core sales and client service activity by providing the necessary support on risk management, regulatory compliance and entity governance. This enables:
• More time for client facing staff to focus on core activities.
• Proper management of risks.
• Provable compliance with Regulations and Group Policies.
• A trusted advisor within the business, who understands the business.

What you'll do
The Client Group Risk and Controls Director, Asia must develop and deliver a governance framework that ensures the Client Group in Asia’s activities are carried out in a way that meets our regulatory obligations; where regulatory compliance can be evidenced; where the risks faced are understood and controlled; and where group policies are understood and followed.

The role works closely with the Client Group management team in Asia, as well as other internal stakeholders, including: risk, compliance, legal, operations and corporate functions. The Client Group Risk and Control Director, Asia acts as a bridge between client needs, internal teams and regulatory requirements, with a focus on enabling commercial success within a risk-controlled environment.

The Client Group Risk and Controls Director, Asia is responsible for:
• Oversight of the response to, and recording of, risk events within the business, ensuring that they are remediated in an appropriate manner, and that the right lessons are learned;
• Managing dedicated forums where senior management in Asia are brought together to discuss current and emerging risks and regulatory issues, with a focus on raising awareness, and sharing lessons learned;
• Understanding and documenting the key risks facing the client group in Asia, in line with group wide risk and control assessment processes;
• Monitoring key risk areas and providing regular feedback to management on items of concern, or where remediation is required;
• Delivering client group operational resilience requirements, working with senior management to ensure important business services and essential communication channels are identified, and that resilience can be demonstrated;
• Managing consumer duty board reporting requirements, ensuring that entity boards are sufficiently well informed to discharge their responsibilities;
• Representing the Client Group in Asia in regulatory change projects, ensuring the needs of clients are represented, then ensuring the business is aware of new requirements once finalised;
• Delivering the Asian requirements of global client group control programs;
• Acting as a local Financial Crime SME, supporting business management in resolving issues and overseeing policy compliance.

The knowledge, experience and qualifications you need

• Minimum 10 years in Asset Management is highly preferred
• Reliable – demonstrate accountability for your responsibilities on a timely and accurate manner
• Diligent - highly reliable, with excellent attention to detail and a disciplined approach to follow-through and timely follow-up.
• Organised – ability to effectively prioritise multiple tasks, meet deadlines, report on progress
• Effective communicator – an exceptional ability to communicate clearly both in writing and verbally
• Energetic – proactive and flexible work attitude alongside passion for delivering
• Results – driven and process-focussed – motivated by achieving results and delivery
• Time management – excellent conflict resolution and time management skills including the ability to maintain composure and diffuse challenging situations
• Collaborative – team driven, with an ability to influence and change the thinking of others
• Strategically minded – able to take a broader strategic perspective, particularly when it comes to development of fund and client solutions
• Relationship building – able to build strong relationships both internally and externally
• Deep knowledge of Fund structures and operational processes
• Able to challenge yourself and others constructively

We Recognise Potential, Whoever You Are
Our purpose is to deliver excellent investment performance to clients through active management. We believe diverse perspectives and an inclusive culture help us make better decisions and achieve better outcomes for our clients. That's why inclusion is a strategic priority for us, and we are an equal opportunities employer. You are welcome here, regardless of your age, disability, gender identity, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, socio-economic background, or any other protected characteristic.


We will consider flexible working arrangements for all roles and provide reasonable accommodations to support applicants and employees, including those with neurodiversity, disability, or physical and mental health needs. For more information, please visit our FAQs.

title: Senior Project Associate (Livelihoods)- Anbar
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is the leading inter-governmental organization in the field of migration and works closely with governmental, intergovernmental, and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all and does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.
IOM is a major actor in post-conflict recovery and reconstruction, and as such is heavily involved in livelihoods development and job creation programmes. IOM’s strengths lie in its field presence around the country and operational capacity to rebuild community infrastructure, conduct vocational and other trainings, provide grant funding at local level to support business development, and support a variety of other areas key to recovery.
Under the overall supervision of Head of Livelihoods Technical team and the direct supervision of the National Project Officer – Livelihoods, the incumbent will be responsible for supporting programmes related to livelihoods portfolio under the area of responsibility. The post will be based in Anbar, Iraq, with travel/roving to various regions/governorates within Iraq as needed to support livelihoods activities and teams.

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Working in close coordination with the Operations Regional Coordinator and Team Leaders across governorates in Iraq, provide technical guidance to field staff on the implementation of all activities under the livelihoods portfolio, in line with livelihoods tools, policies and procedures.

  • Provide technical guidance to field teams across Iraq to conduct livelihoods assessments, including labor market and supply chain mapping, in line with livelihoods technical tools.

  • In coordination with Team Leaders and community engagement technical teams across governorates in Iraq, provide technical inputs and guidance to support the identification and selection of individuals, households, communities, and other target groups for livelihoods assistance, in line with livelihoods guidelines and policies.

  • Assist Team Leaders in identifying partners and creating opportunities with local authorities, private sector actors, livelihoods sub-clusters, associations, chambers of commerce/industry, and other relevant stakeholders to support the implementation of IOM’s livelihoods portfolio across Iraq.

  • Provide support and guidance to field teams in assisting selected beneficiaries and target groups by facilitating orientation meetings, livelihoods trainings, business development support, counselling, mentoring, and other relevant forms of technical assistance as needed.

  • Travel to project sites across Iraq, as required, to monitor livelihoods activities and beneficiaries receiving support under the livelihood’s portfolio; ensure that activities are implemented in accordance with livelihoods guidelines and provide guidance to Team Leaders on necessary improvements or changes to livelihoods service delivery.

  • Follow up with field teams across Iraq to quality check data and service delivery, monitor progress against workplans, and make recommendations in coordination with Team Leaders.

  • Organize and conduct satisfaction and feedback surveys to improve future livelihoods interventions; provide guidance to livelihoods teams and Team Leaders to improve the delivery, quality, and relevance of livelihoods assistance.

  • In coordination with Team Leaders and community engagement technical teams across Iraq, identify challenges and present recommendations to strengthen operational and implementation capacities, and suggest capacity-building measures to maintain effective operational systems.

  • Develop and maintain internal control and compliance processes related to livelihoods programming and recommend to the National Project Officer – Livelihoods measures to strengthen those controls.

  • Support field teams across Iraq to mainstream gender, disability, protection, environmental considerations, accountability to affected populations, and other cross-cutting issues into

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Economics, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Administration, Livelihoods, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or

  • School diploma with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Experience in government engagement, public sector coordination, institutional partnerships, or development‑related work, preferably within an international organization, UN agency, donor‑funded programme, or comparable public institution.

  • Experience in working in an international environment and in liaising with a variety of partners at all levels of the hierarchy.

  • Experience working with government ministries or public authorities at national and/or sub‑national levels.

  • Familiarity with government systems and public administration processes, preferably in Iraq or similar contexts.

  • Ability to meet deadlines and work under pressure

  • Excellent communication and negotiation skills.

  • Ability to work effectively and harmoniously with colleagues from varied cultures and professional backgrounds.

Skills

  • Position specific skills, for example:

  • Knowledge of livelihoods, recovery, resilience, or community-based programming approaches.

  • Good understanding of field implementation, operational follow-up, and monitoring processes.

  • Ability to review activity documentation, track implementation progress, and support timely reporting.

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities under tight deadlines.

  • Strong communication and coordination skills, with the ability to work effectively with colleagues and stakeholders from diverse backgrounds.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

  • Knowledge of data management, reporting tools, and information tracking systems is an advantage.

Languages

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position,

Fluency in English is required

Arabic is an advantage Language

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.

title: Product Line Manager - Industrial Controls
description:
Position Overview

The Product Line Manager is responsible for the strategy, performance, and lifecycle management of an assigned industrial controls product portfolio within an electrical power distribution manufacturing business. This role connects customer and market needs with Engineering, Sales, Operations, Supply Chain, and Quality to drive competitive, manufacturable solutions, profitable growth, and reliable delivery. The position supports products such as industrial control panels, motor control solutions, automation-related assemblies, and associated engineered configurations.


Key Responsibilities


1. Product Strategy & Portfolio Management

  • Develop and maintain product line strategy, positioning, roadmaps, and lifecycle plans aligned with business priorities.
  • Assess market trends, competitive offerings, customer requirements, and applicable industrial control applications.
  • Identify opportunities for new products, standard configurations, upgrades, and product rationalization.
  • Define product requirements, target applications, and differentiation in collaboration with technical teams.
  • Monitor product line performance and recommend actions to improve growth, margin, and customer value.

2. Commercial & Financial Performance

  • Partner with Sales on product positioning, customer opportunities, quotations, and technical-commercial alignment.
  • Support pricing strategy, cost targets, margin analysis, and profitability improvement initiatives.
  • Analyze bookings, revenue, backlog, product mix, and demand forecasts to inform decisions.
  • Provide product knowledge and sales enablement materials for customer-facing teams.
  • Coordinate launch plans and communicate product updates to internal stakeholders.

3. Engineering & Product Development

  • Translate voice-of-customer input into clear product requirements and development priorities.
  • Partner with Electrical and Mechanical Engineering on industrial control panel designs, configurations, and documentation.
  • Participate in design reviews and evaluate tradeoffs involving performance, cost, lead time, and manufacturability.
  • Support product validation, change management, and resolution of recurring technical or quality issues.
  • Promote applicable standards and customer specification awareness, including UL 508A and relevant NFPA/NEC requirements as appropriate.

4. Manufacturing & Supply Chain Coordination

  • Collaborate with Operations, Production, Quality, and Supply Chain to support build readiness and on-time delivery.
  • Identify opportunities for standardization, modularity, component commonality, and cost reduction.
  • Help resolve product-related material constraints, obsolescence, and supplier challenges.
  • Support capacity planning and demand visibility for product families and major opportunities.
  • Coordinate improvements to bills of materials, work instructions, and product data accuracy.

5. Cross-Functional Leadership & Continuous Improvement

  • Lead product line reviews, communicate priorities, and align stakeholders on decisions and milestones.
  • Coordinate product launches, phase-outs, training, and internal change communications.
  • Use customer feedback, field issues, and operational metrics to prioritize corrective and improvement actions.
  • Build strong working relationships across Sales, Engineering, Project Management, and Operations.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Product Management, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience considered.
  • Experience in product management, product line leadership, applications engineering, or technical commercial roles within industrial electrical equipment.
  • Knowledge of industrial control panels, motor controls, PLC-based systems, automation components, and electrical distribution applications preferred.
  • Familiarity with industrial control panel standards and requirements, including UL 508A and applicable NEC/NFPA provisions, preferred.
  • Ability to interpret customer specifications and collaborate on technical product requirements.
  • Experience with pricing, margin analysis, product lifecycle management, and ERP/MRP systems preferred.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership, analytical, communication, and project prioritization skills.
  • Ability to work in a manufacturing environment and travel to company sites, suppliers, or customers as needed.

title: Regional Specialty Program Manager
description:
Parallel Management Group is looking for a Regional Specialty Program Director. This role leads the rollout, training, and ongoing support of Parallel's specialty resident programs — spanning memory care training, end-of-life doula support, and restorative care — across the communities they support. This role partners with building and regional leadership to determine which programs are the right fit for each community and in what order they should be introduced, then works directly with onsite teams (Life Enrichment Directors, Memory Care Coordinators, Wellness Coordinators, Restorative Aides, and End-of-Life Doulas) to launch each program and keep it running well over time.


General Responsibilities

  • Schedule and host ongoing training experiences for staff at all communities within the region.
  • Communicate with building and regional management to identify which specialty programs are appropriate for new communities, and implement programs in order of priority.
  • Provide ongoing support to the staff responsible for day-to-day program delivery, including Life Enrichment Directors, Memory Care Coordinators, Wellness Coordinators, Restorative Aides, and End-of-Life Doulas (where applicable).
  • Hold individual meetings or video calls with communities on a biweekly basis once their programs are established, to check in on progress and provide continued support.
  • Send communities reminders throughout the month to keep program submissions and follow-through on track, and assist communities with carrying out resident requests as needed, with hands-on support for communities that are new to a program.
  • Collect submissions from all communities each month and compile them into a newsletter distributed across the region.

Memory Care & Dementia Training Program Responsibilities

  • Facilitate hands-on staff training experiences, including virtual dementia simulation training, meaningful engagement training, and challenging behavior training (some sessions require a co-facilitator).
  • Launch the program in new communities with memory care: complete resident cognitive assessments, install sensory/way-finding displays, and assemble staff sensory boxes.
  • Launch family education nights in new communities and attend the first several sessions until the community is ready to run them independently.
  • Follow up regularly with onsite staff to confirm the program is being maintained, and provide hands-on help to catch communities up as needed.

End-of-Life Doula Program Responsibilities

  • Complete End-of-Life Doula training/certification in order to train community-based doulas.
  • Host doula training classes — increasingly delivered virtually via Zoom to multiple communities at once, rather than spending multiple days on-site training just a few doulas at a time.
  • Help each community identify and establish a lead doula responsible for maintaining doula assignments.
  • Set up doula program binders for new communities and coach the lead doula to maintain them going forward, checking in and providing catch-up support as needed.
  • Plan periodic appreciation events for doulas and arrange ongoing education opportunities.

Restorative Care Program Responsibilities

  • Recruit and train restorative techs to launch and expand the program in additional communities.
  • Monitor restorative documentation and track resident progress.
  • Meet regularly with outside providers involved in the program.
  • Partner across departments to ensure all components of the program are being carried out consistently.
  • Collaborate with a fitness coach to elevate the program, with plans to extend fitness coach support to communities in the West region.

title: ERP Integration Expert
description:
About GeneralMind

GeneralMind builds AI Systems of Action for complex enterprise workflows. We deploy AI employees that automate messy operational handovers across supply chains - processing orders, validating invoices, coordinating suppliers, and handling exceptions directly on top of enterprise systems like SAP, Oracle, JDE, and Dynamics.

Our platform combines AI agents, operational context graphs, and real transaction data to achieve Autopilot-grade automation in real operational environments.

We work closely with leading global companies across manufacturing, retail, and logistics to deploy AI into mission-critical workflows.

About the role

Every GeneralMind deployment stands or falls with one thing: how well our AI agents talk to the customer's ERP. As our ERP Integration Expert, you own exactly that. You design and build the technical bridges between our platform and our customers' ERP landscapes, from digital cores like S/4HANA and ECC to integration platforms like BTP and Integration Suite, and make sure order confirmations, invoices, and master data flow reliably in both directions.

You'll work at the sharpest edge of the company: real enterprise systems, real transaction data, real go-lives. And you'll help turn every integration you build into reusable patterns, so each deployment gets faster than the last.

What You'll Do

  • Own the integration architecture for new customers end to end: assess their ERP landscape, choose the right interface pattern (OData, RFC/BAPI, IDoc/EDI, CPI/BTP, staging tables, file-based), and design something their IT will approve and operate.
  • Lead technical discovery with customer IT, basis, and process teams, and surface the blocking constraint in week one, not week nine.
  • Own the data and field mapping from the customer's order, item, partner, and pricing structures onto our internal model, including the custom fields that carry the real business logic.
  • Design and build our ERP connectors in Python (S/4HANA and ECC, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Salesforce) and turn per-customer work into reusable abstractions, so the tenth connector costs a fraction of the first.
  • Build durable, long-running integration workflows with safe write-back into customer systems of record: idempotency, retries, replay semantics, and recovery paths from the start.
  • Own integration observability: know when a sync is stuck, degraded, or silently writing the wrong thing before the customer notices.
  • Define the authentication, network, and security posture per customer and get it through their review.
  • Feed what you learn in customer landscapes back into the product. You will see the same five problems before anyone else does.

What we are looking for

  • ERP integration depth, non-negotiable: you have delivered productive ERP integrations and know the interface landscape first-hand (IDoc, BAPI/RFC, OData/Gateway, CPI/BTP Integration Suite), on both S/4HANA and ECC, and you know which one to reach for and why.
  • Functional grounding: fluent in at least one of SD (order-to-cash) or MM (procure-to-pay), credible in the other, plus the FI touchpoints for AP/AR. You know what a schedule line, a condition record, and a three-way match actually are.
  • Engineering, not just configuration: 5+ years building and operating backend systems with real Python depth, owning production services rather than just delivering features.
  • Reliability instinct: idempotency, retries, and observability are part of how you design, not afterthoughts. A workflow engine like Temporal in production is a strong plus.
  • Customer-facing credibility: you can stand in front of an enterprise IT department, absorb their constraints, push back where it matters, and leave them confident.
  • End-to-end ownership: you identify what's broken or missing before you're asked, and you don't leave the system worse than you found it.
  • Professional English; German is a strong advantage given our customer base.
  • You're happy being in the office five days a week.

title: Head of Enterprise AI
description:
Control planes, AI models and agents, oh my!

AI is moving really fast. Models can reason and agents can access enterprise knowledge, use tools and take actions. The challenge isn’t whether to use AI, but how to introduce increasingly powerful capabilities safely, economically and at scale.

That’s where you come in.

We’re looking for a Head of Enterprise AI to build our Enterprise AI capability from the ground up, creating the platforms, architecture, governance and controls that make the responsible way to use AI also the easiest way.

Think of it as creating our well-lit pathway into frontier AI.

The opportunity:

This isn’t an AI evangelist role and it’s definitely not about running a collection of interesting pilots.

You’ll build and lead the capability that enables AI to operate in the real world, owning our Enterprise AI Platform and Control Plane, AI governance, model and agent governance, evaluation and observability, secure knowledge access, platform operations and AI economics.

Every major technology decision needs to balance what AI can do, what it should do, what it costs and the risks created along the way. Your job is to turn those trade-offs into architecture, controls and technology that teams can actually use.

You’ll build a highly specialised Enterprise AI team and work across Architecture, Engineering, Security, Group Technology, Risk, Privacy and the broader business to make AI practical at enterprise scale.

What you’ll do

  • Build and evolve our Enterprise AI Platform and Control Plane
    Shape our AI architecture and technology roadmap
    Establish governance for models, agents and AI-enabled solutions
    Make build, buy and partner decisions across the AI ecosystem
    Define secure patterns for enterprise knowledge and agent access
    Build evaluation and observability into production AI
    Make AI consumption, cost and performance visible
    Turn governance requirements into practical technology controls
    Track the frontier and separate meaningful shifts from hype
    Build and lead a specialist Enterprise AI team

What you’ll bring

  • You’re deeply curious about where AI is heading, but pragmatic about how technology gets introduced into a real enterprise.
    You can comfortably move between enterprise strategy and deep technical conversations. You’re prepared to say both “not yet” and “we need to move now”. You prefer simple, usable pathways over bureaucracy for bureaucracy’s sake.
    You’re ambitious about what AI can unlock, without losing sight of the consequences that come with it.
    Significant leadership experience across AI, architecture or platform engineering
    Experience designing and operating enterprise-scale technology platforms
    Production experience with Generative AI, LLMs and agentic architectures
    Deep knowledge of AI platforms, control planes and model lifecycle
    Strong cloud, API, identity and distributed systems architecture expertise
    Experience with AI evaluation, observability and production monitoring
    Strong understanding of AI security, governance and technical controls
    Experience making complex build, buy and partner decisions
    The judgement to balance capability, security, cost and speed
    The curiosity to know what’s genuinely changing at the AI frontier, and what’s just noise

What you’ll get

Not only will you receive an awesome candidate experience from our caring Talent team, but you’ll get a genuine feel for who we are and what it’s like to be part of our team.

The benefits of working with The Lottery Corporation are pretty good. Just to name a few:

  • Balance work and life with our ‘flex for great outcomes’ approach – hybrid working, plus a range of generous leave options.
  • Reward and recognition programs at all levels. Your hard work won’t go unnoticed.
  • Ignite your potential with our dedicated learning and development platform to support your bright future.
  • We empower careers to grow from within. 50% of all roles in 2025 were filled by our own people, proving that your next opportunity is already here!
  • A true sense of belonging. We’re committed to Inclusion & Diversity with a range of initiatives such as our Gender Affirmation Support, employee inclusion networks and diversity memberships and celebrations.
  • Make positive impacts with opportunities to volunteer with our community partners. We'll also dollar match fundraising efforts of our employees lending their support to registered charities.

We’re committed to providing a safe, respectful and supportive work environment. We encourage you to let us know if we can make any accommodations, so the process can be more user friendly for you.

We acknowledge and pay respect to the traditional custodians of the lands on which our offices, retail outlets and venues operate. We acknowledge the inextricable link First Peoples of Australia have with the land past and present.

Your online safety is important to us. We'll never request payment or credit card details from you to apply for a position. If you're uncertain whether a job ad is legitimate, verify via our website before providing any details.

title: CNC Programmer
description:
About Us:

Burloak Technologies is a leader in the additive manufacturing industry, providing engineering services for additive manufacturing, materials development, high-precision CNC machining and metrology. Burloak Technologies works with innovative companies across the aerospace, defense, nuclear and industrial markets to rapidly transition their most challenging part designs to additive manufacturing at scale.


Location:

3280 South Service Road, Oakville, Ontario, CA L6L 0B1, On-site Position


Summary:

The CNC Programmer is responsible for developing machining strategies and CNC programs for additively manufactured components with complex geometries and high-precision requirements. This role translates engineering requirements into effective machining solutions through CNC programming, setup documentation, tooling selection, and workholding and fixture design.


The CNC Programmer supports both milling and turning applications, with a primary focus on multi-axis milling. Working closely with CNC Machinists, Engineering and Quality, the Programmer develops practical machining approaches for new product development, first articles and ongoing production, incorporating shop-floor feedback into program revisions and improvements.


Key Responsibilities:

CNC Programming & Machining Strategy

  • Develop and maintain CNC programs for multi-axis milling and turning applications.
  • Develop machining strategies for complex, high-precision components based on engineering requirements, material characteristics, machine capabilities, and production requirements.
  • Create and maintain machining setup sheets, tool lists, and other required program documentation.
  • Define appropriate tooling, machining sequences, and cutting parameters to support safe and effective machining.
  • Review and revise CNC programs based on production feedback, engineering changes, quality findings, and process improvement opportunities.

Workholding & Fixture Development

  • Collaborate with Engineering and CNC Machinists to develop effective workholding strategies for complex component geometries.
  • Design machining fixtures and workholding solutions to support machining and dimensional requirements.
  • Evaluate workholding and fixture requirements and recommend improvements to address manufacturing risks or inefficiencies.

Cross-Functional Manufacturing Support

  • Collaborate with CNC Machinists, Engineering, Quality, and Production to support machining strategies and address manufacturing challenges.
  • Review engineering drawings, models, specifications, and customer requirements to ensure programming strategies support manufacturing and quality requirements.
  • Support root cause and corrective action activities related to CNC programming and machining processes.
  • Support new product introduction and ongoing production requirements for new or technically challenging components.

Quality & Continuous Improvement

  • Ensure CNC programs and related documentation are maintained in accordance with AS9100 requirements and company procedures.
  • Maintain controlled CNC programs and documentation to support traceability and effective revision control.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives related to CNC programming and machining processes.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support departmental and organizational objectives.

  • Manage activities and other promotional events to engage bilateral and multilateral institutions/ donors, private sector and civil society to expand and/or sustain interest and resources for UN Women programmes and joint UN system programmes;

  • Provide network and capacity development to partner Civil Society Organizations and other stakeholders.

4. Facilitate knowledge building and sharing

  • Manage capacity building exercises.

title: Cardiac Diagnostic Technician
description:
Job Summary: The Cardiac Diagnostic Technician is responsible for providing basic and advanced electrophysiology services to pediatric, adolescent, adult and geriatric patients. The position also requires extensive scanning, analysis and report generation for Holter monitors received from the CarolinaEast Heart Centers and CIM physician offices. The Technician is also responsible for the day-to-day performance of the departmental duties to include; computerized document and data management systems, and documentation for billing purposes. The individual is required to deliver services to patients in all areas of the hospital and those services are to be performed day/evening/nights and weekends as required to provide continuous, consistent diagnostic testing. On-Call responsibilities are an important part of job requirements. The Cardiac Diagnostic Technician is to perform the duties and responsibilities outlined with minimal supervision and must be capable of making many independent decisions.

At the heart of our system is a 350-bed, full-service medical center equipped with a comprehensive range of inpatient and outpatient services, utilizing the latest medical technologies. CarolinaEast offers a robust benefits package to all full-time employees, as well as benefits for part-time plus and part-time staff. We are proud to be the first medical center in North Carolina recognized as a Cardiovascular Center of Excellence by the American College of Cardiology and the American Heart Association. Additionally, we are honored to be named one of America’s Best-In-State Hospitals by Newsweek, among numerous other prestigious accolades.

Minimum Requirements:

  • High School graduate.
  • Typing skills (40+ WPM), grammar/spelling abilities, and medical terminology required.
  • Previous experience and/or formal Cardiac Diagnostic training required.
  • Cardiographic Technician certification preferred.
  • Candidates must obtain CCT credential within one year of employment.
  • BCLS required.
  • Must be able to demonstrate the knowledge and skills necessary to provide care appropriate to the age of the patients served.

  • Deliver outstanding customer service that upholds CarolinaEast's Standards of Excellence.

title: Commercial Credit Analyst - Senior
description:
Evergreen Federal Bank is seeking talented individuals who believe in offering exceptional customer service and enjoy making a positive difference in the community where they live. Celebrating over 90 years of operation, our institution has provided many stable careers. We offer competitive pay and a community-centric culture. We are currently accepting applications for Senior Commercial Credit Analyst at our Grants Pass headquarters location.


Job Summary and Responsibilities

The Senior Commercial Credit Analyst position is responsible for managing all aspects of the credit administration department. This includes responsibility for supervising credit administration personnel, evaluating the financial viability and accurate underwriting of new loan applicants, as well as ensuring the appropriate financial credit review for designated on-going loan relationships. Essential duties include the following:

  • Supervise, develop and train competent credit analysts.
  • Review credit administration department work to ensure accuracy and quality.
  • Develop, update and implement credit administration best practices.
  • Maintain a working understanding of the different types of loans, loan structures and credit options/terms that are available within lending parameters of institution policy.
  • Accurately and efficiently analyze highly complex business and personal credit data and financial information including, but not limited to tax returns, profit and loss statements, balance sheets and statements of cash flow to determine the degree of risk involved in extending credit or lending money.
  • Generate financial ratios to evaluate financial status, using computer programs including but not limited to Buker’s Tax Analysis and Microsoft Excel.
  • Compile and underwrite relevant data for loan requests including those with highly complex borrowing structures and/or highly complex financial profiles; assist in the evaluation of loan request quality and compliance with commercial lending parameters pursuant to the institution policy.
  • Draft loan proposals and summaries of loan requests which effectively and efficiently convey information about borrowers, collateral, potential strengths/weaknesses and risks and any other pertinent information necessary for review and approval determination by loan committees.
  • Determine items needed from borrowers/applicants.
  • Accurately update and organize both hardcopy and digital loan files.
  • Effectively utilize quality control checklists to ensure regulatory and institution policy compliance.
  • Communicate with customers, internal bank staff and external informational sources in-person, by phone, by email and in written form as needed.
  • Schedule and occasionally perform collateral inspections for potential real estate loans as well as on-going construction loans and direct disbursement of funds as needed.
  • Review and analyze preliminary title reports for any issues affecting value of collateral.
  • Review and analyze appraisal reports for any issues affecting value of collateral.
  • Maintain records and prepare reports as required regarding loan originating activities.
  • Requires compliance with internal policies and procedures, as well as applicable laws and regulations, including the Bank Secrecy Act.

Additional responsibilities of this position are as follows:

  • Performing Administrative Activities – Performing day-to-day administrative tasks such as maintaining information files and processing paperwork.
  • Learn and temporarily perform job duties for other positions in the organization as needed.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Eligibility

The successful individual in this position will possess the following core skills/competencies:

  • Integrity and Trustworthiness
  • Dependability
  • Adaptability/Flexibility
  • Attention to detail
  • Analytic thinking
  • Problem solving, judgment and decision making
  • Well-developed understanding of personal and business accounting
  • Effectively apply highly complex financial analysis and lending concepts
  • Ability to effectively teach others complex financial analysis and concepts
  • High degree of competency with various computer systems and software programs, including MS Office
  • Effective communication with people both inside and outside the organization in person, in writing, by telephone and by email
  • Develop and maintain positive, constructive and cooperative working relationships with people both inside and outside the organization
  • Ability to resolve conflict and negotiate with people both inside and outside the organization
  • Ability to deal calmly and effectively with high-stress situations
  • Organizing, planning and prioritizing work
  • Initiative and work independently
  • Interpersonal skills
  • Willing and able to work overtime as needed during times of higher loan demand

Education/Experience/Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher preferred.
  • Minimum seven years banking/finance or other relevant experience.
  • Requires valid Oregon driver’s license and insurance.

Benefits

Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, life, and long term disability coverage; paid vacation, sick time, holidays, volunteer time off (VTO); and tuition reimbursement to support your continued growth.


Physical Demands

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position for prolonged periods.
  • Moving about the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, etc.
  • Be able to lift/carry up to 30 lbs.
  • Operate a computer and other office machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, printer, scanner, and other standard office equipment.
  • The work primarily performed in this position is done within an indoor, climate-controlled environment. Occasional work in outdoor weather conditions.

Candidates must be able to complete all essential functions and physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation.

While this is intended to be an accurate reflection of the current job, management reserves the right to revise the job or to require that other or different tasks be performed as assigned.

title: Sr Software Engineer-Automation
description:
Our team is building is building a modern hybrid cloud platform from the ground up to support the next generation of applications across our organization. The platform provides the foundational infrastructure, container runtime environments, developer tooling, messaging systems, and observability capabilities required to run reliable and scalable applications.

This is a greenfield engineering opportunity. The team is designing and implementing the core platform architecture that will operate across our data centers and cloud environments. Engineers on this team help define how infrastructure is provisioned, how Kubernetes platforms are operated, and how automation enables consistent and scalable operations.

Our approach emphasizes software-driven infrastructure, infrastructure-as-code, Git-based workflows, and modern observability practices. Engineers on the platform team build production-grade systems that reduce operational complexity and enable teams to operate systems through automated and self-service capabilities.

Work Location: Onsite at one of the listed locations; remote candidates may be considered.

﻿This role improves how work gets done across the organization by designing and delivering software and automation that reduce manual effort, improve efficiency, and support reliable operations at scale.

This role focuses on developing tools, workflows, and services that support both developer and operational workflows, including infrastructure provisioning, deployment pipelines, environment management, and day-to-day operational tasks. You will work across systems and teams to streamline how applications are built, deployed, and operated.

In addition to building automation, you will identify manual, repetitive, or inefficient processes and determine whether they should be automated, simplified, or eliminated entirely. You will use code, APIs, and system integrations to replace manual work with scalable, repeatable solutions.

Success in this role requires strong technical skills, curiosity, and a mindset focused on improving systems. Engineers in this role continuously identify high‑impact opportunities to simplify workflows, reduce operational toil, and help teams work more efficiently.

We are hiring at multiple levels and value strong foundational programming skills and curiosity over prior domain‑specific experience.

Platform Automation Engineering

  • Identify manual operational processes across infrastructure, platform, and operations teams that can be automated
  • Design and build automation systems that reduce operational toil and improve reliability
  • Develop tools and services that enable teams to provision and manage infrastructure through automated workflows
  • Build automation that supports consistent operations across hybrid infrastructure environments

Automation Development & Tooling

  • Develop automation systems using modern programming languages (Go, Python, Java)
  • Integrate automation with infrastructure APIs, platform services, and operational tooling
  • Build internal tools that improve operational workflows and reduce manual intervention

Infrastructure & Platform Integration

  • Automate infrastructure provisioning and lifecycle management using infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform
  • Integrate automation with Kubernetes platforms, CI/CD systems, and Git-based workflows

Toil Reduction & Process Simplification

  • Identify manual, repetitive, and low-value work across engineering and operations
  • Analyze workflows and determine whether they should be automated, simplified, or eliminated
  • Replace manual processes with software, APIs, or automated workflows
  • Drive measurable reductions in operational toil and process complexity

Operational Automation

  • Develop automated workflows for common operational tasks such as provisioning, configuration management, and environment setup
  • Implement automation that improves incident response and operational reliability
  • Identify opportunities to eliminate repetitive tasks and improve system operations

Observability & Reliability

  • Integrate automation with monitoring and observability systems such as Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry
  • Use telemetry and operational data to identify opportunities for automation and reliability improvements

﻿Bachelor's degree in management information systems (MIS), computer science, or related technical field; or equivalent work experience. (Typically four years of related, progressive work experience would be needed for candidates applying for this position who do not possess a bachelor's degree.)

A minimum of six years of experience in automation engineering, infrastructure engineering, platform engineering, or software engineering is required.

  • Automation engineering, infrastructure engineering, platform engineering, or software engineering
  • Strong programming skills in at least one language used for automation development (Go, Python, or Java)
  • Experience working with Linux systems and distributed environments

Core Technical Experience

Experience in several of the following areas:

  • Infrastructure automation and operational tooling
  • Infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform
  • CI/CD pipelines and Git-based workflows
  • Automation of infrastructure or operational processes
  • Cloud platforms or hybrid infrastructure environments
  • Observability systems including Prometheus, Grafana, or OpenTelemetry

  • API-driven automation and system integrations

    Preferred Qualifications:

    Experience implementing GitOps workflows

    Experience building internal developer or operational tooling

    Experience automating incident response or operational workflows

title: SolidWorks PDM Administrator
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

Forgent’s mechanical engineers use SolidWorks and SolidWorks PDM Professional to model the structures, enclosures, and large E-House and switchgear assemblies that go to the floor. As practices are harmonized across the company and CAD data connects to ERP and PLM, these systems need a dedicated daily owner. This role exists to be that owner.

The Associate administers the mechanical design environment for the MV, LV, and E-House/Skid product lines, working with Engineering, Manufacturing, Applications Engineering, and IT. The role is paired with the AutoCAD-Vault Administration Associate; both report to the Engineering Systems Supervisor, who owns standards, architecture, and final decisions. This is an engineering systems administration role, not an IT help-desk or production CAD design seat.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Administer SolidWorks and SolidWorks PDM Professional across all sites: permissions, groups, workflow and lifecycle states, revision controls, and archives.
  • Maintain PDM folder structures, naming, metadata, file relationships, CAD standards, templates, title blocks, and libraries within approved standards.
  • Support change, release, revision, and archival workflows, including the redline/issue-tracking process that communicates changes to the floor.
  • Install, license, and version-control SolidWorks; coordinate updates, testing, and deployments with IT and the Supervisor.
  • Troubleshoot software, licensing, performance, workflow, and access issues; work with IT on workstation performance and crash mitigation.
  • Provide Tier 1 support and act as day-to-day contact for the SolidWorks reseller on PDM issues.
  • Check that engineers follow approved PDM workflows, modeling, and filing practices; report deviations and recurring issues to the Supervisor.
  • Onboard new engineers on CAD/PDM standards; maintain user guides, work instructions, and training materials.
  • Develop templates, tools, and scripts that improve efficiency; recommend automation and process improvements and escalate major decisions to the Supervisor.

TRACK-SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Maintain SolidWorks libraries, templates, and configurations, plus structural entries in the Master Component Library (metadata, part numbers, BOM data).
  • Implement large assembly best practices for complex E-House and switchgear models to improve stability and performance.
  • Apply the approved fastener representation approach (simplified representations, hardware BOMs).
  • Support automated hardware creation and spooling workflows in SolidWorks as they mature.
  • Validate that SolidWorks BOMs and metadata flow accurately through PDM to NetSuite and future PLM (Autodesk Fusion Manage).
  • Support cross-plant transfers of mechanical design data and approved PLM/ERP integrations, including data mapping and migration.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3+ years administering SolidWorks PDM Professional or comparable PDM (permissions, workflows, revisions, metadata, document control).
  • Strong working knowledge of SolidWorks and SolidWorks PDM Professional.
  • Understanding of CAD assemblies, drawings, BOMs, part numbering, and release processes.
  • Experience supporting engineering or manufacturing environments.
  • Strong troubleshooting, documentation, and training skills, with the process discipline to apply established standards.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • CSWA or CSWP certification.
  • SolidWorks PDM Administration training course certificate.
  • Experience with CAD/PDM upgrades, migrations, or implementations, and with large assembly performance.
  • Familiarity with ERP/PLM integration (NetSuite, Autodesk Fusion Manage).
  • Switchgear, switchboard, or structural manufacturing experience; multi-site support experience.
  • WORKING CONDITIONS
  • Primarily office/computer-based at an assigned Forgent engineering facility.
  • Occasional travel between Dayton and Champlin, MN, with periodic coordination with Hanover.
  • Periodic floor time to verify CAD-to-physical accuracy, especially during rollouts.

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Primarily office/computer-based at an assigned Forgent engineering facility.
  • Occasional travel between Dayton and Champlin, MN, with periodic coordination with Hanover.
  • Periodic floor time to verify CAD-to-physical accuracy, especially during rollouts.

JOB BENEFITS:

  • PTO/ESST
  • Paid holidays
  • $100 individual deductible and $300 family deductible health insurance
  • Paid weekly
  • Vision and Dental Insurance
  • 401K / Life Insurance / STD

title: RE2CLID Consultant (4 positions) -Caia, Marromeu, Nhamatanda or Mutarara District, Mozambique
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration


Project Context and Scope

Under the direct supervision of the MECR National Officer, technical guidance of the designated MECR Project Associates and coordination with the wider RE2CLID team, the District Coordinator will provide day-to-day field support, maintain regular engagement with district authorities and communities, monitor implementation and keep the RE2CLID District Dossier up to date.


Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing

Migration, Environment, Climate Change and Risk Reduction (MECR) / RE2CLID Programme
Tasks to be performed under this contract

District context and planning
• Maintain an up-to-date understanding of district institutions, plans, coordination mechanisms, projects, climate and disaster risks, displacement dynamics, livelihoods and natural-resource issues relevant to RE2CLID.
• Gather, review and compile information from Government institutions, partners, existing data and other relevant sources, and flag important gaps or developments.
• Maintain and regularly update the RE2CLID District Dossier and related mapping and planning tools.


Government, partner and community engagement
• Maintain regular contact with the District Administration Office, district technical services, partners and other relevant stakeholders.
• Participate in relevant district coordination mechanisms and support follow-up on agreed actions.
• Maintain an updated overview of actors, projects, Government priorities and plans, identifying complementarities, gaps and opportunities for collaboration.


Climate Ambassadors support
• Maintain regular communication with Climate Ambassadors assigned to RE2CLID target communities.
• Consolidate and summarize information and community feedback received from Climate Ambassadors.
• Flag operational or implementation issues to the Geographic Lead.


Implementation and monitoring
• Follow up on activities implemented directly by IOM and through Government counterparts, implementing partners, consultants, CTGs and other delivery actors.
• Monitor implementation progress through stakeholder engagement and field follow-up, reporting delays, challenges, risks and opportunities.
• Support district-level meetings, consultations, missions, assessments, training and other programme activities.
• Provide contextual information and practical support to RE2CLID staff, specialists and consultants working in the district.


Reporting and information management
• Maintain records of meetings, stakeholder engagements, field follow-up, project developments and agreed actions.
• Provide regular updates, concise field notes, meeting summaries and briefing inputs.
• Promptly escalate significant contextual, operational or stakeholder issues requiring action.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • University degree in development studies, environmental sciences, geography, disaster risk management, climate change, agriculture, natural-resource management, social sciences, public administration, community development or another relevant field, with at least two years of relevant professional experience; or
  • Secondary education with at least four years of relevant professional experience.

Experience

  • Work at district or community level in Mozambique, preferably in Sofala or Tete Province.
  • Engagement with district Government authorities, community leadership, civil society organizations, or development and humanitarian actors.
  • Work related to disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation, community resilience, livelihoods, natural-resource management, environmental management, displacement, community engagement or local development.
  • Field consultations, stakeholder mapping, community engagement, monitoring or contextual information gathering.
  • Previous experience with the United Nations, international organizations, NGOs or Government programmes is an advantage.

Skills

  • Ability to organize fieldwork, follow up with multiple stakeholders and maintain structured records.

  • Strong observation, listening, facilitation and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to collect, summarize and clearly communicate qualitative and quantitative information.

  • Good written and verbal communication skills.

  • Basic computer literacy, including email, Microsoft Word, Excel and shared electronic filing systems.

  • Ability and willingness to travel frequently within the assigned district, including rural and remote communities.

  • Ability to work with limited day-to-day supervision while maintaining close communication with a geographically dispersed team.

  • Experience driving a motorbike and possession of a valid motorbike driving licence are advantages.

Languages

• Fluency in Portuguese and English is required.
• Fluency in one or more local languages spoken in the assigned district is desirable.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Notes

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

As part of a strong network of Crisis Management professionals across E.ON’s German and European business units, you initiate and jointly drive Group-wide topics, foster collaboration and continuously strengthen E.ON’s crisis preparedness and response capabilities.

title: Freight Handler- Part Time- 1st Shift
description:
The Forklift Operator is responsible for the safe, accurate, and efficient loading, unloading, staging, scanning, and movement of freight. As certified forklift operators within the operation, they provide safe, accurate, and efficient loading, unloading, movement, and documentation of cargo/freight within a multimodal transportation terminal, intermodal yard, warehouse, or dock environment, directly contributing to productivity, workflow coordination, and freight integrity. As the most experienced team members without direct reports, they often assist with mentoring, guiding, and onboarding new Material Handlers and solving complex operational problems on the floor.

Compensation: $20.07 per hour

Schedule: Monday- Friday 5am-9am, onsite

Responsibilities

  • Load and unload freight using sit-down/stand-up forklifts and reach trucks, along with other appropriate Material Handling Equipment (MHE), such as pallet jacks, carts, and dollies, and approved physical lifting techniques.

  • Move, stage, sort, and position freight between dock doors, trailers, and designated warehouse areas in accordance with operating procedures.

  • Pick, pack, and prepare items for shipping and delivery.

  • Assist drivers with loading and unloading activities following dock and safety procedures.

  • Label, scan, and track freight using handheld scanning devices and company systems to ensure accuracy and documentation integrity.

  • Identify damaged freight and promptly report issues, unsafe conditions, or equipment concerns to supervisory personnel.

  • Abide by all company safety policies, OSHA requirements, and PPE standards.

  • Maintain a clean, safe, and organized dock environment, including work areas, tools, and MHE.

  • Perform tasks under appropriate supervision while learning equipment operation, safety protocols, and job procedures (for developing roles).

  • Support dock productivity, workflow efficiency, and overall operational goals.

  • Work assigned schedules, including nights, weekends, holidays, and overtime based on business needs.

  • Safely and accurately handle oversized, high‑value, or complex freight.

  • Assist with dock coordination, workflow management, and problem resolution.

  • Prioritize freight and coordinate task assignments, sometimes acting in a lead capacity (without direct supervisory responsibility).

  • Serve as a subject‑matter expert on dock operations, equipment, and procedures.

  • Train, mentor, and support the development of other Material Handlers.

  • All other duties as assigned to meet evolving business needs.

Qualifications

  • Education: High School Diploma or General Education Development (GED)/equivalent preferred but not required.

  • Certification/Licensure: Valid forklift certification/licensure (or ability to obtain before operating equipment) required.

  • Experience: 3+ years of dock or warehouse experience required.

  • Communication: Ability to communicate effectively in English, verbally and in writing, to understand safety and operational instructions, work assignments, and freight documentation.

  • Ability to recognize numbers, labels, barcodes, and freight markings accurately, and to perform basic arithmetic to verify freight counts, quantities, and weights.

  • Basic arithmetic skills to verify freight counts, quantities, and weights.

  • Technology: Willingness and ability to learn and use basic computer systems, handheld scanners, and freight-tracking devices.

  • Equipment: Ability to safely operate material handling equipment (MHE) such as pallet jacks, dollies, hand trucks, order pickers, pallet riders, conveyors, dock plates, dock levelers, sit-down/stand-up forklifts and reach trucks (with company-assisted certification/training), and/or other specialized MHE as required by the site.

  • Ability to maintain regular and predictable attendance.

  • Physical Demands: Extensive standing, walking, bending, stooping, kneeling, crouching, reaching, and twisting for 8-12 hours per/shift, with the ability to lift, push, pull, and carry freight up to 50lbs without assistance, with occasional lifting of freight up to 75lbs with assistance or mechanical aids throughout each 8-12 hour shift, multiple times per/week.

  • Vision, hearing, and verbal communication skills sufficient to work safely in a noisy dock environment.

  • Environment: Ability to work safely around moving equipment, vehicles, and freight in a non-climate-controlled environment, including frequent exposure to temperature extremes (both hot and cold), occasional outdoor work and/or exposure to precipitation (rain, sleet, snow, etc.), regular exposure to moving equipment, vehicle traffic, exhaust, dust, and moderate to loud noise.

title: B2 Associate Delivery Manager on Temporary Promotion/Temporary Level Transfer in Social Security Scotland
description:
Social Security Scotland are seeking an Associate Delivery Manager to sit within the End-to-End Delivery Team.

The End-to-End Delivery Space is a relatively new area within Digital, Delivery and Change. The unit aims to foster a digitally enabled and client centric ecosystem that drives innovation, enhances collaboration, delivers sustainable business value and a seamless, compliant and client-focused service by operationalising policy and legislation effectively, ensuring successful implementation through strong partnerships with Corporate, Scottish Government Policy and other delivery partners.

The End-to-End Client journey ensures the prioritisation, coordination and execution of complex digital products and services across Change and Digital Delivery for client journey service areas (verticals) and benefit service (horizontals). It aligns service roadmaps, manages dependencies, balancing costs with delivery efficiencies and business value.

The Associate Delivery Manager will support the successful delivery of products and business change initiatives by coordinating activities, managing stakeholders and helping to ensure delivery objectives are achieved. They will work closely with delivery teams across End-to-End, the Associate Delivery Manager is a key and integral part of this team as we look to move forward on this journey.

As an Associate Delivery Manager, you will support business-as-usual activities across the end-to-end client journey. You will work alongside Delivery Managers and Senior Delivery Managers to lead and work with multi-disciplinary teams who are delivering complex digital and business change portfolio initiatives. You’ll drive towards progress at pace and to agreed timescales; managing competing priorities, removing blockers and planning at a higher level to ensure key deliverables are met on time.

Responsibilities

  • Apply Agile principles to support delivery effectively.
  • Establish transparent frameworks for teams to work within.
  • Utilise Agile tools intelligently to enhance team productivity.
  • Visualise and communicate team progress and tasks.
  • Serve as the primary contact for contracted suppliers.
  • Navigate internal government department contacts and processes proficiently.
  • Decide optimal involvement of third parties in digital projects.
  • Bridge communication gaps between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Facilitate discussions within multidisciplinary teams.
  • Advocate for the team externally while managing diverse perspectives.
  • Understand and be aware of the financial implications of delivery work.
  • Contribute to the creation and management of budgets.
  • Recognise and accommodate the evolving needs of teams and products throughout the delivery life cycle.
  • Proactively address internal risks and issues.
  • Establish and support sustainable team cadence.
  • Manage, track, and communicate project dependencies effectively.
  • Influence team members to optimise processes.
  • Anticipate and address changing constraints to ensure process effectiveness.
  • Appreciate and embed the importance of planning and forecasting within your team.
  • Demonstrate awareness of various planning methodologies.
  • Foster a collaborative environment within the team.
  • Empower delivery teams and encourage effective teamwork.
  • Value and incorporate feedback to enhance team performance.

Success Profiles
We use an assessment framework called ‘Success Profiles’ which lists the elements we test and provides detailed descriptions of each. Find out more about the framework here.

For this opportunity, the following Success Profile elements will be assessed:

Experience

  1. Experience communicating with a range of stakeholders, including both technical and non-technical colleagues, building positive working relationships and supporting discussions across multidisciplinary teams with differing perspectives.
  2. Experience supporting the delivery of work at pace by helping to identify, manage and communicate risks, issues and dependencies, and understanding how these can affect delivery outcomes and team priorities.
  3. Experience contributing to the planning and coordination of team activities, helping to maintain delivery momentum through effective organisation, prioritisation and management of competing demands.
  4. Experience influencing and working collaboratively with others to improve ways of working, challenge barriers to delivery where appropriate, and support continuous improvement within a team environment.

How to apply
Please apply online, providing a Supporting Statement (of no more than 500 words) providing evidence of how you demonstrate the Success Profiles noted above.

Please note that a CV is not required for this opportunity.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can be used to support your application, but all statements and examples provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, and presented as your own) applications will be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action.

Please see our candidate guidance for more information on acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI in recruitment.

If you are interested in this opportunity, you should seek permission from your manager and C-band manager before applying on a level transfer (TLT) basis. If applying on Temporary Promotion you should inform your manager and C-band manager from the outset of your intention to apply. If successful in your application, your release must be agreed by your line manager and C-band manager or relevant unit head.

Please note that the post is only open to individuals who have satisfactorily completed their probationary period.

This is a Government Digital and Data (GDD) role within the Product and Delivery job family. Candidates who are not currently members of the GDD Profession, or who belong to a different GDD job family, will be required to complete a GDD technical assessment before an appointment can be confirmed.

If you are successful following the informal discussion and a technical assessment is required, further details will be provided in advance to allow you sufficient time to prepare

Dates to Remember
Statement submitted by: 5pm on Tuesday 27th October 2026
Informal chats: week commencing 9th November (This may be subject to change)

Duration of Temporary Opportunity
This opportunity is for 12 months.

Hybrid Working
Our standard hours are 35 hours per week, and we offer a range of flexible working options, depending on the needs of the role. We embrace a hybrid working style where all colleagues will spend time in either our Glasgow or Dundee offices. There is an expectation of a minimum 2 days per week in your assigned location.

Further Information
This role is only available to those currently employed (on a permanent basis) by Social Security Scotland, Scottish Government Main or Common Citizenship organisations. Please note that applicants from Common Citizenship organisations may apply only on a promotion basis and not via a level transfer.

Social Security Scotland are a Disability Confident Employer. We will consider and implement any reasonable adjustments you may require throughout the recruitment process and during the course of your employment, should you be successful in securing a post. If you feel you may require assistance with any part of our recruitment process, please contact us at recruitment@socialsecurity.gov.scot

If you experience any difficulties accessing our website or completing the online application form, please contact the Resourcing Team via recruitment@socialsecurity.gov.scot

If you have any questions about the role please contact Danielle McKenzie at Danielle.McKenzie@socialsecurity.gov.scot
